config_fields.name: container
config_fields.description: Blob container / ADLS Gen2 filesystem name. Required.

config_fields.name: account
config_fields.description:
Storage-account name. Optional when a connection string or the
emulator supplies it, otherwise required.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description:
Credential source. Defaults to the environment / managed-identity
credential chain.

config_fields.name: endpoint
config_fields.description: Custom blob endpoint (e.g. an Azurite emulator or a sovereign cloud).

config_fields.name: allow_http
config_fields.description: Permit plaintext HTTP (required for a local Azurite emulator).

config_fields.name: use_emulator
config_fields.description:
Target the Azurite storage emulator with its well-known
`devstoreaccount1` credentials.

config_fields.name: prefix
config_fields.description: Object-name prefix for written objects.

config_fields.name: path
config_fields.description:
Object key template inside the container, after `prefix` — the file
sink's `path` (#777). May contain `{part}` (numbered objects) and
`${now.*}` tokens; a trailing `/` is a directory of
`part-{part}<extension>` objects. When set, `file_extension` is not
used. Unset: every run writes new objects named
`<prefix><run id>-<part><file_extension>` (`<run id>` is a fresh
time-ordered UUID, `<part>` is `00001`, `00002`, …).

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: if_exists
config_fields.description:
What to do when a blob of the same name already exists
(`if_exists`): `replace` it (default), `append` to it (JSON Lines, CSV,
raw text) or fail with `error` (#777). Needs `path`. `mode` is
accepted as another name for this key, and `overwrite` /
`error_if_exists` for its values.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: write_mode
config_fields.description:
`append` (default) or `overwrite`: write the run's blobs into a
hidden swap area and move them into place only after a successful
run, then remove blobs of an earlier run that match `path` and
were not rewritten (#777). The move is one blob at a time, so a
reader listing the destination while it runs can see new blobs beside
old ones; a move that was interrupted is finished by the next run.
Needs `path`.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: format
config_fields.description: Object format (default `json_lines`) (#604).

config_fields.name: file_extension
config_fields.description: File extension for written objects (default `.jsonl`).

config_fields.name: max_records_per_file
config_fields.description:
Hard cap on records per uploaded object. `None` means a single object
per `write_batch` call (still subject to `batch_size`).

config_fields.name: max_bytes_per_file
config_fields.description:
Maximum **bytes** per object before rolling to a new one (#618).

Rows are a poor proxy for object size, so a rows-only cap either writes
tiny objects for narrow data or unbounded ones for wide data. Counted
on the records' JSON length before any `compression` codec (on the
columnar Parquet path, their in-memory Arrow size). `None` (the
default) removes the byte cap; a single record larger than the cap
still gets its own object rather than being split or dropped.

config_fields.name: concurrency
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of uploads in flight (default 10): a page that rolls
into several objects uploads them concurrently while the next object
is encoded, and a large blob's blocks go up this many at a time.
`flush` returns only after every upload has landed.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per object when `max_records_per_file` is not set (without
`path`). Records accumulate across `write_batch` calls and an object
closes once it holds this many records, or at `flush`. `batch_size =
0` is the "no re-chunking" sentinel: no record cap, so JSON Lines and
the whole-object formats write one object per `flush`, and Parquet one
object per `write_batch` call. Ignored when `path` is set.

config_fields.name: compression
config_fields.description:
Compression codec applied to each uploaded object body. Defaults to
[`CompressionConfig::Auto`](faucet_core::CompressionConfig::Auto) —
resolves against `file_extension` (so `.jsonl.gz` triggers gzip).
Requires the crate-local `compression` feature. Note: this sink does
**not** set any `Content-Encoding` metadata, so consumers must
decompress explicitly.

config_fields.name: csv
config_fields.description: CSV dialect, used when `format: csv` (#604).

config_fields.name: excel
config_fields.description: Worksheet name, used when `format: xlsx` (#604).

config_fields.name: xml
config_fields.description: Record framing, used when `format: xml` (#604).

config_fields.name: avro
config_fields.description: Writer schema and block codec, used when `format: avro` (#719).

config_fields.name: parquet
config_fields.description:
Parquet writer options, used when `format: parquet` (#777):
`compression` (default `zstd`), `row_group_size`, explicit `schema`.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: json_lines
config_fields.description:
JSON Lines writer options (`pretty`), used when `format: json_lines`.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: encryption
config_fields.description:
Encrypt blobs at rest (#777; the `encryption` feature). Scratch
files are not encrypted while the run is in progress; those holding
plaintext are kept in a private directory.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: scratch_dir
config_fields.description:
Directory the sink builds each blob in before uploading it
(default: the system temporary directory). JSON Lines and raw text
go up in parts as they are written and need no scratch space; every
other format needs room for each blob being built (up to
`concurrency` of them while uploads are in flight). A private
subdirectory is created in it for each sink.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

AzureCredentials.description:
Credential source for an Azure storage client.

Serializes as `{ type: <method>, config: { … } }` (adjacent tagging,
snake_case discriminators) — the consistent auth wire shape shared by every
faucet connector, e.g.
`{ type: account_key, config: { account_key: "…" } }`.

oneOf.description: Shared storage-account access key (the primary/secondary key).
Shared-access-signature token (with or without a leading `?`).

Full storage connection string
(`DefaultEndpointsProtocol=…;AccountName=…;AccountKey=…;…`).

Azure Managed Identity (IMDS). For a user-assigned identity, set
`client_id`; leave it unset for the system-assigned identity.
Azure AD service principal (client credentials).

`DefaultAzureCredential`-style resolution: the object-store builder's
default chain (environment variables, workload identity, managed
identity, Azure CLI), honouring `AZURE_*` env vars. This is the default.

IfExists.description:
What happens when a file this run writes already exists (`if_exists`).

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

oneOf.description:
Replace that one file: the new file is built beside it and swapped in,
so the old contents stay readable until the new ones are complete.
`overwrite` is accepted as another name.

Add to it. JSON Lines, CSV and raw text only — a JSON array, XML,
Excel, Avro or Parquet file cannot be appended to without rewriting.
With rollover, numbering continues after the highest existing part.

Fail the run instead of touching an existing file.
`error_if_exists` is accepted as another name.

FileWriteMode.description:
Pipeline-level write mode (`write_mode`).

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

oneOf.description: Write this run's files; leave everything else in place.

Replace the destination's whole output set. The run writes into a
hidden swap area beside the destination; only when it succeeds are the
files moved into place, and then files of an earlier run that match
the path template and were not rewritten are removed. A failed or
cancelled run leaves the previous output untouched. The move is not
atomic across files: a reader listing the destination while it runs
can see some new files beside some old ones. A move that was
interrupted is finished by the next run before it writes anything.

AzureSinkFormat.description:
On-the-wire format of objects written by the Azure Blob sink (#604).

Only [`JsonLines`](Self::JsonLines) can be built a record at a time; every
other format has a header, a wrapper, or a container index, so its records
are buffered and encoded together at the rollover.

oneOf.description: Newline-delimited JSON — one JSON record per line (the default).
A single JSON array per object.

Delimited text. Columns are the union of every record's keys; dialect
from `csv`. Requires `file-format-csv`.

XML, one element per record. Framing from `xml`. Requires
`file-format-xml`.

An Excel workbook. Sheet name from `excel`. Requires
`file-format-excel`.

An Apache Avro Object Container File, against `avro.schema` or a
schema inferred from the object's records; block codec from
`avro.codec`. Requires `file-format-avro` (#719). There is no ORC
variant: ORC is read-only.

Apache Parquet: each object is a complete, self-contained Parquet
file, written with the `parquet` options; enables the columnar fast
path. Requires the `arrow` feature (#777).

Unparsed text: each record's `content` field (or the record as JSON)
on its own line (#777).

Take the format from the object name's extension — `path`'s, else
`file_extension` — looking through a compression suffix (#777).
Detect from filename suffix: `.gz` → Gzip, `.zst` → Zstd, anything else → None.

delimiter.description: Field separator. A single character; `"\t"` is accepted for tabs.

has_headers.description:
Whether the first row names the fields. When false, fields are named
`column_0`, `column_1`, … — the same fallback the REST source and the
`csv` connector already use. On write it decides whether a header row
is written.

quote.description: Quote character. A single byte; default `"`.

flexible.description:
Whether rows may have a different number of fields than the header.
`false` fails the read on the first ragged row, naming its line; `true`
keeps the fields the row has. Unset, each connector picks: the `file`
source is strict, the object-store sources and the REST source are
lenient.

null_values.description: Cell values read as `null` instead of a string (e.g. `["", "NULL"]`).

on_unknown_field.description:
What a streaming CSV writer does with a field the header does not
have. See [`CsvUnknownField`]. Whole-object encoders always write the
union of every record's fields, so it only affects the `file` sink.

CsvUnknownField.description: What a CSV writer does with a field that is not in the header.

oneOf.description: Add it as a new column; earlier rows get an empty cell for it.

Fix the header from the first page and drop the field, logging a
warning once per field.
Fix the header from the first page and fail the write naming the field.

sheet.description: Worksheet name, or an index as a string. Default: the first sheet.

XmlOptions.description:
XML record framing.

XML has no canonical record boundary, so one must be declared. On read,
`record_element` names the repeated element; without it the decoder falls
back to "the document's root children", which is right for the common
`<rows><row/>…</rows>` shape and wrong often enough that naming the element
is recommended in the docs.

record_element.description:
Element that delimits one record. Read: select these. Write: wrap each
record in one.

root_element.description: Document element wrapping the records. Write only.

schema.description:
An Avro schema (the JSON form: an object, an array for a union, or a
primitive name). On a **source** it is the *reader* schema every file
is resolved against — projection, aliases, defaults for added fields.
On a **sink** it is the *writer* schema; without it the schema is
inferred from the records.

codec.description:
Block codec for written files: `null` (default), `deflate`, `snappy`,
`zstd`. Reading detects the codec from the file header.

oneOf.description: Uncompressed blocks — the Avro default and the most portable.
Raw deflate (RFC 1951), readable by every Avro implementation.
Snappy with the per-block CRC-32 the spec requires.
Zstandard.

ParquetOptions.description:
Parquet write options.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

compression.description:
Column-chunk compression. Unset, it is `zstd` on the object-store and
SFTP sinks and `snappy` on the local file sink. A file-level
`compression` codec, when one applies, compresses the finished file
on top of this.

row_group_size.description:
Maximum rows per row group (default 1,048,576). Smaller groups let
readers skip more data and bound the writer's memory.

schema.description:
An explicit schema, in column order. Without it the schema is
inferred from the records and widened when a later page adds a field.
With it the file has exactly these columns: a record field the schema
does not name fails the write, and a value that does not fit its
column's type fails naming the column.

oneOf.description: Uncompressed pages.
Snappy: fast and universally readable.
Gzip.
Zstandard.
LZ4 (the `LZ4_RAW` codec).

ParquetField.description: One column of an explicit Parquet schema.

name.description: Column name — the record field it is read from.

nullable.description: Whether the column may be null or missing (default `true`).

ParquetType.description: A column type of an explicit Parquet schema.

oneOf.description: `true` / `false`.
32-bit signed integer.
64-bit signed integer.
64-bit unsigned integer.
32-bit float.
64-bit float.
UTF-8 text.
A calendar date, from `YYYY-MM-DD` text.
A UTC timestamp in milliseconds, from RFC 3339 text or epoch numbers.
A UTC timestamp in microseconds.
A UTC timestamp in nanoseconds.

A fixed-point decimal with the given precision and scale, from
numbers or numeric text.

JsonLinesOptions.description:
JSON Lines write options.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

pretty.description:
Pretty-print each record across several lines. The output is then a
stream of JSON documents rather than one record per line, which the
file source cannot read back.

EncryptionSpec.description:
The user-facing `encryption:` config block (state store / jsonl sink).

```yaml
encryption:
  key: ${vault:secret/faucet#state-key}
  # previous_keys: ["${env:OLD_STATE_KEY}"]   # rotation: read-only
  # algorithm: aes-256-gcm                     # default
```

key.description:
Key material used to seal new writes (and tried first on reads).
Should come from a secrets manager; derived to a 32-byte AES key via
SHA-256.

previous_keys.description:
Older keys tried (in order) when decrypting, for rotation. Never used
to seal new writes.

EncryptionAlgorithm.description:
Supported AEAD algorithms. A single variant today; the format byte in the
on-disk header leaves room for more without breaking old files.

oneOf.description: AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption (the default and only option).

connectors.description: Google BigQuery streaming-insert sink

dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

config_fields.name: project_id
config_fields.description: GCP project ID.

config_fields.name: dataset_id
config_fields.description: BigQuery dataset ID.

config_fields.name: table_id
config_fields.description: BigQuery table ID.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description:
Authentication credentials. YAML/JSON key is `auth` for consistency with
every other connector's auth block.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Maximum rows per `tabledata.insertAll` request. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

When the upstream `StreamPage` carries more records than `batch_size`,
the sink slices the page into `batch_size`-row chunks and issues one
`insertAll` HTTP call per chunk. When `batch_size = 0`, the page is
sent as a single request — useful when the source already chunks to
BigQuery's preferred size (e.g. ~500 rows for streaming inserts).

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the entire upstream
page is forwarded in one `insertAll` call, subject to BigQuery's
natural per-request limits (~10MB body, ~500 rows recommended).
Larger pages may exceed those limits — keep the default unless the
upstream `StreamPage` size is already tuned for BigQuery.

config_fields.name: insert_id_field
config_fields.description:
Optional record field whose value is sent as the BigQuery streaming
`insertId` for each row. BigQuery uses `insertId` for best-effort
de-duplication over a short window, so a stable per-row key here makes
streaming inserts resilient to transport retries (which are otherwise
at-least-once and can produce duplicate rows) (#78/#31). When `None`
(the default) no `insertId` is sent. A row missing the field is
inserted without an `insertId` (no dedup for that row).

config_fields.name: write_mode
config_fields.description: Append (default), upsert, or delete.

config_fields.name: key
config_fields.description: Key columns. Required and non-empty for upsert/delete; ignored for append.

config_fields.name: delete_marker
config_fields.description:
Optional. Upsert only: rows whose `field` matches one of `values` are
deletes; all others are upserts. The marker field is stripped from
upsert rows before writing.

config_fields.name: rollback
config_fields.description:
Runtime rollback settings (#706): the run id to journal under, the
run-id column, and whether to journal before-images / keep a replaced
table. Injected per invocation by the CLI when a config has a
top-level `rollback:` block — not meant to be written by hand.

config_fields.name: scope
config_fields.description:
Scoped/windowed overwrite (#518): with `write_mode: overwrite`, replace
only the rows matching this scope (e.g. a partition/date window) instead
of the whole table — the out-of-scope rows are preserved.

config_fields.name: create_table
config_fields.description:
Create the target table (and its dataset) if it does not exist, inferring
the schema from the first written page. Enabled by default: a first-ever
sync cannot assume the destination table already exists. Set to `false` to
require the table to pre-exist and fail fast when it is missing (e.g. the
schema is managed externally and a missing table signals a typo).

config_fields.name: schema
config_fields.description:
**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this field may change shape in a
minor release; changes are called out in the changelog.

Explicit column schema, in the `infer_schema` JSON-Schema shape
(`{"type":"object","properties":{"col":{"type":"integer"}, …}}`). When
set it is used **verbatim** for the `media_load` load job (so BigQuery
types columns from this instead of `autodetect`) and for `create_table`.
This is the escape hatch for typed sources whose JSON is heterogeneous
enough that `autodetect` mis-types a column and then fails the whole load
on one non-conforming row (e.g. an OData feed — the OData `$metadata`
document is the authoritative source of these types). Absent ⇒ the prior
behaviour (autodetect on `media_load`, first-page inference on
`create_table`).

config_fields.name: location
config_fields.description:
Location (region or multi-region, e.g. `US`, `EU`, `us-central1`) used only
when `create_table` has to create the dataset. `None` uses the BigQuery
job's default location. Ignored once the dataset exists.

config_fields.name: media_load
config_fields.description:
Bucket-free bulk load for the **append** and **overwrite** write paths
(default **`true`**, #612).

The alternative — one `jobs.query`
`INSERT … SELECT FROM UNNEST(@payload)` per page — is job-latency bound,
not volume bound: a 59,358-row overwrite at the default `batch_size`
issued ~60 sequential query jobs and took **6m44s**, and a
million-row table would issue thousands. A load job fed by a resumable
`multipart/related` upload of newline-delimited JSON moves the whole run
in **one** job, so time scales with data rather than page count. No GCS
bucket is involved (unlike the Arrow `bulk_load` path).

It is the default because it is better on every axis this sink is
measured on: **fewer** BigQuery jobs (one per run against BigQuery's
1,500 load-jobs-per-table-per-day budget, versus one query job per
page), atomic on its own for overwrite (a failed `WRITE_TRUNCATE` load
leaves the prior data intact), and bounded memory — pages feed the
session and are dropped, so peak is O(chunk), not O(table) (#614).

Set `false` to take the per-page query path. `upsert` / `delete` /
`delivery: exactly_once` ignore this field entirely: their writes commit
with a watermark or a `MERGE` in one transaction, which a load job
cannot express. `insert_id_field` likewise wins over this default —
only `insertAll` implements BigQuery's best-effort `insertId` dedup, so
asking for it keeps appends on the streaming path.

config_schema.title: BigQuerySinkConfig
config_schema.description: Configuration for the BigQuery streaming insert sink.

auth.description:
Authentication credentials. YAML/JSON key is `auth` for consistency with
every other connector's auth block.

batch_size.description:
Maximum rows per `tabledata.insertAll` request. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

When the upstream `StreamPage` carries more records than `batch_size`,
the sink slices the page into `batch_size`-row chunks and issues one
`insertAll` HTTP call per chunk. When `batch_size = 0`, the page is
sent as a single request — useful when the source already chunks to
BigQuery's preferred size (e.g. ~500 rows for streaming inserts).

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the entire upstream
page is forwarded in one `insertAll` call, subject to BigQuery's
natural per-request limits (~10MB body, ~500 rows recommended).
Larger pages may exceed those limits — keep the default unless the
upstream `StreamPage` size is already tuned for BigQuery.

insert_id_field.description:
Optional record field whose value is sent as the BigQuery streaming

streaming inserts resilient to transport retries (which are otherwise
at-least-once and can produce duplicate rows) (#78/#31). When `None`
(the default) no `insertId` is sent. A row missing the field is
inserted without an `insertId` (no dedup for that row).

key.description: Key columns. Required and non-empty for upsert/delete; ignored for append.

delete_marker.description:
Optional. Upsert only: rows whose `field` matches one of `values` are
deletes; all others are upserts. The marker field is stripped from
upsert rows before writing.

rollback.description:
Runtime rollback settings (#706): the run id to journal under, the
run-id column, and whether to journal before-images / keep a replaced
table. Injected per invocation by the CLI when a config has a
top-level `rollback:` block — not meant to be written by hand.

scope.description:
Scoped/windowed overwrite (#518): with `write_mode: overwrite`, replace
only the rows matching this scope (e.g. a partition/date window) instead
of the whole table — the out-of-scope rows are preserved.

create_table.description:
Create the target table (and its dataset) if it does not exist, inferring
the schema from the first written page. Enabled by default: a first-ever
sync cannot assume the destination table already exists. Set to `false` to
require the table to pre-exist and fail fast when it is missing (e.g. the
schema is managed externally and a missing table signals a typo).

schema.description:

minor release; changes are called out in the changelog.

set it is used **verbatim** for the `media_load` load job (so BigQuery

behaviour (autodetect on `media_load`, first-page inference on

when `create_table` has to create the dataset. `None` uses the BigQuery
job's default location. Ignored once the dataset exists.

BigQueryCredentials.description:
How to authenticate with Google BigQuery.

Serializes as `{ type: <method>, config: { … } }` (adjacent tagging,
snake_case discriminators) — the consistent auth wire shape shared by
every faucet connector.

oneOf.description: Path to a service account JSON key file.

path.description: Filesystem path to the service-account JSON key.

oneOf.description: Inline service account JSON key content.

json.description: Service-account JSON key as an inline string.

oneOf.description: Use application default credentials (e.g. workload identity, `gcloud auth`).

WriteMode.description: Write semantics for a sink. Serialized snake_case. Default `Append`.

oneOf.description: Insert every record (today's behaviour).
Insert-or-update by `key`; optionally route delete-marked rows to deletes.
Delete by `key` for every record.

Replace the entire destination with this run's records (truncate-load /
full refresh). The old contents are swapped out atomically only after the
run completes successfully, so a mid-run failure leaves them intact. No
`key` is required — it is a whole-dataset operation, not a keyed one.

DeleteMarker.description:
Identifies a record as a delete (vs. an upsert) by a marker field's value.
e.g. `{ field: "__op", values: ["d", "delete"] }`.

field.description: Field name whose value flags a delete.

values.description: Values of `field` that mean "this row is a delete".

RollbackWriteSpec.description:
Runtime rollback settings the executor hands a sink through its
[`WriteSpec`](crate::write_mode::WriteSpec) (`rollback:` field). Not user
config: the top-level `rollback:` block decides these, and the CLI injects
them per invocation.

run_id.description: The run id this invocation writes under.

run_id_column.description:
The destination column carrying the run id (stamped by the metadata
decorator).

journal.description: Record before-images of every upserted / deleted key.

keep_previous.description: Keep the replaced table of an overwrite as `<table>__faucet_prev`.

OverwriteScope.description:
Scope for a **scoped/windowed overwrite** (#518): with `write_mode:
overwrite`, replace only the destination rows matching this scope instead of
truncating the whole table. The sink-side sibling of scoped cleanup (#478).

v1 supports a half-open date/number **window** on a single column.

oneOf.description: Replace rows where `column` is in the half-open range `[from, to)`.

column.description: The destination column to window on.

connectors.name: clickhouse
connectors.title: ClickHouse
connectors.description: ClickHouse sink (HTTP INSERT … FORMAT JSONEachRow; optional async inserts)

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

dimensions.name: Schema evolution
dimensions.note: evolves the destination schema on drift

config_fields.name: table
config_fields.description:
Target table. May be schema-qualified (`db.table`); each identifier
segment is quoted before use.

config_fields.name: url
config_fields.description:
Full base URL of the ClickHouse HTTP interface, e.g.
`"http://localhost:8123"`. Mutually exclusive with
[`host`](Self::host). A trailing slash is trimmed.

config_fields.name: host
config_fields.description:
Hostname of the ClickHouse server. Mutually exclusive with
[`url`](Self::url); combined with [`http_port`](Self::http_port) and
[`tls`](Self::tls) to build the base URL.

config_fields.name: http_port
config_fields.description:
HTTP-interface port used with [`host`](Self::host). Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_HTTP_PORT`] (`8123`).

config_fields.name: tls
config_fields.description:
Use `https://` instead of `http://` when building the base URL from
[`host`](Self::host). Ignored when [`url`](Self::url) is set. Defaults to
`false`.

config_fields.name: database
config_fields.description: Target database. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_DATABASE`] (`"default"`).

config_fields.name: user
config_fields.description: ClickHouse user. When set, sent as the `X-ClickHouse-User` header.

config_fields.name: password
config_fields.description: ClickHouse password. When set, sent as the `X-ClickHouse-Key` header.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per `INSERT` request. When the upstream `StreamPage` carries more
records than `batch_size`, the sink splits it into `batch_size`-row
chunks and issues one `INSERT … FORMAT JSONEachRow` per chunk. `0`
forwards the whole page as a single request. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

config_fields.name: create_table
config_fields.description:
Create the target table if it does not exist, inferring the columns
from the first written page (#580). Enabled by default: a first-ever
sync cannot assume the destination already exists. The table is created
with the `MergeTree` engine and `ORDER BY tuple()` — the neutral choice
when faucet has no key to sort by; define the table yourself and set
`create_table: false` when the sort key matters, which it does for any
table you intend to query at scale.

Every inferred column is `Nullable(…)`: a column present in page 1 is
not required forever, and ClickHouse rejects a null into a non-nullable
column, so inferring non-nullability would fail page 2.

config_fields.name: commit_rows
config_fields.description:
Commit-group size for the cross-page accumulator (#617).

Warehouse loads are dominated by per-operation overhead, and
`batch_size` can only ever *split* a page — it can never merge
undersized ones, so a small source page meant one expensive warehouse
operation per small page. Records now accumulate across `write_batch`
calls and commit once per threshold, plus once at `flush`.

`None` (the default) accumulates the **whole run** into one commit.
Set it to bound how much is buffered, or to commit progressively on a
long run. `0` means the same as `None`.

Only the append path accumulates: `delivery: exactly_once` and the DLQ
path commit per page, because a watermark must land with its own page
and a DLQ must report which rows of *this* page failed.

config_fields.name: commit_bytes
config_fields.description:
Estimated-bytes counterpart of [`commit_rows`](Self::commit_rows)
(#617). Rows are a poor proxy for how much work a warehouse commit is;
this bounds the buffered size. `None` (the default) removes the byte
threshold.

config_fields.name: async_insert
config_fields.description:
Enable ClickHouse [asynchronous inserts](https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/optimize/asynchronous-inserts)
(`async_insert=1`): the server buffers rows and flushes them in the
background, which greatly improves throughput for many small inserts.
Defaults to `false`.

config_fields.name: wait_for_async_insert
config_fields.description:
When [`async_insert`](Self::async_insert) is enabled, whether the server
waits for the buffered rows to be flushed before acknowledging the
request (`wait_for_async_insert=1`). Keeping this `true` (the default)
preserves faucet's at-least-once durability contract — the bookmark only
advances after ClickHouse has durably accepted the batch. Ignored when
`async_insert` is `false`.

config_fields.name: staging
config_fields.description:
Staged bulk load (#528): stage each page to S3/GCS and have the
ClickHouse server pull it with `s3()` / `gcs()` instead of an
`INSERT … FORMAT JSONEachRow` body. Absent ⇒ the ordinary insert path.
Requires the crate's `staging` feature at build time to execute.

ClickHouseStagingConfig.description: Staged-load configuration for the ClickHouse sink (#528).

location.description:
Object-store location to stage files under, e.g.
`s3://my-bucket/faucet-stage/`. Scheme selects the backend
(`s3://` / `gs://` / `az://`).

format.description: File format written to the stage. Default `parquet`.

compression.description: Outer compression for `csv`/`jsonl` (ignored for `parquet`). Default `none`.

cleanup.description: When staged objects are deleted. Default `always`.

copy_options.description:

oneOf.description:

it maps by column name (no positional column list needed).
Comma-separated values with a header row.

warehouse supports it. Written by the sink (needs Arrow), not by this
module's byte serializers.

StagingCompression.description: Outer compression for text staging formats.

oneOf.description: No compression (the default).
gzip (`.gz`).
zstd (`.zst`).

StagingCleanup.description: When staged objects are deleted after a load.

oneOf.description:

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

dimensions.name: Schema evolution
dimensions.note: evolves the destination schema on drift

config_fields.name: path
config_fields.description: Path to the output CSV file.

config_fields.name: delimiter
config_fields.description: Field delimiter byte. Defaults to `b','`.

config_fields.name: write_headers
config_fields.description: Whether to write a header row. Defaults to `true`.

config_fields.name: append
config_fields.description: Whether to append to an existing file. Defaults to `false` (truncates).

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per upstream [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). The CSV
sink writes rows to disk one at a time inside a `spawn_blocking` task
fronted by a buffered `csv::Writer`, so this field has **no
behavioural impact** at the sink — it is exposed purely for config
parity across every sink in the workspace. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` (the "no batching" sentinel) and any positive value
produce byte-for-byte identical output for this sink: each record is
serialised and written individually regardless of how upstream chunked
the page.

config_fields.name: on_unknown_field
config_fields.description:
What to do when a record contains a field that is not part of the
frozen column set (the CSV header is fixed from the first batch and
cannot be rewritten without rewriting the whole file). A field that
first appears in a *later* batch — or in a later record once the header
is already written — cannot be added to the header, so its value is
dropped from the output. Defaults to [`OnUnknownField::Warn`].

config_fields.name: compression
config_fields.description:
Compression codec for the output file. Defaults to
[`CompressionConfig::Auto`](faucet_core::CompressionConfig::Auto) —
`.gz` / `.zst` suffix selects gzip / zstd. Requires the crate-local
`compression` feature.

OnUnknownField.description:
Policy for a record key that is not in the sink's frozen column set.

The CSV header is fixed from the first non-empty batch and cannot be
rewritten in place. A field that first appears after the header is written
(in a later batch, or a later record of the first batch once the header is
determined) therefore cannot become a column, so its value would be lost.

oneOf.description:
Emit a one-shot `tracing::warn!` naming the dropped field(s) and keep
writing — the unknown field's value is dropped from the output. This is
the default: it preserves the historical streaming/append behaviour
while making the column-level loss visible instead of silent.

Abort the write with a [`FaucetError::Sink`](faucet_core::FaucetError::Sink)
the first time any record carries a field outside the frozen column set.
Opt into this when silent column-level data loss is unacceptable.
Detect from filename suffix: `.gz` → Gzip, `.zst` → Zstd, anything else → None.

    # append: false    # Whether to append to an existing file.
    # batch_size: 1000    # Records per upstream [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage).
    # on_unknown_field: null    # Policy for a record key that is not in the sink's frozen column set.
    # compression: null    # User-facing compression config.

config_schema.description:

Writes into a Delta table through a SQL warehouse's
[Statement Execution API](https://docs.databricks.com/api/workspace/statementexecution).
`write_mode` / `key` / `delete_marker` are flattened in from
[`WriteSpec`](faucet_core::WriteSpec).

auth.description:
Authentication (PAT / OAuth bearer), inline or via a shared `auth: { ref }`
(use an `oauth2` client-credentials provider for an M2M service principal).

catalog.description: Unity Catalog catalog. When unset, the warehouse's default catalog.

schema.description: Target schema.

create_table.description:
Create the table from the first page's inferred schema when it does not
exist. Default `true`.

copy_threshold_bytes.description:
`auto` stages a page whose estimated size is at least this many bytes.
Default 1 MiB.

batch_size.description:
Rows per `INSERT` / `MERGE` statement on the insert path (`0` = no row
limit — statements are then bounded only by `max_statement_bytes`).

max_statement_bytes.description:
Upper bound on one statement's SQL text on the insert path; a page is
split into several statements above it. Default 8 MiB (the API accepts
up to 16 MiB).

wait_timeout_secs.description: Server-side wait before a statement goes async (`0` or `5`–`50` s).

poll_interval_ms.description:
Poll cadence while a statement is queued or running (a serverless
warehouse may take a minute to start). Default 1000 ms.

statement_timeout_secs.description:
Client deadline for one statement; the statement is cancelled when it
is exceeded. `0` waits indefinitely. Default 3600 s.

max_retries.description:
Retries on `429` / `503` and on Delta concurrent-write conflicts of
idempotent statements. Default 5.

retry_backoff_ms.description: Base of the exponential retry backoff. Default 1000 ms.

key.description: Key columns. Required and non-empty for upsert/delete; ignored for append.

delete_marker.description:
Optional. Upsert only: rows whose `field` matches one of `values` are
deletes; all others are upserts. The marker field is stripped from
upsert rows before writing.

rollback.description:
Runtime rollback settings (#706): the run id to journal under, the
run-id column, and whether to journal before-images / keep a replaced
table. Injected per invocation by the CLI when a config has a
top-level `rollback:` block — not meant to be written by hand.

AuthSpec.description:
A connector's `auth:` field: **either** an inline auth definition `A`
(the `{ type, config }` shape), **or** a `{ ref: <name> }` reference to a
shared provider defined in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

`ref` is mutually exclusive with inline fields — supplying both is a
deserialization error.

anyOf.description: Inline auth, spelled out on the connector.
A reference to a shared provider in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

DatabricksAuth.description:
Authentication for the Databricks SQL Statement Execution API.

Both variants send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` — Databricks accepts a
Personal Access Token (PAT) or an OAuth machine-to-machine (M2M) access
token in the same header. Uses the project-wide adjacently-tagged
`{ type, config }` shape, e.g. `auth: { type: pat, config: { token: … } }`.
A shared `auth: { ref: <name> }` provider that yields a `Bearer`/`Token`
credential maps onto [`DatabricksAuth::Token`] — that is how an OAuth M2M
service principal is wired: an `oauth2` client-credentials provider against
`{workspace_url}/oidc/v1/token` with scope `all-apis`, which refreshes the
token before it expires.

oneOf.description: Databricks Personal Access Token.
A pre-obtained OAuth (M2M) bearer token.

AuthReference.description:
A `{ ref: <name> }` pointer to a named provider in the top-level `auth:`
catalog. The only permitted key is `ref`.

ref.description: Name of the provider in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

DatabricksLoadMethod.description: How a page is loaded into the table.

oneOf.description:
Stage the page when `staging` is configured and the page is at least
`copy_threshold_bytes`; otherwise a multi-row `INSERT` (the default).

Always a multi-row `INSERT … SELECT … FROM VALUES` through the
Statement Execution API. No staging location needed.

Always stage the page as Parquet, then `COPY INTO` (append) or read it
with `read_files` (upsert / delete / exactly-once). Requires `staging`.

DatabricksStagingConfig.description: Where staged Parquet files are written before the warehouse loads them.

location.description:
Staging root. Either a Unity Catalog volume path
(`/Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<volume>[/prefix]`, uploaded through the
Files API with the sink's own credentials) or a cloud location the
warehouse can read through an external location: `s3://bucket/prefix`,
`gs://bucket/prefix`, or
`abfss://container@account.dfs.core.windows.net/prefix`. Cloud locations
need the crate's `staging` feature and ambient cloud credentials for the
upload.

cleanup.description: When staged files are deleted after a load. Default `always`.

copy_options.description:
Extra `COPY_OPTIONS` entries appended verbatim to the append path's
`COPY INTO`, e.g. `'mergeSchema' = 'false'`. The operator owns their
correctness.

StagingCleanup.description: When staged objects are deleted after a load.

oneOf.description:
Delete staged objects whether the load succeeded or failed (the default —
keeps the stage tidy).
Delete only after a successful load; leave them on failure for inspection.
Never delete — the caller/operator manages the stage lifecycle.

WriteMode.description: Write semantics for a sink. Serialized snake_case. Default `Append`.

oneOf.description: Insert every record (today's behaviour).
Insert-or-update by `key`; optionally route delete-marked rows to deletes.
Delete by `key` for every record.

Replace the entire destination with this run's records (truncate-load /
full refresh). The old contents are swapped out atomically only after the
run completes successfully, so a mid-run failure leaves them intact. No
`key` is required — it is a whole-dataset operation, not a keyed one.

DeleteMarker.description:
Identifies a record as a delete (vs. an upsert) by a marker field's value.
e.g. `{ field: "__op", values: ["d", "delete"] }`.

field.description: Field name whose value flags a delete.

values.description: Values of `field` that mean "this row is a delete".

RollbackWriteSpec.description:
Runtime rollback settings the executor hands a sink through its
[`WriteSpec`](crate::write_mode::WriteSpec) (`rollback:` field). Not user
config: the top-level `rollback:` block decides these, and the CLI injects
them per invocation.

run_id.description: The run id this invocation writes under.

run_id_column.description:
The destination column carrying the run id (stamped by the metadata
decorator).

journal.description: Record before-images of every upserted / deleted key.

keep_previous.description: Keep the replaced table of an overwrite as `<table>__faucet_prev`.

config_fields.name: table_uri

Delta table location URI: `file:///abs/path`, `s3://bucket/key`,
`abfss://…`, `gs://bucket/key`. A bare local path is accepted and
treated as `file://`.

config_fields.name: credentials
config_fields.description: Object-store credentials. Defaults to the ambient provider chain.

config_fields.name: storage_options
config_fields.description:
Extra `storage_options` passed verbatim to delta-rs (e.g. a MinIO
endpoint override, or any object-store key the [`DeltaCredentials`]
enum does not model). Keys set here **win** over credential-derived
keys.

config_fields.name: create_table
config_fields.description:
Create the table (and its schema, from the inferred record shape) on the
first write when it does not already exist. When `false`, an absent
table fails the first write with a typed error.

Spelled `create_table` on the wire since #580, matching every other
table sink; the historical `create_if_not_missing` stays accepted as an
alias. Same default (`true`): a first-ever sync cannot assume the
destination exists.

config_fields.name: partition_by
config_fields.description:
Partition columns, applied only when the table is created. Ignored when
appending to an existing table (its stored partitioning is used).

config_fields.name: schema_sample_size
config_fields.description: Records sampled to infer the Arrow/Delta schema when creating the table.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Re-chunk size for [`Sink::write_batch`](faucet_core::Sink::write_batch).
Incoming pages larger than this are sliced into `batch_size`-row Arrow
batches before writing. `0` writes each page through as one batch.

config_fields.name: target_file_size
config_fields.description:
Optional target data-file size (bytes) hint for the writer's rollover.
Advisory — delta-rs rolls files at buffer boundaries near this size.

config_schema.title: DeltaSinkConfig
config_schema.description:
Configuration for the Delta Lake sink connector (append-only in v1).

The `table_uri` / `credentials` / `storage_options` keys are flattened in
from the shared [`DeltaConnection`]. On first write the sink opens the
table (creating it from the inferred schema when `create_if_not_missing`),
then appends one Delta commit per `flush()`.

table_uri.description:
Delta table location URI: `file:///abs/path`, `s3://bucket/key`,
`abfss://…`, `gs://bucket/key`. A bare local path is accepted and
treated as `file://`.

credentials.description: Object-store credentials. Defaults to the ambient provider chain.

storage_options.description:
Extra `storage_options` passed verbatim to delta-rs (e.g. a MinIO
endpoint override, or any object-store key the [`DeltaCredentials`]
enum does not model). Keys set here **win** over credential-derived
keys.

create_table.description:
Create the table (and its schema, from the inferred record shape) on the
first write when it does not already exist. When `false`, an absent
table fails the first write with a typed error.

Spelled `create_table` on the wire since #580, matching every other
table sink; the historical `create_if_not_missing` stays accepted as an
alias. Same default (`true`): a first-ever sync cannot assume the
destination exists.

partition_by.description:
Partition columns, applied only when the table is created. Ignored when
appending to an existing table (its stored partitioning is used).

schema_sample_size.description: Records sampled to infer the Arrow/Delta schema when creating the table.

batch_size.description:
Re-chunk size for [`Sink::write_batch`](faucet_core::Sink::write_batch).
Incoming pages larger than this are sliced into `batch_size`-row Arrow
batches before writing. `0` writes each page through as one batch.

target_file_size.description:
Optional target data-file size (bytes) hint for the writer's rollover.
Advisory — delta-rs rolls files at buffer boundaries near this size.

DeltaCredentials.description:
Object-store credentials for reading/writing a Delta table.

Uses the project-wide adjacently-tagged `{ type, config }` shape
(snake_case discriminators): e.g. `credentials: { type: aws, config: { … } }`.
The default is [`DeltaCredentials::Default`], which resolves credentials from
the ambient environment / instance metadata via the object-store default
provider chain — nothing is injected into `storage_options`.

oneOf.description:
Resolve credentials from the ambient environment / default provider
chain (AWS instance profile, `AZURE_*` env, GCP ADC, …). Injects no
keys of its own.
Static AWS credentials (or an S3-compatible endpoint such as MinIO).
Azure Blob / ADLS Gen2 credentials.
Google Cloud Storage credentials.

AwsCredentials.description:
Static AWS credentials and optional S3-compatible endpoint overrides.

Leaving a field unset lets the object-store default chain resolve it (so
`region` alone with an instance profile is valid). `endpoint_url` +
`allow_http: true` targets MinIO / LocalStack.

allow_http.description: `AWS_ALLOW_HTTP` — permit plaintext HTTP to the endpoint (MinIO in dev).

service_account_path.description: `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` — path to a service-account JSON key file.

config_fields.name: base_url
config_fields.description: Base URL of the Elasticsearch cluster (e.g. `"http://localhost:9200"`).

config_fields.name: index
config_fields.description: Target index name.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description:
Authentication: either inline (`{ type, config }`) or a `{ ref: <name> }`
pointer to a shared provider in the CLI's top-level `auth:` catalog.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Maximum documents per `_bulk` HTTP request. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

When the upstream `StreamPage` carries more records than `batch_size`,
the sink slices the page into `batch_size`-row chunks and issues one
`POST /_bulk` per chunk. When `batch_size = 0`, the page is sent as a
single bulk request — useful when the source already sizes pages for
Elasticsearch's per-request sweet spot.

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the entire upstream
page is forwarded in one `_bulk` call. Elasticsearch's documented
sweet spot for `_bulk` payloads is **5–15 MB** of NDJSON per request;
the right document count depends on average document size. A
reasonable starting range is **1000–5000 docs** for typical
log/event payloads (~1–5 KB per document); lower it for fat
documents (analytics aggregates, large nested objects), raise it
for tiny ones.

config_fields.name: id_field
config_fields.description:
Optional JSON field name to use as the document `_id`.

If `None`, Elasticsearch auto-generates a fresh ID for every indexed
document. Under faucet's at-least-once contract that means a **resumed or
retried run re-indexes already-written records as duplicates** (a page
can partially commit across `_bulk` chunks before failing, and the
bookmark only advances once the whole page is written). Set `id_field` to
a stable business key so re-sends become **idempotent overwrites** (the
recommended setting for resumable pipelines); alternatively, configure a
DLQ, whose per-row `write_batch_partial` path avoids the whole-page re-send.

config_fields.name: write_mode
config_fields.description: Append (default), upsert, or delete.

config_fields.name: key
config_fields.description: Key columns. Required and non-empty for upsert/delete; ignored for append.

config_fields.name: delete_marker
config_fields.description:
Optional. Upsert only: rows whose `field` matches one of `values` are
deletes; all others are upserts. The marker field is stripped from
upsert rows before writing.

config_fields.name: rollback
config_fields.description:
Runtime rollback settings (#706): the run id to journal under, the
run-id column, and whether to journal before-images / keep a replaced
table. Injected per invocation by the CLI when a config has a
top-level `rollback:` block — not meant to be written by hand.

connectors.name: file
connectors.title: Local files
connectors.description: Local file sink; JSONL/JSON/CSV/XML/Excel/Avro/Parquet by extension, rollover, atomic temp+rename, atomic overwrite

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

dimensions.name: Schema evolution
dimensions.note: evolves the destination schema on drift

config_fields.name: path
config_fields.description:
The file to write, as a template. `{part}` is replaced by the rollover
part number (`00001`, `00002`, …); with a rollover cap and no `{part}`,
`-{part}` is inserted before the extension. A path ending in `/` is a
directory: files are named `part-{part}` plus the format's extension,
so `format` must be set. `${now.*}` tokens are resolved by the CLI
before the sink sees the path.

config_fields.name: format
config_fields.description:
File format: `auto` (default) resolves from the path's extension,
looking through a compression suffix (`.csv.gz` is CSV). ORC is
read-only and refused.

config_fields.name: compression
config_fields.description:
Compression of the finished file: `auto` (default) resolves from the
suffix (`.gz`, `.zst`). It applies to every format; Parquet, Avro and
Excel already compress internally, so a codec on them compresses the
file a second time and most readers then cannot open it without
decompressing first.

config_fields.name: if_exists
config_fields.description:
What to do with a file that already exists (default `replace`):
`replace` it, `append` to it (JSON Lines, CSV, raw text), or fail
with `error`. `mode` is accepted as another name for this field, and
`overwrite` / `error_if_exists` for its values.

config_fields.name: write_mode
config_fields.description:
`append` (default) or `overwrite` — replace the destination's whole
output set when the run succeeds.

config_fields.name: max_records_per_file
config_fields.description: Roll to a new file after this many records.

config_fields.name: max_bytes_per_file
config_fields.description:
Roll to a new file once the current one reaches about this many
bytes, counted on the records' JSON length before compression (on the
columnar Parquet path, their in-memory Arrow size). A single page
larger than the cap still lands in one file.

config_fields.name: create_dirs
config_fields.description: Create missing parent directories (default `true`).

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per upstream page. Informational: the sink writes each page it
is handed. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

config_fields.name: csv
config_fields.description: CSV dialect, used when the format is CSV.

config_fields.name: excel
config_fields.description: Worksheet name, used when the format is Excel.

config_fields.name: xml
config_fields.description: Record framing, used when the format is XML.

config_fields.name: avro
config_fields.description: Writer schema and block codec, used when the format is Avro.

config_fields.name: parquet
config_fields.description:
Compression (default `snappy`), row groups and an optional explicit
schema, used when the format is Parquet.

config_fields.name: json_lines
config_fields.description: Pretty-printing, used when the format is JSON Lines.

config_fields.name: encryption
config_fields.description:
Encrypt the output at rest (AES-256-GCM). Uncompressed JSON Lines and
raw text seal each record on its own line (base64), exactly as the
jsonl sink does, so the file stays appendable. Every other file —
compressed JSON Lines included — is sealed whole when it is
published, after any `compression`; appending to one decrypts it
first. Appending to an existing file that is not sealed the same way
is refused. The file source's `encryption` block reads both back.
Scratch files are not encrypted while the run is in progress; those
holding plaintext are readable by their owner only.

FileFormatChoice.description: Which format a file is in: resolved from its extension (`auto`) or fixed.

oneOf.description:
Resolve per file from its extension, looking through a compression
suffix (`.csv.gz` is CSV): `.jsonl`/`.ndjson`, `.json`, `.csv`, `.xml`,
`.xlsx`, `.parquet`, `.avro`, `.orc`, `.txt`.
One JSON value per line.
A JSON array (a lone object is one record).
Delimited text; dialect from `csv`.
XML; record framing from `xml`.
An Excel workbook; sheet from `excel`.
Apache Parquet.
Unparsed text, one record per file.
Apache Avro Object Container File; schema and codec from `avro`.
Apache ORC (read-only); projection from `orc`.
Detect from filename suffix: `.gz` → Gzip, `.zst` → Zstd, anything else → None.

IfExists.description:
What happens when a file this run writes already exists (`if_exists`).

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

oneOf.description:
Replace that one file: the new file is built beside it and swapped in,
so the old contents stay readable until the new ones are complete.
`overwrite` is accepted as another name.

Add to it. JSON Lines, CSV and raw text only — a JSON array, XML,
Excel, Avro or Parquet file cannot be appended to without rewriting.
With rollover, numbering continues after the highest existing part.

Fail the run instead of touching an existing file.
`error_if_exists` is accepted as another name.

FileWriteMode.description:
Pipeline-level write mode (`write_mode`).

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

oneOf.description: Write this run's files; leave everything else in place.

Replace the destination's whole output set. The run writes into a
hidden swap area beside the destination; only when it succeeds are the
files moved into place, and then files of an earlier run that match
the path template and were not rewritten are removed. A failed or
cancelled run leaves the previous output untouched. The move is not
atomic across files: a reader listing the destination while it runs
can see some new files beside some old ones. A move that was
interrupted is finished by the next run before it writes anything.

delimiter.description: Field separator. A single character; `"\t"` is accepted for tabs.

has_headers.description:
Whether the first row names the fields. When false, fields are named
`column_0`, `column_1`, … — the same fallback the REST source and the
`csv` connector already use. On write it decides whether a header row
is written.

quote.description: Quote character. A single byte; default `"`.

flexible.description:
Whether rows may have a different number of fields than the header.
`false` fails the read on the first ragged row, naming its line; `true`
keeps the fields the row has. Unset, each connector picks: the `file`
source is strict, the object-store sources and the REST source are
lenient.

null_values.description: Cell values read as `null` instead of a string (e.g. `["", "NULL"]`).

on_unknown_field.description:
What a streaming CSV writer does with a field the header does not
have. See [`CsvUnknownField`]. Whole-object encoders always write the
union of every record's fields, so it only affects the `file` sink.

CsvUnknownField.description: What a CSV writer does with a field that is not in the header.

oneOf.description: Add it as a new column; earlier rows get an empty cell for it.

Fix the header from the first page and drop the field, logging a
warning once per field.
Fix the header from the first page and fail the write naming the field.

sheet.description: Worksheet name, or an index as a string. Default: the first sheet.

XmlOptions.description:
XML record framing.

XML has no canonical record boundary, so one must be declared. On read,
`record_element` names the repeated element; without it the decoder falls
back to "the document's root children", which is right for the common
`<rows><row/>…</rows>` shape and wrong often enough that naming the element
is recommended in the docs.

record_element.description:
Element that delimits one record. Read: select these. Write: wrap each
record in one.

root_element.description: Document element wrapping the records. Write only.

schema.description:
An Avro schema (the JSON form: an object, an array for a union, or a
primitive name). On a **source** it is the *reader* schema every file
is resolved against — projection, aliases, defaults for added fields.
On a **sink** it is the *writer* schema; without it the schema is
inferred from the records.

codec.description:
Block codec for written files: `null` (default), `deflate`, `snappy`,
`zstd`. Reading detects the codec from the file header.

oneOf.description: Uncompressed blocks — the Avro default and the most portable.
Raw deflate (RFC 1951), readable by every Avro implementation.
Snappy with the per-block CRC-32 the spec requires.
Zstandard.

ParquetOptions.description:
Parquet write options.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

compression.description:
Column-chunk compression. Unset, it is `zstd` on the object-store and
SFTP sinks and `snappy` on the local file sink. A file-level
`compression` codec, when one applies, compresses the finished file
on top of this.

row_group_size.description:
Maximum rows per row group (default 1,048,576). Smaller groups let
readers skip more data and bound the writer's memory.

schema.description:
An explicit schema, in column order. Without it the schema is
inferred from the records and widened when a later page adds a field.
With it the file has exactly these columns: a record field the schema
does not name fails the write, and a value that does not fit its
column's type fails naming the column.

oneOf.description: Uncompressed pages.
Snappy: fast and universally readable.
Gzip.
Zstandard.
LZ4 (the `LZ4_RAW` codec).

ParquetField.description: One column of an explicit Parquet schema.

name.description: Column name — the record field it is read from.

nullable.description: Whether the column may be null or missing (default `true`).

ParquetType.description: A column type of an explicit Parquet schema.

oneOf.description: `true` / `false`.
32-bit signed integer.
64-bit signed integer.
64-bit unsigned integer.
32-bit float.
64-bit float.
UTF-8 text.
A calendar date, from `YYYY-MM-DD` text.
A UTC timestamp in milliseconds, from RFC 3339 text or epoch numbers.
A UTC timestamp in microseconds.
A UTC timestamp in nanoseconds.

A fixed-point decimal with the given precision and scale, from
numbers or numeric text.

JsonLinesOptions.description:
JSON Lines write options.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

pretty.description:
Pretty-print each record across several lines. The output is then a
stream of JSON documents rather than one record per line, which the
file source cannot read back.

EncryptionSpec.description:
The user-facing `encryption:` config block (state store / jsonl sink).


config_fields.name: bucket
config_fields.description: GCS bucket name.

config_fields.name: prefix
config_fields.description: Object-name prefix for written files.

config_fields.name: path
config_fields.description:
Object key template inside the bucket, after `prefix` — the file
sink's `path` (#777). May contain `{part}` (numbered objects) and
`${now.*}` tokens; a trailing `/` is a directory of
`part-{part}<extension>` objects. When set, `file_extension` is not
used. Unset: every run writes new objects named
`<prefix><run id>-<part><file_extension>` (`<run id>` is a fresh
time-ordered UUID, `<part>` is `00001`, `00002`, …).

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: if_exists
config_fields.description:
What to do when an object of the same name already exists
(`if_exists`): `replace` it (default), `append` to it (JSON Lines, CSV,
raw text) or fail with `error` (#777). Needs `path`. `mode` is
accepted as another name for this key, and `overwrite` /
`error_if_exists` for its values.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: write_mode
config_fields.description:
`append` (default) or `overwrite`: write the run's objects into a
hidden swap area and move them into place only after a successful
run, then remove objects of an earlier run that match `path` and
were not rewritten (#777). The move is one object at a time, so a
reader listing the destination while it runs can see new objects beside
old ones; a move that was interrupted is finished by the next run.
Needs `path`.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: format
config_fields.description:
Object format (default: `json_lines`). Set to `parquet` (with the
`arrow` feature) to write Parquet objects and enable the columnar
fast path.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description: Credential source.

config_fields.name: file_extension
config_fields.description: File extension for written objects (default `.jsonl`).

config_fields.name: max_records_per_file
config_fields.description:
Hard cap on records per uploaded object. `None` leaves the cap to
`batch_size`.

config_fields.name: max_bytes_per_file
config_fields.description:
Maximum **bytes** per object before rolling to a new one (#618).

Rows are a poor proxy for object size, so a rows-only cap either writes
tiny objects for narrow data or unbounded ones for wide data. It also
bounds the scratch disk each object needs while it is built. Counted
on the records' JSON length before any `compression` codec (on the
columnar Parquet path, their in-memory Arrow size), so the threshold
means the same thing whatever the codec.
`None` (the default) removes the byte cap. A single record larger than
the cap still gets its own object rather than being split or dropped.

config_fields.name: concurrency
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of uploads in flight (default 10): a page that rolls
into several objects uploads them concurrently while the next object
is encoded. `flush` returns only after every upload has landed.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per object when `max_records_per_file` is not set (without
`path`). Records accumulate across `write_batch` calls and an object
closes once it holds this many records, or at `flush`. `batch_size =
0` is the "no re-chunking" sentinel: no record cap, so JSON Lines and
the whole-object formats write one object per `flush`, and Parquet one
object per `write_batch` call. Ignored when `path` is set.

config_fields.name: storage_host
config_fields.description: Optional storage-host override (integration-test escape hatch).

config_fields.name: compression
config_fields.description:
Compression codec applied to each uploaded object body. Defaults to
[`CompressionConfig::Auto`](faucet_core::CompressionConfig::Auto) —
resolves against `file_extension` (so `.jsonl.gz` triggers gzip).
Requires the crate-local `compression` feature. Note: this sink does
**not** set the GCS `Content-Encoding` metadata, so consumers must
decompress explicitly.

config_fields.name: csv
config_fields.description: CSV dialect, used when `format: csv` (#604).

config_fields.name: excel
config_fields.description: Worksheet name, used when `format: xlsx` (#604).

config_fields.name: xml
config_fields.description: Record framing, used when `format: xml` (#604).

config_fields.name: avro
config_fields.description: Writer schema and block codec, used when `format: avro` (#719).

config_fields.name: parquet
config_fields.description:
Parquet writer options, used when `format: parquet` (#777):
`compression` (default `zstd`), `row_group_size`, explicit `schema`.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: json_lines
config_fields.description:
JSON Lines writer options (`pretty`), used when `format: json_lines`.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: encryption
config_fields.description:
Encrypt objects at rest (#777; the `encryption` feature). Scratch
files are not encrypted while the run is in progress; those holding
plaintext are kept in a private directory.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: scratch_dir
config_fields.description:
Directory the sink builds each object in before uploading it
(default: the system temporary directory). JSON Lines and raw text
need scratch space for the whole object; every
other format needs room for each object being built (up to
`concurrency` of them while uploads are in flight). A private
subdirectory is created in it for each sink.

oneOf.description:
Replace that one file: the new file is built beside it and swapped in,
so the old contents stay readable until the new ones are complete.
`overwrite` is accepted as another name.

Add to it. JSON Lines, CSV and raw text only — a JSON array, XML,
Excel, Avro or Parquet file cannot be appended to without rewriting.
With rollover, numbering continues after the highest existing part.

Fail the run instead of touching an existing file.

FileWriteMode.description:
Pipeline-level write mode (`write_mode`).

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a

oneOf.description: Write this run's files; leave everything else in place.

Replace the destination's whole output set. The run writes into a
hidden swap area beside the destination; only when it succeeds are the
files moved into place, and then files of an earlier run that match
the path template and were not rewritten are removed. A failed or
cancelled run leaves the previous output untouched. The move is not
atomic across files: a reader listing the destination while it runs
can see some new files beside some old ones. A move that was
interrupted is finished by the next run before it writes anything.

GcsSinkFormat.description: On-the-wire format of objects written by the GCS sink.

oneOf.description: Newline-delimited JSON — one JSON record per line (the default).

Apache Parquet. Each written object is a complete, self-contained
Parquet file. Enables the **columnar** fast path
([`Sink::write_batch_columnar`](faucet_core::Sink::write_batch_columnar))
so a `parquet`/`delta` → `gcs(parquet)` chain never materializes
`serde_json::Value`. Requires the crate-local `arrow` feature
(RFC 0002 / #375).
A single JSON array per object.

Delimited text. Columns are the union of every record's keys; dialect
from [`csv`](GcsSinkConfig::csv). Requires `file-format-csv` (#604).

XML, one element per record. Framing from
[`xml`](GcsSinkConfig::xml). Requires `file-format-xml` (#604).

An Excel workbook. Sheet name from [`excel`](GcsSinkConfig::excel).
Requires `file-format-excel` (#604).

An Apache Avro Object Container File, against `avro.schema` or a
schema inferred from the object's records; block codec from
`avro.codec`. Requires `file-format-avro` (#719). There is no ORC
variant: ORC is read-only.

Unparsed text: each record's `content` field (or the record as JSON)
on its own line (#777).

Take the format from the object name's extension — `path`'s, else
`file_extension` — looking through a compression suffix (#777).

GcsCredentials.description:
Credential source for a GCS client.

Serializes as `{ type: <method>, config: { … } }` (adjacent tagging,
snake_case discriminators) — the consistent auth wire shape shared by
every faucet connector:
`{ type: service_account_json_file, config: { path: "/run/secrets/sa.json" } }`.

oneOf.description: Path to a service-account JSON key file on disk.

Service-account JSON key as an inline string. Useful for
environment-variable injection via `${env:GCP_SA_JSON}` in CLI
configs.

Application Default Credentials — honours
`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, gcloud user creds, and the
GCE/GKE metadata server, in that order.

Anonymous credentials. Use this with emulators (e.g.
`fake-gcs-server`) that do not validate bearer tokens — the SDK
otherwise tries to fetch ADC tokens at request time and fails in
environments without GCP credentials.
Detect from filename suffix: `.gz` → Gzip, `.zst` → Zstd, anything else → None.

delimiter.description: Field separator. A single character; `"\t"` is accepted for tabs.

has_headers.description:
Whether the first row names the fields. When false, fields are named
`column_0`, `column_1`, … — the same fallback the REST source and the
`csv` connector already use. On write it decides whether a header row
is written.

quote.description: Quote character. A single byte; default `"`.

flexible.description:
Whether rows may have a different number of fields than the header.
`false` fails the read on the first ragged row, naming its line; `true`
keeps the fields the row has. Unset, each connector picks: the `file`
source is strict, the object-store sources and the REST source are
lenient.

null_values.description: Cell values read as `null` instead of a string (e.g. `["", "NULL"]`).

on_unknown_field.description:
What a streaming CSV writer does with a field the header does not
have. See [`CsvUnknownField`]. Whole-object encoders always write the
union of every record's fields, so it only affects the `file` sink.

CsvUnknownField.description: What a CSV writer does with a field that is not in the header.

oneOf.description: Add it as a new column; earlier rows get an empty cell for it.

Fix the header from the first page and drop the field, logging a
warning once per field.
Fix the header from the first page and fail the write naming the field.

sheet.description: Worksheet name, or an index as a string. Default: the first sheet.

XmlOptions.description:
XML record framing.

XML has no canonical record boundary, so one must be declared. On read,
`record_element` names the repeated element; without it the decoder falls
back to "the document's root children", which is right for the common
`<rows><row/>…</rows>` shape and wrong often enough that naming the element
is recommended in the docs.

record_element.description:
Element that delimits one record. Read: select these. Write: wrap each
record in one.

root_element.description: Document element wrapping the records. Write only.

schema.description:
An Avro schema (the JSON form: an object, an array for a union, or a
primitive name). On a **source** it is the *reader* schema every file
is resolved against — projection, aliases, defaults for added fields.
On a **sink** it is the *writer* schema; without it the schema is
inferred from the records.

codec.description:
Block codec for written files: `null` (default), `deflate`, `snappy`,
`zstd`. Reading detects the codec from the file header.

oneOf.description: Uncompressed blocks — the Avro default and the most portable.
Raw deflate (RFC 1951), readable by every Avro implementation.
Snappy with the per-block CRC-32 the spec requires.
Zstandard.

ParquetOptions.description:
Parquet write options.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

compression.description:
Column-chunk compression. Unset, it is `zstd` on the object-store and
SFTP sinks and `snappy` on the local file sink. A file-level
`compression` codec, when one applies, compresses the finished file
on top of this.

row_group_size.description:
Maximum rows per row group (default 1,048,576). Smaller groups let
readers skip more data and bound the writer's memory.

schema.description:
An explicit schema, in column order. Without it the schema is
inferred from the records and widened when a later page adds a field.
With it the file has exactly these columns: a record field the schema
does not name fails the write, and a value that does not fit its
column's type fails naming the column.

oneOf.description: Uncompressed pages.
Snappy: fast and universally readable.
Gzip.
Zstandard.
LZ4 (the `LZ4_RAW` codec).

ParquetField.description: One column of an explicit Parquet schema.

name.description: Column name — the record field it is read from.

nullable.description: Whether the column may be null or missing (default `true`).

ParquetType.description: A column type of an explicit Parquet schema.

oneOf.description: `true` / `false`.
32-bit signed integer.
64-bit signed integer.
64-bit unsigned integer.
32-bit float.
64-bit float.
UTF-8 text.
A calendar date, from `YYYY-MM-DD` text.
A UTC timestamp in milliseconds, from RFC 3339 text or epoch numbers.
A UTC timestamp in microseconds.
A UTC timestamp in nanoseconds.

A fixed-point decimal with the given precision and scale, from
numbers or numeric text.

config_fields.description: Target endpoint URL.

config_fields.description: HTTP method (default: POST).

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description:
Authentication: either inline (`{ type, config }`) or a `{ ref: <name> }`
pointer to a shared provider in the CLI's top-level `auth:` catalog.

config_fields.name: batch_mode
config_fields.description: How to batch records in requests.

config_fields.name: max_retries
config_fields.description: Number of retries on transient failures (default: 0).

config_fields.name: concurrency
config_fields.description: Maximum number of concurrent requests in Individual mode (default: 10).

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of records sent per outbound HTTP request. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`] (1000).

Interpretation depends on [`batch_mode`](Self::batch_mode):

- In [`HttpBatchMode::Array`] mode, `write_batch` re-chunks the
  incoming slice into `batch_size`-row chunks and issues one POST
  request per chunk, with each request body a JSON array of up to
  `batch_size` records. `batch_size = 0` is the **"no batching"
  sentinel**: the entire upstream `StreamPage` is forwarded as a
  single JSON array — useful when the source already chunks to a
  size the destination endpoint accepts.
- In [`HttpBatchMode::Individual`] mode the sink already sends one
  request per record, so `batch_size` has no effect on wire framing;
  the field is accepted for config-shape parity with other sinks
  and validated via [`faucet_core::validate_batch_size`] at load
  time.

Recommended value for HTTP POST endpoints that accept arrays:
match the destination's documented batch limit (commonly 100–1000
records per request).
