  sentinel**: the entire upstream `StreamPage` is forwarded as a
  single JSON array — useful when the source already chunks to a
  size the destination endpoint accepts.
- In [`HttpBatchMode::Individual`] mode the sink already sends one
  request per record, so `batch_size` has no effect on wire framing;
  the field is accepted for config-shape parity with other sinks
  and validated via [`faucet_core::validate_batch_size`] at load
  time.

Recommended value for HTTP POST endpoints that accept arrays:
match the destination's documented batch limit (commonly 100–1000
records per request).

AuthSpec.description:
A connector's `auth:` field: **either** an inline auth definition `A`
(the `{ type, config }` shape), **or** a `{ ref: <name> }` reference to a
shared provider defined in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

`ref` is mutually exclusive with inline fields — supplying both is a
deserialization error.

anyOf.description: Inline auth, spelled out on the connector.
A reference to a shared provider in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

HttpSinkAuth.description: Authentication method for the HTTP sink.

oneOf.description: No authentication.
Bearer token in the Authorization header.
HTTP Basic authentication.
Custom headers for authentication (e.g. API keys).

headers.description: Header name → value map applied to every request.

AuthReference.description:
A `{ ref: <name> }` pointer to a named provider in the top-level `auth:`
catalog. The only permitted key is `ref`.

ref.description: Name of the provider in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

HttpBatchMode.description: How records are sent in HTTP requests.

oneOf.description: Send one HTTP request per record.
Send all records as a JSON array in a single request.

      type: none    # one of: none, bearer, basic, custom

      # type: bearer

        # token: ""    # REQUIRED

config_fields.name: namespace
config_fields.description:
Multi-part namespace that contains the target table, e.g.
`["analytics", "events"]`. Must be non-empty; no segment may be empty.

config_fields.name: table
config_fields.description: Name of the Iceberg table (without namespace), e.g. `"page_views"`.

config_fields.name: create_table
config_fields.description:
Create the table if it does not exist, inferring the schema from the
first batch. When `false`, `load_table` is called at startup and an
absent table causes a `FaucetError::Sink` immediately.

Spelled `create_table` on the wire since #580, matching every other
table sink; the historical `create_if_missing` stays accepted as an
alias. Same default (`true`).

config_fields.name: partition_spec
config_fields.description:
Partition fields applied when creating the table. Ignored on writes to
an existing table (the table's existing spec is used).

config_fields.name: write_mode
config_fields.description:
Write semantics. Uses the shared [`faucet_core::WriteMode`] enum
(`append` | `upsert` | `delete`). Only `append` is supported at
runtime; non-append modes are rejected by [`IcebergSink::new`](crate::sink::IcebergSink::new) with a
`FaucetError::Config`. Upsert via equality-delete is tracked in #179.

config_fields.name: target_file_size_mb
config_fields.description:
Roll over to a new Parquet data file when the estimated file size
(uncompressed Arrow bytes × 0.4) exceeds this threshold.

config_fields.name: parquet
config_fields.description: Parquet codec settings.

config_fields.name: snapshot_properties
config_fields.description: Key-value pairs written into the Iceberg snapshot summary.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Maximum records buffered in memory before flushing a write to the
iceberg writer pipeline. `0` = no limit (single batch). Default: 10 000.

config_fields.name: cleanup_orphans_on_failure
config_fields.description:
Delete the Parquet data files this flush already uploaded when the
snapshot commit *definitively* fails, so they do not accumulate as
orphans.

Iceberg commits use optimistic concurrency: the data files are written
to object storage *before* the snapshot commit. iceberg-rust already
retries retryable commit conflicts internally (reloading table metadata
and re-applying the append against the latest snapshot — tunable via the
standard `commit.retry.*` table properties). If those retries are
exhausted (a competing writer won) the just-written files are orphaned —
valid Parquet, but referenced by no snapshot.

With this flag set, such orphans are deleted automatically on a
**definitive** loss (an exhausted commit conflict, or a catalog-rejected
commit). An **ambiguous** failure — e.g. a network error on the catalog
update where the commit may have landed server-side — is *never* cleaned
up regardless of this flag, because deleting then could remove files a
successful-but-unacknowledged commit references.

Default `false`: leave orphans in place (recoverable later via Iceberg's
standard `remove_orphan_files` maintenance) so cleanup is an explicit,
opt-in choice.

config_schema.title: IcebergSinkConfig
config_schema.description:
Configuration for the Apache Iceberg sink.

Records are buffered into Arrow batches, written as Parquet data files via
the iceberg-rust writer pipeline, and committed as a single snapshot per
`flush()` call using `Transaction::fast_append`.

## Append-only (v1)

Only `write_mode: append` is supported at runtime. The `write_mode` field
accepts the shared [`faucet_core::WriteMode`] enum, so `upsert` and
`delete` deserialise without error but are rejected by
[`IcebergSink::new`](crate::sink::IcebergSink::new) with a `FaucetError::Config`. Configuring
`write_mode: overwrite` still produces a deserialization error (it is not
a recognised variant). Equality-delete upsert is tracked in #179.

## Catalog feature gates

The REST catalog is included in the default build (`catalog-rest`). Glue,
SQL, and HMS each require their own Cargo feature (`catalog-glue`,
`catalog-sql`, `catalog-hms`). Configuring a disabled catalog type returns
`FaucetError::Config` at startup.

table.description: Name of the Iceberg table (without namespace), e.g. `"page_views"`.

alias. Same default (`true`).

CatalogConfig.description:
Iceberg catalog type and its connection settings.

Uses serde's internally-tagged enum: the JSON/YAML `type` key selects the
variant. Each variant carries the same inner fields (`uri`, `warehouse`,
`credential`, `properties`); the relevant set differs per catalog type and
is documented in each variant.

| Variant | Cargo feature required   |
|---------|--------------------------|
| `rest`  | `catalog-rest` (default) |
| `glue`  | `catalog-glue`           |
| `sql`   | `catalog-sql`            |
| `hms`   | `catalog-hms`            |

becomes the REST bearer token.

uri.description:

For REST: `https://catalog.example.com`.
For HMS: `thrift://hms:9083`.
For SQL: the JDBC/SQLx connection string, e.g. `postgres://…`.

Redacted in `Debug` output — never logged.

PartitionField.description:
A single partition field: source column + transform.

Supported transforms: `identity`, `year`, `month`, `day`, `hour`, `void`,
and parameterized forms `bucket[N]` and `truncate[N]` (e.g. `bucket[16]`,
`truncate[8]`). Used only when `create_if_missing: true` and the table
does not yet exist.

source.description: Source column name in the table schema.

WriteMode.description: Write semantics for a sink. Serialized snake_case. Default `Append`.

oneOf.description: Insert every record (today's behaviour).
Insert-or-update by `key`; optionally route delete-marked rows to deletes.
Delete by `key` for every record.

Replace the entire destination with this run's records (truncate-load /
full refresh). The old contents are swapped out atomically only after the
run completes successfully, so a mid-run failure leaves them intact. No
`key` is required — it is a whole-dataset operation, not a keyed one.

`gzip`, `lz4`, `none`.

connectors.name: jsonl
connectors.title: JSON Lines
connectors.description: JSON Lines file sink

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

dimensions.name: Schema evolution
dimensions.note: evolves the destination schema on drift

config_fields.name: path
config_fields.description: Path to the output file.

config_fields.name: append
config_fields.description: Whether to append to an existing file (default: false, truncates).

config_fields.name: pretty
config_fields.description: Whether to pretty-print each JSON record (default: false, compact).

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per upstream [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). The JSONL
sink writes records to disk one at a time through a buffered async
writer, so this field has **no behavioural impact** at the sink — it is
exposed purely for config parity across every sink in the workspace.
Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` (the "no batching" sentinel) and any positive value
produce byte-for-byte identical output for this sink: each record is
serialised and appended individually regardless of how upstream chunked
the page.

config_fields.name: compression
config_fields.description:
Compression codec for the output file. Defaults to
[`CompressionConfig::Auto`](faucet_core::CompressionConfig::Auto) —
`.gz` / `.zst` suffix selects gzip / zstd, anything else writes
uncompressed. Requires the crate-local `compression` feature.

config_fields.name: encryption
config_fields.description:
Encryption at rest (#207): seal every record line with AES-256-GCM and
write it base64-encoded (one sealed record per line, append-safe).
The natural fit for a file-backed DLQ holding sensitive failed rows;
`faucet dlq inspect/replay/discard` decrypt transparently given the
key. Mutually exclusive with `compression`. Requires the crate-local
`encryption` feature.

path.description: Path to the output file.

Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` (the "no batching" sentinel) and any positive value

Encryption at rest (#207): seal every record line with AES-256-GCM and

The natural fit for a file-backed DLQ holding sensitive failed rows;

oneOf.description: Detect from filename suffix: `.gz` → Gzip, `.zst` → Zstd, anything else → None.

EncryptionSpec.description:
The user-facing `encryption:` config block (state store / jsonl sink).

```yaml
encryption:
  key: ${vault:secret/faucet#state-key}
  # previous_keys: ["${env:OLD_STATE_KEY}"]   # rotation: read-only
  # algorithm: aes-256-gcm                     # default
```

key.description:
Key material used to seal new writes (and tried first on reads).
Should come from a secrets manager; derived to a 32-byte AES key via
SHA-256.

previous_keys.description:
Older keys tried (in order) when decrypting, for rotation. Never used
to seal new writes.

EncryptionAlgorithm.description:
Supported AEAD algorithms. A single variant today; the format byte in the
on-disk header leaves room for more without breaking old files.

oneOf.description: AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption (the default and only option).

connectors.name: kafka
connectors.title: Apache Kafka
connectors.description: Apache Kafka producer with QueueFull retry and topic routing

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

dimensions.name: Schema evolution
dimensions.note: evolves the destination schema on drift

config_fields.name: brokers
config_fields.description:
Comma-separated `host:port` bootstrap brokers, passed straight through
as librdkafka's `bootstrap.servers` (e.g. `"b1:9092,b2:9092"`).
Required; a blank value is rejected at config load.

config_fields.name: topic
config_fields.description:
Destination topic. Either a fixed name
(`{ type: fixed, name: events }`) or a per-record JSONPath lookup
(`{ type: from_path, path: "$.dest" }`) for multi-topic routing.
Required.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description:
Broker authentication — SASL/PLAIN, SASL/SCRAM, SSL client certs, or
SASL-over-SSL. Defaults to `{ type: none }` (plaintext brokers only).

config_fields.name: value_format
config_fields.description:
Encoding applied to each record to produce the message **value**.
Defaults to `{ type: json }`. The Confluent Schema Registry formats
(`confluent_avro` / `confluent_protobuf` / `confluent_json_schema`)
additionally require [`Self::value_schema`] and the crate's
`schema-registry` feature.

config_fields.name: key_format
config_fields.description:
Encoding applied to the value extracted at [`Self::key_path`] to
produce the message **key**. When unset, the extracted value is used
verbatim as UTF-8 key bytes (numbers and booleans are stringified) —
set this only when the key needs a real encoder, e.g. a Schema
Registry format. Ignored when `key_path` is unset (no key is sent).

config_fields.name: value_schema
config_fields.description:
Schema text (Avro `.avsc` JSON, Protobuf `.proto`, or JSON Schema) for
the **value** when `value_format` is a Confluent Schema Registry format
(`confluent_avro` / `confluent_protobuf` / `confluent_json_schema`).
Registered under the `{topic}-value` subject on first use. Required for
those formats; ignored otherwise.

config_fields.name: key_schema
config_fields.description:
Schema text for the **key**, used when `key_format` is a Confluent
Schema Registry format. Registered under `{topic}-key`. Required for
those key formats; ignored otherwise.

config_fields.name: key_path
config_fields.description:
JSONPath to the field that becomes each message's key (the first match
wins). Unset — the default — produces keyless messages, so the broker
partitions round-robin and log compaction cannot key on them. A path
that resolves to nothing is handled per [`Self::on_key_error`].

config_fields.name: partition_path
config_fields.description:
JSONPath to an explicit destination partition for each message. The
match must be an integer in `0..=i32::MAX`; anything else fails the
record with [`FaucetError::Sink`]. Unset — the default — lets
librdkafka pick the partition from the key (or round-robin when there
is no key), which is almost always what you want.

config_fields.name: headers_path
config_fields.description:
JSONPath to a flat JSON object whose entries become Kafka message
headers (values are stringified). Unset by default.

Applied on both the at-least-once and the transactional (exactly-once)
produce paths. A JSON `null` becomes a **valueless** header rather than
the string `"null"`, which is what Kafka's header model actually
expresses. The commit-token record on the side-topic never carries these
— it is faucet's own watermark, not a user record.

A path that resolves to nothing yields no headers; one that resolves to
a non-object fails the batch, matching [`Self::partition_path`]'s
strictness: a header map the operator asked for and did not get is not
something to paper over.

config_fields.name: on_key_error
config_fields.description:
What to do when [`Self::key_path`] resolves to nothing for a record:
`fail` (default) aborts the batch with [`FaucetError::Sink`], `skip`
drops the record (counted and warned once per batch), `round_robin`
sends it with no key and lets the broker place it. Only consulted when
`key_path` is set.

config_fields.name: compression
config_fields.description:
Producer-side batch compression, set as librdkafka's
`compression.type`: `none` (default), `gzip`, `snappy`, `lz4`, or
`zstd`. `lz4` or `zstd` usually pays for itself on JSON payloads.

config_fields.name: acks
config_fields.description:
Broker acknowledgement level (librdkafka `acks`): `all` (default, every
in-sync replica), `leader` (leader only), or `none` (fire-and-forget).
Anything but `all` can lose data on a broker failure, and
[`Self::idempotent`] requires `all` — that combination is rejected at
config load.

config_fields.name: idempotent
config_fields.description:
Enable the librdkafka idempotent producer (`enable.idempotence`),
which de-duplicates broker-side retries so a retried send cannot
append the message twice. Defaults to `true` and requires
`acks: all`. Independent of `delivery: exactly_once`, which adds a
transactional producer plus a commit-token side-topic on top.

config_fields.name: linger
config_fields.description:
How long the producer waits for more messages before sending a batch
(librdkafka `linger.ms`). Raising it trades latency for larger,
better-compressed batches. Defaults to 5 ms.

**Config granularity is whole seconds**, so the sub-second default is
not expressible in YAML — omit the key to keep 5 ms (writing
`linger: 0` *disables* lingering), and set `linger.ms` through
[`Self::extra_client_config`] for any other sub-second value.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of in-flight `FuturesUnordered` send futures during a
single [`Sink::write_batch`](faucet_core::Sink::write_batch) call.
Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

When `batch_size > 0`, the producer's `queue.buffering.max.messages`
librdkafka property is also set to this value (so the broker-side
buffer matches the sink-side send window) unless the user has
already set it via `extra_client_config`. `QueueFull` errors still
flow through the existing retry path (`queue_full_backoff` /
`queue_full_max_retries`) — the only effect of the in-flight cap is
to apply backpressure earlier inside the sink loop instead of
queueing the request and waiting for librdkafka to push back.

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: every record in the
incoming slice is enqueued into the `FuturesUnordered` immediately
(bounded only by `max_in_flight`) and the librdkafka
`queue.buffering.max.messages` knob is left at its default. Use it
for sources that emit a single page per run (small lookup tables,
one-shot drains) where forcing additional backpressure adds latency.

config_fields.name: message_timeout
config_fields.description:
Delivery deadline for a single message (librdkafka
`message.timeout.ms`), in **whole seconds**. Defaults to 30 s. Also
used as the timeout for `flush()`, for `init_transactions`, and as the
floor for the exactly-once `transaction.timeout.ms` (which is raised to
at least 60 s so a long `message_timeout` cannot make
`init_transactions` reject the producer).

config_fields.name: max_in_flight
config_fields.description:
Hard ceiling on concurrent in-flight sends inside one
[`Sink::write_batch`](faucet_core::Sink::write_batch) call. Defaults to
100 and must be at least 1. When [`Self::batch_size`] is non-zero the
effective window is `min(max_in_flight, batch_size)`, so this is the
cap that applies under the `batch_size = 0` sentinel.

config_fields.name: queue_full_backoff
config_fields.description:
How long to wait before retrying a send that librdkafka rejected with
`QueueFull`. Defaults to 100 ms. See
[`Self::queue_full_max_retries`].

**Config granularity is whole seconds**, so the sub-second default is
not expressible in YAML — omit the key to keep 100 ms (`0` retries
immediately with no pause).

config_fields.name: queue_full_max_retries
config_fields.description:
How many times to retry a `QueueFull` send before failing the batch.
Defaults to 3; `0` fails on the first `QueueFull`. `QueueFull` means
the local producer buffer is saturated — raising
`queue.buffering.max.messages` (via [`Self::extra_client_config`]) or
lowering [`Self::batch_size`] treats the cause rather than the symptom.

config_fields.name: exactly_once
config_fields.description:
Exactly-once knobs, grouped (#654 M20). Only consulted under
`delivery: exactly_once`; when present it supersedes the four
deprecated flat keys below.

config_fields.name: transactional_id_prefix
config_fields.description:
**Deprecated** — use `exactly_once.transactional_id_prefix`.

Optional namespace prefix for the producer's auto-derived
`transactional.id` (exactly-once mode only). The id is
`"{prefix}.{sanitized_scope}"`; `prefix` defaults to `"faucet"` when
unset. Set this to isolate transactional ids across clusters or
environments that share a pipeline scope namespace.

config_fields.name: commit_token_topic
config_fields.description:
**Deprecated** — use `exactly_once.commit_token_topic`.

Compacted side-topic that holds one commit-token record per pipeline
scope (exactly-once mode only). Auto-created with
`cleanup.policy=compact` if absent.

config_fields.name: commit_token_topic_partitions
config_fields.description:
**Deprecated** — use `exactly_once.commit_token_topic_partitions`.

Partition count used when auto-creating the commit-token topic.

config_fields.name: commit_token_topic_replication
config_fields.description:
**Deprecated** — use `exactly_once.commit_token_topic_replication`.

Replication factor used when auto-creating the commit-token topic.
`-1` means "use the broker default".

config_fields.name: extra_client_config
config_fields.description:
Raw librdkafka producer properties, applied **last** so they override
everything this config derives (`acks`, `enable.idempotence`,
`compression.type`, `linger.ms`, `message.timeout.ms`,
`queue.buffering.max.messages`). Empty by default.

The escape hatch for a knob faucet does not model — and the sharp edge
that goes with it: overriding a safety property here can weaken
delivery guarantees. The only exceptions are the exactly-once
invariants (`transactional.id`, `enable.idempotence`, `acks=all`),
which the transactional producer force-sets on top so an override
cannot break EOS.

config_schema.title: KafkaSinkConfig
config_schema.description:
Configuration for the Kafka sink connector.

Only [`brokers`](Self::brokers) and [`topic`](Self::topic) are required;
everything else has a safe default (`acks: all` + `idempotent: true`).
Validated at config load by [`validate`](Self::validate).

brokers.description:
Comma-separated `host:port` bootstrap brokers, passed straight through
as librdkafka's `bootstrap.servers` (e.g. `"b1:9092,b2:9092"`).
Required; a blank value is rejected at config load.

topic.description:
Destination topic. Either a fixed name
(`{ type: fixed, name: events }`) or a per-record JSONPath lookup
(`{ type: from_path, path: "$.dest" }`) for multi-topic routing.
Required.

auth.description:
Broker authentication — SASL/PLAIN, SASL/SCRAM, SSL client certs, or
SASL-over-SSL. Defaults to `{ type: none }` (plaintext brokers only).

value_format.description:
Encoding applied to each record to produce the message **value**.
Defaults to `{ type: json }`. The Confluent Schema Registry formats
(`confluent_avro` / `confluent_protobuf` / `confluent_json_schema`)
additionally require [`Self::value_schema`] and the crate's
`schema-registry` feature.

key_format.description:
Encoding applied to the value extracted at [`Self::key_path`] to
produce the message **key**. When unset, the extracted value is used
verbatim as UTF-8 key bytes (numbers and booleans are stringified) —
set this only when the key needs a real encoder, e.g. a Schema
Registry format. Ignored when `key_path` is unset (no key is sent).

value_schema.description:
Schema text (Avro `.avsc` JSON, Protobuf `.proto`, or JSON Schema) for
the **value** when `value_format` is a Confluent Schema Registry format
(`confluent_avro` / `confluent_protobuf` / `confluent_json_schema`).
Registered under the `{topic}-value` subject on first use. Required for
those formats; ignored otherwise.

key_schema.description:
Schema text for the **key**, used when `key_format` is a Confluent
Schema Registry format. Registered under `{topic}-key`. Required for
those key formats; ignored otherwise.

key_path.description:
JSONPath to the field that becomes each message's key (the first match
wins). Unset — the default — produces keyless messages, so the broker
partitions round-robin and log compaction cannot key on them. A path
that resolves to nothing is handled per [`Self::on_key_error`].

partition_path.description:
JSONPath to an explicit destination partition for each message. The
match must be an integer in `0..=i32::MAX`; anything else fails the
record with [`FaucetError::Sink`]. Unset — the default — lets
librdkafka pick the partition from the key (or round-robin when there
is no key), which is almost always what you want.

headers_path.description:
JSONPath to a flat JSON object whose entries become Kafka message
headers (values are stringified). Unset by default.

Applied on both the at-least-once and the transactional (exactly-once)
produce paths. A JSON `null` becomes a **valueless** header rather than
the string `"null"`, which is what Kafka's header model actually
expresses. The commit-token record on the side-topic never carries these
— it is faucet's own watermark, not a user record.

A path that resolves to nothing yields no headers; one that resolves to
a non-object fails the batch, matching [`Self::partition_path`]'s
strictness: a header map the operator asked for and did not get is not
something to paper over.

on_key_error.description:
What to do when [`Self::key_path`] resolves to nothing for a record:
`fail` (default) aborts the batch with [`FaucetError::Sink`], `skip`
drops the record (counted and warned once per batch), `round_robin`
sends it with no key and lets the broker place it. Only consulted when
`key_path` is set.

compression.description:
Producer-side batch compression, set as librdkafka's
`compression.type`: `none` (default), `gzip`, `snappy`, `lz4`, or
`zstd`. `lz4` or `zstd` usually pays for itself on JSON payloads.

acks.description:
Broker acknowledgement level (librdkafka `acks`): `all` (default, every
in-sync replica), `leader` (leader only), or `none` (fire-and-forget).
Anything but `all` can lose data on a broker failure, and
[`Self::idempotent`] requires `all` — that combination is rejected at
config load.

idempotent.description:
Enable the librdkafka idempotent producer (`enable.idempotence`),
which de-duplicates broker-side retries so a retried send cannot
append the message twice. Defaults to `true` and requires
`acks: all`. Independent of `delivery: exactly_once`, which adds a
transactional producer plus a commit-token side-topic on top.

linger.description:
How long the producer waits for more messages before sending a batch
(librdkafka `linger.ms`). Raising it trades latency for larger,
better-compressed batches. Defaults to 5 ms.

**Config granularity is whole seconds**, so the sub-second default is
not expressible in YAML — omit the key to keep 5 ms (writing
`linger: 0` *disables* lingering), and set `linger.ms` through
[`Self::extra_client_config`] for any other sub-second value.

batch_size.description:
Maximum number of in-flight `FuturesUnordered` send futures during a
single [`Sink::write_batch`](faucet_core::Sink::write_batch) call.
Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

When `batch_size > 0`, the producer's `queue.buffering.max.messages`
librdkafka property is also set to this value (so the broker-side
buffer matches the sink-side send window) unless the user has
already set it via `extra_client_config`. `QueueFull` errors still
flow through the existing retry path (`queue_full_backoff` /
`queue_full_max_retries`) — the only effect of the in-flight cap is
to apply backpressure earlier inside the sink loop instead of
queueing the request and waiting for librdkafka to push back.

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: every record in the
incoming slice is enqueued into the `FuturesUnordered` immediately
(bounded only by `max_in_flight`) and the librdkafka
`queue.buffering.max.messages` knob is left at its default. Use it
for sources that emit a single page per run (small lookup tables,
one-shot drains) where forcing additional backpressure adds latency.

message_timeout.description:
Delivery deadline for a single message (librdkafka
`message.timeout.ms`), in **whole seconds**. Defaults to 30 s. Also
used as the timeout for `flush()`, for `init_transactions`, and as the
floor for the exactly-once `transaction.timeout.ms` (which is raised to
at least 60 s so a long `message_timeout` cannot make
`init_transactions` reject the producer).

100 and must be at least 1. When [`Self::batch_size`] is non-zero the
effective window is `min(max_in_flight, batch_size)`, so this is the
cap that applies under the `batch_size = 0` sentinel.

queue_full_backoff.description:
How long to wait before retrying a send that librdkafka rejected with

[`Self::queue_full_max_retries`].

**Config granularity is whole seconds**, so the sub-second default is
not expressible in YAML — omit the key to keep 100 ms (`0` retries
immediately with no pause).

queue_full_max_retries.description:
How many times to retry a `QueueFull` send before failing the batch.
Defaults to 3; `0` fails on the first `QueueFull`. `QueueFull` means
the local producer buffer is saturated — raising
`queue.buffering.max.messages` (via [`Self::extra_client_config`]) or

exactly_once.description:
Exactly-once knobs, grouped (#654 M20). Only consulted under
`delivery: exactly_once`; when present it supersedes the four
deprecated flat keys below.

transactional_id_prefix.description:
**Deprecated** — use `exactly_once.transactional_id_prefix`.

Optional namespace prefix for the producer's auto-derived
`transactional.id` (exactly-once mode only). The id is
`"{prefix}.{sanitized_scope}"`; `prefix` defaults to `"faucet"` when
unset. Set this to isolate transactional ids across clusters or
environments that share a pipeline scope namespace.

commit_token_topic.description:
**Deprecated** — use `exactly_once.commit_token_topic`.

Compacted side-topic that holds one commit-token record per pipeline
scope (exactly-once mode only). Auto-created with
`cleanup.policy=compact` if absent.

commit_token_topic_partitions.description:
**Deprecated** — use `exactly_once.commit_token_topic_partitions`.

Partition count used when auto-creating the commit-token topic.

commit_token_topic_replication.description:
**Deprecated** — use `exactly_once.commit_token_topic_replication`.

Replication factor used when auto-creating the commit-token topic.
`-1` means "use the broker default".

extra_client_config.description:
Raw librdkafka producer properties, applied **last** so they override
everything this config derives (`acks`, `enable.idempotence`,
`compression.type`, `linger.ms`, `message.timeout.ms`,
`queue.buffering.max.messages`). Empty by default.

The escape hatch for a knob faucet does not model — and the sharp edge
that goes with it: overriding a safety property here can weaken

which the transactional producer force-sets on top so an override

KafkaSinkTopic.description: Where each message's destination topic comes from.

oneOf.description: One fixed topic for every record.

name.description: Topic name. Must not be blank.

oneOf.description: Per-record routing: the topic is read from the record itself.

path.description:
JSONPath to the topic name (first match wins). A record whose path
does not resolve fails the batch. Must not be blank.

oneOf.description: No authentication — plaintext brokers only.
SASL/PLAIN username + password.
SASL/SCRAM-SHA-256 or SCRAM-SHA-512.
SSL/TLS client-certificate authentication (path-based).

ca_path.description: Path to the CA certificate file.

cert_path.description: Path to the client certificate file.

key_path.description: Path to the client private key file.

key_password.description: Optional passphrase for the private key.

oneOf.description: SASL over SSL — combines a SASL mechanism with TLS transport.

ScramMechanism.description: SCRAM hash algorithm used for SASL/SCRAM authentication.

oneOf.description: SCRAM-SHA-256
SCRAM-SHA-512

KafkaValueFormat.description: How a Kafka message value (or key) is encoded on the wire.

oneOf.description: Parse value bytes as a JSON document.
Treat value bytes as a UTF-8 string. Invalid UTF-8 fails per `OnDecodeError`.

Pass value bytes through as a base64-encoded string inside the JSON record.
On the sink side, expects a base64 string in the source record.

OnKeyError.description: What the sink does when key/partition extraction fails for a record.

oneOf.description: Drop the record (logs a warning).
Surface `FaucetError::Sink` and abort the batch.
Send the record with no key (librdkafka picks the partition).

Acks.description:
Broker acknowledgement level required before a send is considered
delivered — librdkafka's `acks`.

oneOf.description:
`acks=0` — fire-and-forget: no acknowledgement is awaited, so a send
can be silently lost. Fastest and least safe.

`acks=1` — the partition leader has written the message; it can still
be lost if the leader fails before the followers replicate it.

`acks=all` — every in-sync replica has written the message. The
default, and the only level compatible with
[`KafkaSinkConfig::idempotent`].

KafkaExactlyOnceSpec.description:
Exactly-once delivery knobs for the Kafka sink (#654 M20).

These four apply **only** under `delivery: exactly_once` — the transactional
producer and its compacted commit-token side-topic. They used to sit flat
beside `brokers` / `linger_ms`, where nothing said they were inert in the
default at-least-once mode; grouping them is what makes that legible.

transactional_id_prefix.description:
Namespace prefix for the producer's auto-derived `transactional.id`.
The id is `"{prefix}.{sanitized_scope}"`; defaults to `"faucet"`. Set it
to isolate transactional ids across clusters or environments that share

scope. Auto-created with `cleanup.policy=compact` if absent.

Replication factor used when auto-creating the commit-token topic.
`-1` means "use the broker default".

flat and byte-identical in two connector configs, beside unrelated sizing
keys — one block, one definition, per Principle 4.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of documents per `insert_many` call. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`] (1000), which is a good balance for MongoDB's
per-request limits and round-trip cost.

When `write_batch` is handed a slice larger than `batch_size`, the
sink re-chunks it into `batch_size` slices and issues one
`insert_many` per chunk. `batch_size = 0` is the **"no batching"
sentinel** — the records slice is forwarded as a single
`insert_many`, no matter how large, so upstream `StreamPage` framing
flows through untouched.

**Not applied on the exactly-once path**: `write_batch_idempotent`
always writes the whole page in one transaction (one page = one
transaction), so re-chunking would break page↔watermark atomicity.

config_fields.name: ordered
config_fields.description:
Whether `insert_many` is **ordered**. Default `false` (unordered).

With the MongoDB default of `ordered = true`, the first failing
document (a duplicate `_id`, a validation error, …) aborts the rest of
the batch — the documents before it commit, those after are silently
dropped. Unordered (`false`) instead attempts every document and only
the genuinely-bad ones fail, so a single poison record can't drop the
rest of the batch (#78/#20).

config_fields.description: Append (default), upsert, or delete.

config_fields.name: key
config_fields.description: Key columns. Required and non-empty for upsert/delete; ignored for append.

config_fields.name: delete_marker
config_fields.description:
Optional. Upsert only: rows whose `field` matches one of `values` are
deletes; all others are upserts. The marker field is stripped from
upsert rows before writing.

config_fields.description:

run-id column, and whether to journal before-images / keep a replaced
table. Injected per invocation by the CLI when a config has a

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Maximum rows per multi-row `INSERT` statement. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

When the upstream `StreamPage` carries more records than `batch_size`,
the sink slices the page into `batch_size`-row chunks and issues one
multi-row `INSERT INTO ... VALUES (...), (...), ...` statement per
chunk. When `batch_size = 0`, the entire upstream page is forwarded
in a single multi-row `INSERT` — useful when the source already
chunks to a size tuned for MySQL.

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the full upstream
page is forwarded as one `INSERT`, subject to MySQL's
`max_allowed_packet` limit (default 64MB). Keep the default unless
the upstream `StreamPage` size is already tuned for MySQL.

config_fields.description:
Maximum number of connections in the pool. Defaults to 5.

Bounded on purpose: a finite pool keeps a wide fan-out from exhausting
the server's own connection limit. There is no "unlimited" setting.

from the first written page (#580). Enabled by default: a first-ever
sync cannot assume the destination already exists.

to be present in page 1 is not required forever, and a `NOT NULL`
inferred from one page turns page 2 into a hard failure the first time
a record omits the field. Narrowing is the `schema:` drift policy's job.

Set `false` to require the table to pre-exist and fail fast when it is
missing (the schema is managed externally, and a missing table means a
typo rather than a first run).

config_fields.name: destination
config_fields.description: Where to write the Parquet files (local filesystem or S3).

config_fields.name: schema
config_fields.description:
How the Arrow schema is determined. `None` means infer from the first
batch using `DEFAULT_SAMPLE_SIZE` records.

config_fields.name: compression
config_fields.description: Compression codec for column data.

config_fields.name: row_group_size
config_fields.description: Maximum rows per Parquet row group. Defaults to `DEFAULT_ROW_GROUP_SIZE`.

config_fields.name: max_rows_per_file
config_fields.description:
Roll over to a new file once the current writer has accepted this many
rows. `None` writes everything to a single file (until `flush()`).

config_fields.name: max_bytes_per_file
config_fields.description:
Roll over to a new file once the writer's `bytes_written()` exceeds this
threshold. Compared after each batch — so the actual file size may
slightly exceed the limit by one batch worth of data.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Re-chunk size for [`Sink::write_batch`](faucet_core::Sink::write_batch).
When `batch_size > 0` and an incoming page exceeds this many records,
the sink slices the page into `batch_size`-sized chunks and runs the
internal write path once per chunk. When `batch_size = 0` (the "no
batching" sentinel) the page is written through as-is. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

This is purely a knob for downstream callers that want tighter control
than the upstream source provides; for Parquet/S3 the source-defined
page size is usually optimal, so leaving this at the default (or even
at `0`) is recommended. The independent row/byte rollover thresholds
(`max_rows_per_file`, `max_bytes_per_file`) still apply regardless of
`batch_size`.

connectors.name: postgres
connectors.title: PostgreSQL
connectors.description: PostgreSQL sink (JSONB or auto-mapped columns)

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

dimensions.name: Schema evolution
dimensions.note: evolves the destination schema on drift

config_fields.name: connection_url
config_fields.description: PostgreSQL connection URL (e.g. `postgres://user:pass@host/db`).

config_fields.name: table_name
config_fields.description: Target table name.

config_fields.name: schema
config_fields.description:
Optional schema (namespace) qualifying [`table_name`](Self::table_name).

When set, both the AutoMap column-discovery probe and the `INSERT`
target `schema.table_name` explicitly. When unset (the default), the
table resolves against the connection's `search_path`, and column
discovery is scoped to whichever schema the `INSERT` actually resolves
to — so a same-named table in another schema no longer pollutes the
AutoMap column set (#146 M13).

config_fields.name: column_mapping
config_fields.description:
How to map JSON records to columns. Defaults to a single `jsonb`
column named `data`.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Maximum rows per multi-row `INSERT` statement. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

When the upstream `StreamPage` carries more records than `batch_size`,
the sink slices the page into `batch_size`-row chunks and issues one
multi-row `INSERT` per chunk. When `batch_size = 0`, the entire slice
is sent in a single `INSERT` — useful when the source already chunks
to a Postgres-friendly size.

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the entire upstream
page is forwarded in one statement, subject to Postgres' natural
per-statement bind-parameter limit of 65 535. AutoMap mode binds one
parameter per column per row, so the safe ceiling is roughly
`65_535 / num_columns` rows per call; JSONB mode binds a single
array parameter and has no such ceiling. Keep the default unless the
upstream page size is already tuned for Postgres.

**Recommended value: ~1000** — Postgres' multi-row `INSERT` sweet
spot. Larger chunks rarely add throughput and risk hitting the
65 535-parameter ceiling in AutoMap mode.

config_fields.name: max_connections
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of connections in the pool. Defaults to 5.

Bounded on purpose: the pool must be finite so a wide fan-out (many
matrix rows / shards) cannot exhaust the server's own `max_connections`.
There is no "unlimited" setting — raise this explicitly if you need more.

config_fields.name: create_table
config_fields.description:
Create the target table (and its schema, when `schema:` is set) if it
does not exist, inferring the columns from the first written page
(#580). Enabled by default: a first-ever sync cannot assume the
destination already exists.

Every inferred column is created **nullable** — a column that happened
to be present in page 1 is not required forever, and a `NOT NULL`
inferred from one page turns page 2 into a hard failure the first time
a record omits the field. Narrowing is the `schema:` drift policy's job.

Set `false` to require the table to pre-exist and fail fast when it is
missing (the schema is managed externally, and a missing table means a
typo rather than a first run).

config_fields.name: write_mode
config_fields.description: Append (default), upsert, or delete.

config_fields.name: key
config_fields.description: Key columns. Required and non-empty for upsert/delete; ignored for append.

config_fields.name: delete_marker
config_fields.description:
Optional. Upsert only: rows whose `field` matches one of `values` are
deletes; all others are upserts. The marker field is stripped from
upsert rows before writing.

config_fields.name: rollback
config_fields.description:
Runtime rollback settings (#706): the run id to journal under, the
run-id column, and whether to journal before-images / keep a replaced
table. Injected per invocation by the CLI when a config has a
top-level `rollback:` block — not meant to be written by hand.

config_fields.name: write_method
config_fields.description:
How append-mode rows are shipped: multi-row `insert` (default) or the
`copy` bulk-load fast-path (`COPY … FROM STDIN`, typically 5–10×
faster for bulk append). `copy` is append-only — it is rejected with
`write_mode: upsert|delete` — and the exactly-once path always stays
on `insert` so data + watermark commit in one transaction.

config_fields.name: scope
config_fields.description:
Scoped/windowed overwrite (#518): with `write_mode: overwrite`, replace
only the rows matching this scope (e.g. a date window) instead of
truncating the whole table. The prior out-of-scope rows are preserved.

config_schema.title: PostgresSinkConfig
config_schema.description: Configuration for the PostgreSQL sink.

schema.description:
Optional schema (namespace) qualifying [`table_name`](Self::table_name).

When set, both the AutoMap column-discovery probe and the `INSERT`
target `schema.table_name` explicitly. When unset (the default), the
table resolves against the connection's `search_path`, and column
discovery is scoped to whichever schema the `INSERT` actually resolves
to — so a same-named table in another schema no longer pollutes the
AutoMap column set (#146 M13).

column_mapping.description:
How to map JSON records to columns. Defaults to a single `jsonb`
column named `data`.

batch_size.description:
Maximum rows per multi-row `INSERT` statement. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

When the upstream `StreamPage` carries more records than `batch_size`,
the sink slices the page into `batch_size`-row chunks and issues one
multi-row `INSERT` per chunk. When `batch_size = 0`, the entire slice
is sent in a single `INSERT` — useful when the source already chunks
to a Postgres-friendly size.

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the entire upstream
page is forwarded in one statement, subject to Postgres' natural
per-statement bind-parameter limit of 65 535. AutoMap mode binds one
parameter per column per row, so the safe ceiling is roughly
`65_535 / num_columns` rows per call; JSONB mode binds a single
array parameter and has no such ceiling. Keep the default unless the
upstream page size is already tuned for Postgres.

**Recommended value: ~1000** — Postgres' multi-row `INSERT` sweet
spot. Larger chunks rarely add throughput and risk hitting the
65 535-parameter ceiling in AutoMap mode.

max_connections.description:
Maximum number of connections in the pool. Defaults to 5.

Bounded on purpose: the pool must be finite so a wide fan-out (many
matrix rows / shards) cannot exhaust the server's own `max_connections`.
There is no "unlimited" setting — raise this explicitly if you need more.

create_table.description:
Create the target table (and its schema, when `schema:` is set) if it
does not exist, inferring the columns from the first written page
(#580). Enabled by default: a first-ever sync cannot assume the
destination already exists.

Every inferred column is created **nullable** — a column that happened
to be present in page 1 is not required forever, and a `NOT NULL`
inferred from one page turns page 2 into a hard failure the first time
a record omits the field. Narrowing is the `schema:` drift policy's job.

Set `false` to require the table to pre-exist and fail fast when it is
missing (the schema is managed externally, and a missing table means a
typo rather than a first run).

key.description: Key columns. Required and non-empty for upsert/delete; ignored for append.

delete_marker.description:
Optional. Upsert only: rows whose `field` matches one of `values` are
deletes; all others are upserts. The marker field is stripped from
upsert rows before writing.

rollback.description:
Runtime rollback settings (#706): the run id to journal under, the
run-id column, and whether to journal before-images / keep a replaced
table. Injected per invocation by the CLI when a config has a
top-level `rollback:` block — not meant to be written by hand.

write_method.description:
How append-mode rows are shipped: multi-row `insert` (default) or the
`copy` bulk-load fast-path (`COPY … FROM STDIN`, typically 5–10×
faster for bulk append). `copy` is append-only — it is rejected with
`write_mode: upsert|delete` — and the exactly-once path always stays
on `insert` so data + watermark commit in one transaction.

scope.description:
Scoped/windowed overwrite (#518): with `write_mode: overwrite`, replace
only the rows matching this scope (e.g. a date window) instead of
truncating the whole table. The prior out-of-scope rows are preserved.

PostgresColumnMapping.description: How to map JSON records to table columns.

oneOf.description:
Insert each record as a single `jsonb` column. The column name
defaults to `"data"` but can be overridden.

Map top-level JSON keys directly to table columns.
Only keys that match existing columns are inserted; extra keys are ignored.

WriteMode.description: Write semantics for a sink. Serialized snake_case. Default `Append`.

oneOf.description: Insert every record (today's behaviour).
Insert-or-update by `key`; optionally route delete-marked rows to deletes.
Delete by `key` for every record.

Replace the entire destination with this run's records (truncate-load /
full refresh). The old contents are swapped out atomically only after the
run completes successfully, so a mid-run failure leaves them intact. No
`key` is required — it is a whole-dataset operation, not a keyed one.

DeleteMarker.description:
Identifies a record as a delete (vs. an upsert) by a marker field's value.
e.g. `{ field: "__op", values: ["d", "delete"] }`.

field.description: Field name whose value flags a delete.

values.description: Values of `field` that mean "this row is a delete".

RollbackWriteSpec.description:
Runtime rollback settings the executor hands a sink through its
[`WriteSpec`](crate::write_mode::WriteSpec) (`rollback:` field). Not user
config: the top-level `rollback:` block decides these, and the CLI injects
them per invocation.

run_id.description: The run id this invocation writes under.

run_id_column.description:
The destination column carrying the run id (stamped by the metadata
decorator).

journal.description: Record before-images of every upserted / deleted key.

keep_previous.description: Keep the replaced table of an overwrite as `<table>__faucet_prev`.

PostgresWriteMethod.description: How rows are shipped to PostgreSQL in append mode.

oneOf.description:
Multi-row `INSERT INTO … VALUES …` — the default. Works with every
write mode and the exactly-once transaction path.

`COPY … FROM STDIN (FORMAT text)` bulk load — typically **5–10×
faster** than multi-row `INSERT` for bulk append (issue #308).

**Append-only**: `COPY` has no `ON CONFLICT`, so combining
`write_method: copy` with `write_mode: upsert|delete` is rejected at
config load. The exactly-once path (`write_batch_idempotent`) always
uses the `INSERT`/transaction path regardless of this setting — the
watermark token must commit atomically with the page's data.

Error semantics are all-or-nothing per batch, the same as a failed
multi-row `INSERT`: one bad row fails the whole `COPY` and the DLQ
router's `on_batch_error` policy applies.

OverwriteScope.description:
Scope for a **scoped/windowed overwrite** (#518): with `write_mode:
overwrite`, replace only the destination rows matching this scope instead of
truncating the whole table. The sink-side sibling of scoped cleanup (#478).

v1 supports a half-open date/number **window** on a single column.

oneOf.description: Replace rows where `column` is in the half-open range `[from, to)`.

column.description: The destination column to window on.

config_fields.name: topic
config_fields.description:
Topic id (short name, not the fully-qualified path). The client forms

config_fields.name: project_id
config_fields.description:
GCP project id that owns the topic / subscription. Required for real
Pub/Sub; the emulator infers it from `PUBSUB_PROJECT_ID` when unset.

config_fields.name: endpoint
config_fields.description:
Override the Pub/Sub API endpoint (host:port or URL). Rarely needed —
prefer `emulator_host` for the emulator.

config_fields.name: emulator_host
config_fields.description:
Point the client at a Pub/Sub emulator (`host:port`). When set, auth is
skipped and the endpoint is taken from this value — mirrors the
`PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST` environment variable the SDK honours.

config_fields.name: credentials
config_fields.description: How to authenticate. Defaults to Application Default Credentials.

config_fields.name: value_format
config_fields.description: Record payload encoding. Default: `json`.

config_fields.name: ordering_key
config_fields.description: Ordering-key derivation. Default: `none`.

config_fields.name: attributes_field
config_fields.description:
Optional record field holding a JSON object of message attributes.
Values are stringified; the field is stripped from the payload before
encoding. Absent field → no attributes (not an error).

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per publish batch (1–1000). Default 100.

**The house `batch_size = 0` "no batching" sentinel does not apply
here** — Pub/Sub caps a single `Publish` request at
[`MAX_BATCH`](crate::MAX_BATCH) (1000) messages, so an
unbatched whole-page request is not expressible. `0` (and anything
above 1000) is rejected at config load; pages larger than `batch_size`
are re-chunked into several publishes.

config_fields.name: concurrency
config_fields.description: Bounded concurrent in-flight publishes. Default 4.

How to authenticate with Google Cloud Pub/Sub.

Serializes as `{ type: <method>, config: { … } }` (adjacent tagging,

config_fields.name: url
config_fields.description:
Full AMQP URI, e.g. `amqp://user:pass@rabbit:5672/%2f` (the vhost is
URL-encoded; `%2f` is `/`). `amqps://` selects TLS. Mutually exclusive
with `host`/`port`/`vhost`.

config_fields.name: host
config_fields.description: Broker host. Defaults to `127.0.0.1` when `url` is not set.

config_fields.name: port
config_fields.description: Broker port. Defaults to `5672` (`5671` with TLS).

config_fields.name: vhost
config_fields.description: Virtual host. Defaults to `/`.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description: Authentication. Defaults to [`RabbitMqAuth::None`].

config_fields.name: tls
config_fields.description: TLS settings. Disabled by default.

config_fields.description: Client connection name shown in the RabbitMQ management UI.

config_fields.description:
Requested heartbeat interval in seconds (`0` disables heartbeats).

config_fields.name: connect_timeout_secs
config_fields.description:
Upper bound, in seconds, on establishing the connection (TCP + AMQP
handshake, including any retries). Defaults to 30.

config_fields.name: connect_retries
config_fields.description:
Extra TCP connect attempts (exponential backoff) before giving up.
Defaults to 0 — an unreachable broker fails immediately.

config_fields.name: exchange
config_fields.description:
Exchange to publish to. Defaults to `""`, the default exchange, which
routes each message to the queue named by its routing key.

config_fields.name: exchange_kind
config_fields.description:
When set, `exchange` is declared (durable) with this type before the
first publish; otherwise it must already exist. Not allowed with the
default exchange.

config_fields.name: routing_key
config_fields.description: Static routing key for every message.

config_fields.name: routing_key_field
config_fields.description:
Top-level record field whose value (string, number or bool) is the

config_fields.name: routing_key_jsonpath
config_fields.description: JSONPath (e.g. `$.meta.route`) whose first match is the routing key.

config_fields.name: value_format
config_fields.description: How records encode into message bodies. Defaults to `json`.

config_fields.name: persistent
config_fields.description:
Publish with delivery mode 2 (persisted to disk on durable queues).

config_fields.name: mandatory
config_fields.description:
Publish with the `mandatory` flag: a message no queue is bound to
receive is returned by the broker and surfaces as a per-row error

Defaults to `false`.

config_fields.name: confirm
config_fields.description:
Enable publisher confirms: every batch waits for the broker to
acknowledge each message before the write returns. Defaults to `true`
(the reliable setting — without it a broker-side failure is invisible).

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Messages published before waiting on their confirms. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`]. `0` publishes the whole batch handed over by
the pipeline at once.

RabbitMqAuth.description:
RabbitMQ authentication.

Serializes with an adjacent `{ "type": <method>, "config": { … } }` tag in
snake_case, matching every other faucet connector's auth shape. The
hand-written [`std::fmt::Debug`] never prints the password.

oneOf.description:
No explicit credentials: the userinfo embedded in `url` is used, or the
AMQP default (`guest`/`guest`, which RabbitMQ only accepts from
loopback).
SASL `PLAIN` username + password. Overrides any userinfo in `url`.

SASL `EXTERNAL` — the broker authenticates the TLS client certificate
(requires `tls.enabled` plus `tls.client_cert_path`/`client_key_path`).

RabbitMqTls.description:
TLS (`amqps://`) settings. Server certificates are always verified — there
is no insecure mode.

enabled.description:
Connect over TLS. Also implied by an `amqps://` `url`. Requires the
connector's `tls` Cargo feature.

ca_cert_path.description:
PEM file of extra CA certificates to trust (in addition to the
platform's native root store) — for brokers with a private CA.

client_cert_path.description:
PEM client certificate for mutual TLS. Must be set together with

oneOf.description: Route on an exact routing-key match.
Broadcast to every bound queue, ignoring the routing key.
Route on a dotted routing-key pattern (`*` one word, `#` zero or more).
Route on message header values.

RabbitMqValueFormat.description: How a message body maps to and from a JSON record.

oneOf.description:
The body is a JSON document. The source fails (or skips, per
`on_decode_error`) a body that is not valid JSON; the sink serializes
each record as JSON.

The body is UTF-8 text, emitted as a JSON string. The sink requires
string records.

The body is opaque bytes, emitted as a standard base64 JSON string. The
sink requires base64 string records.

connectors.title: Redis
connectors.description: Redis (streams, lists, key-value) sink

dimensions.name: Config schema

config_fields.name: url
config_fields.description: Redis connection URL (e.g. `"redis://127.0.0.1:6379"`).

config_fields.name: sink_type
config_fields.description: The type of Redis data structure to write to.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of commands packed into a single Redis pipeline.
Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`] (1000), which is a comfortable
per-pipeline working set for Redis: pipelined commands are cheap,
so bigger windows amortise the round-trip but very large pipelines
can stall other clients sharing the server.

When `write_batch` receives a slice larger than `batch_size`, the
sink re-chunks it into `batch_size` slices and issues one Redis
pipeline per chunk. `batch_size = 0` is the **"no batching"
sentinel**: the entire records slice is packed into a single
Redis pipeline, no matter how large, preserving upstream
[`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage) framing.

config_schema.description: Configuration for the Redis sink connector.

Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`] (1000), which is a comfortable
per-pipeline working set for Redis: pipelined commands are cheap,
so bigger windows amortise the round-trip but very large pipelines
can stall other clients sharing the server.

When `write_batch` receives a slice larger than `batch_size`, the
sink re-chunks it into `batch_size` slices and issues one Redis
pipeline per chunk. `batch_size = 0` is the **"no batching"
sentinel**: the entire records slice is packed into a single
Redis pipeline, no matter how large, preserving upstream
[`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage) framing.

RedisSinkType.description: The type of Redis data structure to write to.

oneOf.description: Append records to a Redis list via `RPUSH`.

key.description: The list key.

oneOf.description: Add entries to a Redis stream via `XADD`.

key.description: The stream key.

oneOf.description: Set individual keys via `SET`, using a field from each record as the key.

key_field.description: The field name in each record whose value becomes the Redis key.

config_fields.name: host
config_fields.description: Cluster / endpoint host (e.g. `my-cluster.abc123.us-east-1.redshift.amazonaws.com`).

config_fields.name: database
config_fields.description: Database name.

config_fields.name: user
config_fields.description: Database user.

config_fields.name: credentials
config_fields.description: Authentication credentials.

config_fields.name: table_name
config_fields.description: Target table name.

config_fields.name: port
config_fields.description: Port. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_PORT`] (5439).

config_fields.name: tls
config_fields.description:
Whether to require TLS. Defaults to `true` (Redshift clusters require SSL
by default). `true` maps to `sslmode=require`; `false` maps to
`sslmode=prefer` (opportunistic TLS with plaintext fallback) — it never
forbids encryption outright.

config_fields.name: create_table
config_fields.description:
Create the target table (and its schema, when `schema:` is set) if it
does not exist, inferring the columns from the first written page
(#580). Enabled by default: a first-ever sync cannot assume the
destination already exists.

Every inferred column is created nullable, and without a DISTKEY or
SORTKEY — faucet has no basis to choose either, and the wrong choice is
baked into the table. Define the table yourself and set
`create_table: false` when distribution or sort matters, which it does
for any table you intend to query at scale.

config_fields.name: commit_rows
config_fields.description:
Commit-group size for the cross-page accumulator (#617).

Warehouse loads are dominated by per-operation overhead, and
`batch_size` can only ever *split* a page — it can never merge
undersized ones, so a small source page meant one expensive warehouse
operation per small page. Records now accumulate across `write_batch`
calls and commit once per threshold, plus once at `flush`.

`None` (the default) accumulates the **whole run** into one commit.
Set it to bound how much is buffered, or to commit progressively on a
long run. `0` means the same as `None`.

Only the append path accumulates: `delivery: exactly_once` and the DLQ
path commit per page, because a watermark must land with its own page
and a DLQ must report which rows of *this* page failed.

config_fields.name: commit_bytes
config_fields.description:
Estimated-bytes counterpart of [`commit_rows`](Self::commit_rows)
(#617). Rows are a poor proxy for how much work a warehouse commit is;
this bounds the buffered size. `None` (the default) removes the byte
threshold.

config_fields.description: Optional schema (namespace) qualifying [`table_name`](Self::table_name).

config_fields.name: write_strategy
config_fields.description: How rows are loaded. Defaults to [`RedshiftWriteStrategy::Copy`].

config_fields.name: copy
config_fields.description:
`COPY`-path settings, grouped (#654 M20). Applies only to
`write_strategy: copy`; when present it supersedes the six deprecated
flat keys below. This mirrors the BigQuery sink's `bulk_load:` block,
which is the house shape for a staged-load configuration.

RedshiftCredentials.description:
How to authenticate with Amazon Redshift.

Serializes as `{ type: <method>, config: { … } }` (adjacent tagging,
snake_case discriminators) — the consistent auth wire shape shared by every
faucet connector.

v1 implements only [`RedshiftCredentials::Password`]. The [`Iam`] and
[`RedshiftDataApi`] variants are accepted by the config parser (so a future
version can add them without a breaking change) but currently return a typed
[`FaucetError::Config`](faucet_core::FaucetError::Config) at client-build
time.

[`Iam`]: RedshiftCredentials::Iam
[`RedshiftDataApi`]: RedshiftCredentials::RedshiftDataApi

oneOf.description:
Username/password authentication (the user comes from
[`RedshiftConnection::user`]). The only mechanism supported in v1.

password.description:
The password (use `${env:…}` / `${vault:…}` to inject it, never a
literal).

oneOf.description:
IAM authentication via temporary cluster credentials
(`GetClusterCredentials`). **Not yet supported** — reserved for a future
version; building a client with this variant returns a typed error.

cluster_identifier.description: Provisioned cluster identifier used to request temporary credentials.

oneOf.description:
Authentication through the Redshift Data API (HTTP, not the PG wire).
**Not yet supported** — reserved for a future version; building a client
with this variant returns a typed error.

secret_arn.description: Secrets Manager ARN holding the database credentials.

RedshiftWriteStrategy.description: How the sink loads rows into Redshift.

oneOf.description:
Stage each page to S3 and bulk-load it with `COPY … FROM 's3://…'` — the
default and by far the fastest path for Redshift (the recommended way to
load data). Requires `staging_bucket` and `iam_role`.

Multi-row `INSERT INTO … VALUES (…), (…)`. Portable and needs no S3, but
much slower than `COPY` for anything beyond small batches. Redshift does
not recommend row-by-row inserts for bulk data.

RedshiftCopySpec.description:
`COPY`-path settings for the Redshift sink (#654 M20).

Six keys that only mean anything under `write_strategy: copy` used to sit
flat beside `table_name` and `batch_size`, with nothing saying they were
inert for `insert`. Grouping them is what makes that legible — the same
shape the BigQuery sink already uses for `bulk_load:`.

staging_bucket.description: S3 bucket used to stage `COPY` files. **Required** for `copy`.

staging_prefix.description:
Key prefix for staged objects (e.g. `redshift-staging/`). Empty by
default.

iam_role.description:
IAM role ARN Redshift assumes to read the staged file
(`COPY … IAM_ROLE '<arn>'`). **Required** for `copy`.

region.description:
AWS region of the staging bucket, used for both the S3 client and the
`COPY … REGION '<region>'` clause. `None` uses the SDK default.

endpoint_url.description:
Custom endpoint URL for S3-compatible services (e.g. MinIO) — a testing
aid; production loads use real S3.

RedshiftCopyFormat.description: Format of the staged file that `COPY` reads.

oneOf.description:
Newline-delimited JSON objects, loaded with `FORMAT AS JSON 'auto'`.
Maps by column **name** (order-independent) and handles NULLs and typed
columns cleanly — the default.

RFC-4180 CSV, loaded with `FORMAT AS CSV`. Column order is taken from the
destination table's schema and passed explicitly in the `COPY` column
list.

connectors.name: s3
connectors.title: Amazon S3
connectors.description: AWS S3 object sink

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

dimensions.name: Schema evolution
dimensions.note: evolves the destination schema on drift

config_fields.name: bucket
config_fields.description: S3 bucket name.

config_fields.name: prefix
config_fields.description: Key prefix for written objects.

config_fields.name: path
config_fields.description:
Object key template inside the bucket, after `prefix` — the file
sink's `path` (#777). May contain `{part}` (numbered objects) and
`${now.*}` tokens; a trailing `/` is a directory of
`part-{part}<extension>` objects. When set, `file_extension` is not
used. Unset: every run writes new objects named
`<prefix><run id>-<part><file_extension>` (`<run id>` is a fresh
time-ordered UUID, `<part>` is `00001`, `00002`, …).

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: if_exists
config_fields.description:
What to do when an object of the same name already exists
(`if_exists`): `replace` it (default), `append` to it (JSON Lines, CSV,
raw text) or fail with `error` (#777). Needs `path`. `mode` is
accepted as another name for this key, and `overwrite` /
`error_if_exists` for its values.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: write_mode
config_fields.description:
`append` (default) or `overwrite`: write the run's objects into a
hidden swap area and move them into place only after a successful
run, then remove objects of an earlier run that match `path` and
were not rewritten (#777). The move is one object at a time, so a
reader listing the destination while it runs can see new objects beside
old ones; a move that was interrupted is finished by the next run.
Needs `path`.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: format
config_fields.description:
Object format (default: `json_lines`). Set to `parquet` (with the
`arrow` feature) to write Parquet objects and enable the columnar
fast path.

config_fields.name: region
config_fields.description: AWS region. `None` uses the SDK default.

config_fields.name: endpoint_url
config_fields.description: Custom endpoint URL for S3-compatible services (e.g. MinIO).

config_fields.name: file_extension
config_fields.description:
File extension for written objects (default: `.jsonl`). Not used when
`path` is set.

config_fields.name: max_records_per_file
config_fields.description:
Maximum records per object. Since #618 the sink **accumulates across
`write_batch` calls** and rolls to a new object when this (or
[`max_bytes_per_file`](Self::max_bytes_per_file)) is reached, so a
small upstream page no longer means a small object. `None` removes the
record cap; with neither cap set the whole run lands in one object,
closed at `flush`.

config_fields.name: max_bytes_per_file
config_fields.description:
Maximum **bytes** per object before rolling to a new one (#618).

Rows are a poor proxy for object size — 10k wide rows and 10k
`{"id":1}` rows differ by orders of magnitude — so a rows-only cap
either writes tiny objects for narrow data or unbounded ones for wide
data. It also bounds the scratch disk each object in a format other
than JSON Lines or raw text needs while it is built. Counted on the
records' JSON length before any `compression` codec (on the columnar
Parquet path, their in-memory Arrow size), so the threshold means the
same thing whatever the codec. `None` (the default) removes the byte
cap.

A single record larger than the cap still gets its own object rather
than being split (which would corrupt it) or dropped.

config_fields.name: concurrency
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of uploads in flight (default: 10). A page that rolls
into several objects uploads them concurrently, up to this many, while
the next object is encoded; a large object's multipart parts are also
uploaded up to this many at a time. `flush` returns only after every
upload has landed.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per S3 object when `max_records_per_file` is not set (without
`path`). Records accumulate across
[`Sink::write_batch`](faucet_core::Sink::write_batch) calls and an
object closes once it holds `batch_size` records, or at `flush`.
Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no re-chunking" sentinel: no record cap
(still honouring `max_records_per_file` / `max_bytes_per_file` if
set). JSON Lines and the whole-object formats then write one object
per `flush`; Parquet writes one object per `write_batch` call, as the
sink always has. Many tiny S3 objects are a well-known anti-pattern
(per-request overhead, slower downstream reads, LIST/PUT cost), so
size objects with the caps rather than a small `batch_size`.

When both `batch_size > 0` and `max_records_per_file` are set, the
effective per-object cap is `min(batch_size, max_records_per_file)`.
Ignored when `path` is set.

config_fields.name: compression
config_fields.description:
Compression codec applied to each uploaded object body. Defaults to
[`CompressionConfig::Auto`](faucet_core::CompressionConfig::Auto) —
resolves against `file_extension` (so `.jsonl.gz` triggers gzip).
Requires the crate-local `compression` feature. Note: this sink does
**not** set the S3 `Content-Encoding` header, so consumers must
decompress explicitly.

config_fields.name: csv
config_fields.description: CSV dialect, used when `format: csv` (#604).

config_fields.name: excel
config_fields.description: Worksheet name, used when `format: xlsx` (#604).

config_fields.name: xml
config_fields.description: Record framing, used when `format: xml` (#604).

config_fields.name: avro
config_fields.description: Writer schema and block codec, used when `format: avro` (#719).

config_fields.name: parquet
config_fields.description:
Parquet writer options, used when `format: parquet` (#777):
`compression` (default `zstd`), `row_group_size`, explicit `schema`.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: json_lines
config_fields.description:
JSON Lines writer options (`pretty`), used when `format: json_lines`.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: encryption
config_fields.description:
Encrypt objects at rest (#777; the `encryption` feature). Scratch
files are not encrypted while the run is in progress; those holding
plaintext are kept in a private directory.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: scratch_dir
config_fields.description:
Directory the sink builds each object in before uploading it
(default: the system temporary directory). JSON Lines and raw text
go up in parts as they are written and need no scratch space; every
other format needs room for each object being built (up to
`concurrency` of them while uploads are in flight). A private
subdirectory is created in it for each sink.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.description:
File-name template inside `path` — the file sink's `path` file name
(#777). May contain `{part}` (numbered files) and `${now.*}` tokens; a
trailing `/` is a subdirectory of `part-{part}<extension>` files. When

named `<run id>-<part><file_extension>` (`<run id>` is a fresh

config_fields.name: if_exists
config_fields.description:

(`if_exists`): `replace` it (default), `append` to it (JSON Lines, CSV,
raw text) or fail with `error` (#777). Needs `file_name`. `mode` is
accepted as another name for this key, and `overwrite` /
`error_if_exists` for its values.

minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.name: write_mode
config_fields.description:
`append` (default) or `overwrite`: write the run's files into a
hidden swap area and move them into place only after a successful
run, then remove files of an earlier run that match `file_name` and
were not rewritten (#777). The move is one file at a time, so a
reader listing the destination while it runs can see new files beside
old ones; a move that was interrupted is finished by the next run.
Needs `file_name`.

minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

config_fields.description:

`.gz` / `.zst`). The `compression` feature (#777).

config_fields.name: format
config_fields.description: File format (default `json_lines`) (#604).

config_fields.name: file_extension
config_fields.description: File extension for written objects (default: `.jsonl`).

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per file when `max_records_per_file` is not set (without
`file_name`). Records accumulate across `write_batch` calls and a file
closes once it holds this many records, or at `flush`. `batch_size =
0` is the "no re-chunking" sentinel: no record cap, so JSON Lines and
the whole-file formats write one file per `flush`, and Parquet one
file per `write_batch` call. Ignored when `file_name` is set.
Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

config_fields.name: concurrency
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of file uploads in flight over the SSH session
(default 4): a page that rolls into several files uploads them
concurrently while the next file is encoded. `flush` returns only
after every upload has landed.

config_fields.name: max_records_per_file
config_fields.description:
Maximum records per file before rolling to a new one (#618). `None`
removes the record cap; the sink accumulates across `write_batch`
calls, so a small upstream page no longer means a small file.

config_fields.name: max_bytes_per_file
config_fields.description:
Maximum **bytes** per file before rolling to a new one (#618).

Rows are a poor proxy for file size, so a rows-only cap either writes
tiny files for narrow data or unbounded ones for wide data. It also
bounds the scratch disk each file needs while it is built. Counted on
the records' JSON length before any `compression` codec. `None` (the
default) removes the byte cap; a single record larger than the cap
still gets its own file rather than being split.
