`zstd`. Reading detects the codec from the file header.

oneOf.description: Uncompressed blocks — the Avro default and the most portable.
Raw deflate (RFC 1951), readable by every Avro implementation.
Snappy with the per-block CRC-32 the spec requires.
Zstandard.

ParquetOptions.description:
Parquet write options.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

compression.description:
Column-chunk compression. Unset, it is `zstd` on the object-store and
SFTP sinks and `snappy` on the local file sink. A file-level
`compression` codec, when one applies, compresses the finished file
on top of this.

row_group_size.description:
Maximum rows per row group (default 1,048,576). Smaller groups let
readers skip more data and bound the writer's memory.

schema.description:
An explicit schema, in column order. Without it the schema is
inferred from the records and widened when a later page adds a field.
With it the file has exactly these columns: a record field the schema
does not name fails the write, and a value that does not fit its
column's type fails naming the column.

oneOf.description: Uncompressed pages.
Snappy: fast and universally readable.
Gzip.
Zstandard.
LZ4 (the `LZ4_RAW` codec).

ParquetField.description: One column of an explicit Parquet schema.

name.description: Column name — the record field it is read from.

nullable.description: Whether the column may be null or missing (default `true`).

ParquetType.description: A column type of an explicit Parquet schema.

oneOf.description: `true` / `false`.
32-bit signed integer.
64-bit signed integer.
64-bit unsigned integer.
32-bit float.
64-bit float.
UTF-8 text.
A calendar date, from `YYYY-MM-DD` text.
A UTC timestamp in milliseconds, from RFC 3339 text or epoch numbers.
A UTC timestamp in microseconds.
A UTC timestamp in nanoseconds.

A fixed-point decimal with the given precision and scale, from
numbers or numeric text.

JsonLinesOptions.description:
JSON Lines write options.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

pretty.description:
Pretty-print each record across several lines. The output is then a
stream of JSON documents rather than one record per line, which the
file source cannot read back.

EncryptionSpec.description:
The user-facing `encryption:` config block (state store / jsonl sink).

```yaml
encryption:
  key: ${vault:secret/faucet#state-key}
  # previous_keys: ["${env:OLD_STATE_KEY}"]   # rotation: read-only
  # algorithm: aes-256-gcm                     # default
```

key.description:
Key material used to seal new writes (and tried first on reads).
Should come from a secrets manager; derived to a 32-byte AES key via
SHA-256.

previous_keys.description:
Older keys tried (in order) when decrypting, for rotation. Never used
to seal new writes.

EncryptionAlgorithm.description:
Supported AEAD algorithms. A single variant today; the format byte in the
on-disk header leaves room for more without breaking old files.

oneOf.description: AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption (the default and only option).

config_fields.name: target_command
config_fields.description:
The target executable to run (looked up on `PATH`, or an absolute
path), e.g. `target-jsonl` or `/opt/targets/target-postgres`.

config_fields.name: args
config_fields.description: Extra arguments appended after faucet's own `--config <file>` flag.

config_fields.name: target_config
config_fields.description:
The target's configuration object. Written to a private (0600) temp
file passed as `--config`; its string values are scrubbed from the
target's echoed stderr.

config_fields.name: env
config_fields.description: Extra environment variables for the target process.

config_fields.name: stream
config_fields.description:
The Singer stream name records are sent under. The `faucet` CLI fills
it from the matrix row id (or the pipeline name for a single-row
config) when unset; Template Hub sink templates set it to `${stream}`.
Library callers default to `faucet`.

config_fields.name: schema
config_fields.description:
The JSON Schema sent in the stream's `SCHEMA` message. When unset the
`faucet` CLI uses the pipeline's `contract:` (as JSON Schema) if one is
declared; otherwise the schema is inferred from the records and a new
`SCHEMA` is sent whenever a page widens it.

config_fields.name: key_properties
config_fields.description:
`key_properties` for the `SCHEMA` message. Defaults to `key` under
`write_mode: upsert`, else empty.

config_fields.name: flush_on
config_fields.description:
When written records count as persisted: `exit` (default) closes the
target at every flush and waits for a clean exit; `state` keeps it
running and waits for it to echo a `STATE`.

config_fields.name: flush_timeout_secs
config_fields.description:
How long a flush waits for the target to echo `STATE` (or to exit, with
`flush_on: exit`) before failing. Default 600.

config_fields.name: write_mode
config_fields.description: Append (default), upsert, or delete.

config_fields.name: key
config_fields.description: Key columns. Required and non-empty for upsert/delete; ignored for append.

config_fields.name: delete_marker
config_fields.description:
Optional. Upsert only: rows whose `field` matches one of `values` are
deletes; all others are upserts. The marker field is stripped from
upsert rows before writing.

config_fields.name: rollback
config_fields.description:
Runtime rollback settings (#706): the run id to journal under, the
run-id column, and whether to journal before-images / keep a replaced
table. Injected per invocation by the CLI when a config has a
top-level `rollback:` block — not meant to be written by hand.

config_fields.name: _activate_version
config_fields.description:
Internal: the table version for `write_mode: overwrite`, shared by
every writer of a run. Injected by the `faucet` CLI (the run clock in
milliseconds); library callers may leave it unset (a millisecond
timestamp is chosen on first use).

config_schema.title: SingerSinkConfig
config_schema.description:
Configuration for the Singer target bridge sink.

Runs an external [Singer](https://www.singer.io/) target executable and
feeds it faucet records as one Singer stream (`SCHEMA` / `RECORD` /
`STATE`, plus `ACTIVATE_VERSION` for `write_mode: overwrite`).

target_command.description:
The target executable to run (looked up on `PATH`, or an absolute
path), e.g. `target-jsonl` or `/opt/targets/target-postgres`.

args.description: Extra arguments appended after faucet's own `--config <file>` flag.

target_config.description:
The target's configuration object. Written to a private (0600) temp
file passed as `--config`; its string values are scrubbed from the
target's echoed stderr.

env.description: Extra environment variables for the target process.

stream.description:
The Singer stream name records are sent under. The `faucet` CLI fills
it from the matrix row id (or the pipeline name for a single-row
config) when unset; Template Hub sink templates set it to `${stream}`.
Library callers default to `faucet`.

schema.description:
The JSON Schema sent in the stream's `SCHEMA` message. When unset the
`faucet` CLI uses the pipeline's `contract:` (as JSON Schema) if one is
declared; otherwise the schema is inferred from the records and a new
`SCHEMA` is sent whenever a page widens it.

key_properties.description:
`key_properties` for the `SCHEMA` message. Defaults to `key` under
`write_mode: upsert`, else empty.

flush_on.description:
When written records count as persisted: `exit` (default) closes the
target at every flush and waits for a clean exit; `state` keeps it
running and waits for it to echo a `STATE`.

flush_timeout_secs.description:
How long a flush waits for the target to echo `STATE` (or to exit, with
`flush_on: exit`) before failing. Default 600.

key.description: Key columns. Required and non-empty for upsert/delete; ignored for append.

delete_marker.description:
Optional. Upsert only: rows whose `field` matches one of `values` are
deletes; all others are upserts. The marker field is stripped from
upsert rows before writing.

rollback.description:
Runtime rollback settings (#706): the run id to journal under, the
run-id column, and whether to journal before-images / keep a replaced
table. Injected per invocation by the CLI when a config has a
top-level `rollback:` block — not meant to be written by hand.

_activate_version.description:
Internal: the table version for `write_mode: overwrite`, shared by
every writer of a run. Injected by the `faucet` CLI (the run clock in
milliseconds); library callers may leave it unset (a millisecond
timestamp is chosen on first use).

FlushOn.description:
When the sink treats written records as durably persisted by the target.

Most Singer targets (including the Meltano SDK ones) emit `STATE` only when
they drain their buffers — usually at end of input — so `exit` is the
default: it works with every target.

oneOf.description:
Send a `STATE`, close the target's stdin and wait for a successful exit;
the next write starts a fresh target process (default).

Keep one long-lived target: send a `STATE` and wait for the target to
echo it back — the Singer contract for "everything before this state is
persisted". For targets that echo `STATE` as soon as the preceding
records are persisted.

WriteMode.description: Write semantics for a sink. Serialized snake_case. Default `Append`.

oneOf.description: Insert every record (today's behaviour).
Insert-or-update by `key`; optionally route delete-marked rows to deletes.
Delete by `key` for every record.

Replace the entire destination with this run's records (truncate-load /
full refresh). The old contents are swapped out atomically only after the
run completes successfully, so a mid-run failure leaves them intact. No
`key` is required — it is a whole-dataset operation, not a keyed one.

DeleteMarker.description:
Identifies a record as a delete (vs. an upsert) by a marker field's value.
e.g. `{ field: "__op", values: ["d", "delete"] }`.

field.description: Field name whose value flags a delete.

values.description: Values of `field` that mean "this row is a delete".

RollbackWriteSpec.description:
Runtime rollback settings the executor hands a sink through its
[`WriteSpec`](crate::write_mode::WriteSpec) (`rollback:` field). Not user
config: the top-level `rollback:` block decides these, and the CLI injects
them per invocation.

run_id.description: The run id this invocation writes under.

run_id_column.description:
The destination column carrying the run id (stamped by the metadata
decorator).

journal.description: Record before-images of every upserted / deleted key.

keep_previous.description: Keep the replaced table of an overwrite as `<table>__faucet_prev`.

connectors.name: snowflake
connectors.title: Snowflake
connectors.description: Snowflake SQL REST API sink

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

dimensions.name: Schema evolution
dimensions.note: evolves the destination schema on drift

config_fields.name: account
config_fields.description: Snowflake account identifier (e.g. `"xy12345.us-east-1"`).

config_fields.name: warehouse
config_fields.description: Warehouse to use for the session.

config_fields.name: database
config_fields.description: Database name.

config_fields.name: schema
config_fields.description: Schema name.

config_fields.name: table
config_fields.description: Target table name.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description:
Authentication: either inline (`{ type, config }`) or a `{ ref: <name> }`
pointer to a shared provider in the CLI's top-level `auth:` catalog.
A shared provider must yield a `Bearer` or `Token` credential, which
maps onto [`SnowflakeAuth::OAuth`]; key-pair JWT is always inline.

config_fields.name: create_table
config_fields.description:
Create the target table if it does not exist, inferring the column
**names** from the first written page (#580). Enabled by default: a
first-ever sync cannot assume the destination already exists.

Columns are created as nullable `STRING`, not as inferred types,
because the insert path projects every value with `::string` — a
`NUMBER` column would reject its own writer's cast. Define the table
yourself and set `create_table: false` when you want typed columns
(then use `schema:` drift to keep them aligned).

config_fields.name: commit_rows
config_fields.description:
Commit-group size for the cross-page accumulator (#617).

Warehouse loads are dominated by per-operation overhead, and
`batch_size` can only ever *split* a page — it can never merge
undersized ones, so a small source page meant one expensive warehouse
operation per small page. Records now accumulate across `write_batch`
calls and commit once per threshold, plus once at `flush`.

`None` (the default) accumulates the **whole run** into one commit.
Set it to bound how much is buffered, or to commit progressively on a
long run. `0` means the same as `None`.

Only the append path accumulates: `delivery: exactly_once` and the DLQ
path commit per page, because a watermark must land with its own page
and a DLQ must report which rows of *this* page failed.

config_fields.name: commit_bytes
config_fields.description:
Estimated-bytes counterpart of [`commit_rows`](Self::commit_rows)
(#617). Rows are a poor proxy for how much work a warehouse commit is;
this bounds the buffered size. `None` (the default) removes the byte
threshold.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of records sent per Snowflake SQL REST API request.
Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`] (1000), which matches the
documented sweet spot for the SQL REST API.

When `write_batch` is handed a slice larger than `batch_size`, the
sink re-chunks it into `batch_size` slices and issues one INSERT per
chunk. `batch_size = 0` is the **"no batching" sentinel** — the
records slice is forwarded as a single INSERT, no matter how large,
so upstream `StreamPage` framing flows through untouched.

config_fields.name: poll_timeout
config_fields.description:
Maximum wall-clock time to wait for an asynchronously-executed
INSERT to finish. Snowflake's SQL REST API answers an accepted but
not-yet-finished statement with HTTP 202 and a `statementHandle`;
the sink polls `GET /api/v2/statements/{handle}` until the statement
reports success before counting the rows as written. Without this
the sink would report success the moment Snowflake *accepted* the
statement, losing durability. Defaults to 300 seconds. Set to `0`
to poll indefinitely.

config_fields.name: bulk_load
config_fields.description:
Arrow columnar **bulk-load** mode (#381): buffer Arrow `RecordBatch`es
to Parquet, upload to an external cloud stage's backing storage, then
`COPY INTO <table> FROM @stage FILE_FORMAT=(TYPE=PARQUET)` over the SQL
REST API. Requires a binary built with this crate's `arrow` feature; a
config that sets it on an `arrow`-off build is rejected at construction.

This only drives the Arrow fast path the pipeline negotiates when the
source *and* sink are both columnar and no `Value`-shaped stage
(transforms, DLQ, exactly-once, masking, …) is configured. The regular
row path (`INSERT … PARSE_JSON`) and the exactly-once watermark MERGE
are unaffected — bulk-load is append-only.

AuthSpec.description:
A connector's `auth:` field: **either** an inline auth definition `A`
(the `{ type, config }` shape), **or** a `{ ref: <name> }` reference to a
shared provider defined in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

`ref` is mutually exclusive with inline fields — supplying both is a
deserialization error.

anyOf.description: Inline auth, spelled out on the connector.
A reference to a shared provider in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

SnowflakeAuth.description:
Authentication method for Snowflake.

Serializes as `{ type: <method>, config: { … } }` (adjacent tagging,
snake_case discriminators) — the consistent auth wire shape shared by
every faucet connector. `key_pair` is stateless (JWT minted locally);
`o_auth` carries a bearer token (and can be supplied via a shared
`auth: { ref }` provider).

oneOf.description:
JWT key-pair authentication.

Uses an RSA private key (PEM-encoded) to generate JWT tokens for the
Snowflake SQL REST API.
OAuth2 bearer token (e.g. from an external identity provider).

AuthReference.description:
A `{ ref: <name> }` pointer to a named provider in the top-level `auth:`
catalog. The only permitted key is `ref`.

ref.description: Name of the provider in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

SnowflakeStageConfig.description:
External-stage Parquet bulk-load configuration for the Arrow columnar path.

The named `stage` must already exist in Snowflake and point at the same
cloud location as `url`; the sink uploads Parquet files to `url` (via
`object_store`) and then references them as `@stage/<file>` in `COPY INTO`.

stage.description:
Named **external** stage in Snowflake — `MY_DB.MY_SCHEMA.MY_STAGE` or a
schema-relative `MY_STAGE`. Must already exist and reference `url`.
(Internal named stages use the `PUT` driver command, which the SQL REST
API does not support, so only external stages work here.)

url.description:
Object-store URL of the stage's backing location, e.g.
`s3://bucket/prefix/`, `gs://bucket/prefix/`, or
`azure://container/prefix/`. Uploaded Parquet files land here and are
then loaded via `@stage/<file>`.

storage_options.description:
Extra `object_store` config keys for the upload client (credentials,
region, endpoint, …), applied verbatim — e.g. `aws_access_key_id`,
`aws_secret_access_key`, `aws_region`, `google_service_account_key`.
Prefer `${secret:…}` / `${env:…}` interpolation for secret values.

match_by_column_name.description:
`MATCH_BY_COLUMN_NAME` COPY option — defaults to `CASE_INSENSITIVE` so
Parquet columns map to table columns by name. Set to `NONE` for
positional loading (rarely wanted for Parquet).

purge.description:
Append `PURGE = TRUE` so Snowflake removes staged files after a
successful load. Default `false` (leave files for audit / debugging).

config_fields.description: Target table name.

config_fields.name: column_mapping

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of rows per multi-row INSERT. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`] (1000); the recommended value for SQLite.

When the upstream `StreamPage` carries more records than `batch_size`,
the sink slices the page into `batch_size`-row chunks and issues one
multi-row INSERT per chunk, each wrapped in its own `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`
transaction. When `batch_size = 0`, the entire slice is written as a
single multi-row INSERT inside one transaction — useful when the
source already emits pages sized for SQLite (e.g. a Postgres source
configured with `batch_size: 1000`).

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: upstream framing is
preserved exactly, no internal re-chunking is performed.

config_fields.name: max_connections
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of connections in the pool. Defaults to `1`.

SQLite serializes writers at the file level, so a single SQLite file
can only ever have one writer at a time. A multi-connection pool against
one file therefore races for the write lock and risks `SQLITE_BUSY`
errors under concurrency; one writer is the safe default. Raise this only
if your workload is read-heavy against a WAL database (the sink opens the
pool in WAL mode with a `busy_timeout`, so extra connections can still
read concurrently with the single writer).

config_fields.name: create_table
config_fields.description:
Create the target table if it does not exist, inferring the columns
from the first written page (#580). Enabled by default: a first-ever
sync cannot assume the destination already exists.

Every inferred column is created **nullable** — a column that happened
to be present in page 1 is not required forever, and a `NOT NULL`
inferred from one page turns page 2 into a hard failure the first time
a record omits the field. Narrowing is the `schema:` drift policy's job.

Set `false` to require the table to pre-exist and fail fast when it is
missing (the schema is managed externally, and a missing table means a
typo rather than a first run).

config_fields.name: queue_url
config_fields.description: SQS queue URL (e.g. `https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/1234/my-q`).

config_fields.description: Custom endpoint URL for LocalStack / VPC endpoints.

config_fields.name: credentials
config_fields.description: AWS credentials. Defaults to the SDK default provider chain.

config_fields.name: message_group_id
config_fields.description:
FIFO message group id, applied to every message. Required by FIFO
queues; omit for standard queues. Default: none.

config_fields.name: message_deduplication_id_field
config_fields.description:
Record field whose (stringified) value becomes each message's
`MessageDeduplicationId` on a FIFO queue. A record missing the field
(or with a non-scalar value) fails per-record (DLQ-routable). Only used
when set. Default: none.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Max entries per `SendMessageBatch` request (1–10). Default 10.

**The house `batch_size = 0` "no batching" sentinel does not apply
here** — `SendMessageBatch` caps a request at
[`MAX_ENTRIES_PER_REQUEST`](crate::MAX_ENTRIES_PER_REQUEST)
(10) entries, so an unbatched whole-page request is not expressible.
`0` (and anything above 10) is rejected at config load; pages larger
than `batch_size` are re-chunked into several requests (also
re-chunked to stay under the 256 KiB per-request payload limit).

config_fields.name: concurrency
config_fields.description: Bounded concurrent in-flight `SendMessageBatch` requests. Default 4.

config_fields.name: retry
config_fields.description:
Per-record retry for partial failures, grouped (#654 M20). When
present it supersedes the three deprecated flat `retry_*` keys below.

config_fields.name: retry_max_attempts
config_fields.description:
**Deprecated** — use `retry.max_attempts`.

Per-record retry budget for partial failures. Default 5.

config_fields.name: retry_initial_backoff_ms
config_fields.description:
**Deprecated** — use `retry.initial_backoff_ms`.

Initial retry backoff (milliseconds). Default 100.

config_fields.name: retry_max_backoff_ms
config_fields.description:
**Deprecated** — use `retry.max_backoff_ms`.

Backoff ceiling (milliseconds). Default 30000.

How to authenticate with AWS SQS.

The AWS SDK default provider chain: environment variables, shared
config/credentials files, ECS/EKS container credentials, web-identity
tokens (`AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` / EKS IRSA), and EC2 instance
profiles — with automatic refresh/rotation.

Static access keys. Prefer `${env:…}` / secrets-manager interpolation
over literals in config files.

chain, which honors `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` + `AWS_ROLE_ARN` —
kept as an explicit variant so intent is visible in configs.

PartialRetrySpec.description:
Per-record retry budget for a sink whose bulk API reports **partial**
failures (#654 M20).

AWS batch APIs (`PutRecords`, `SendMessageBatch`) return a 200 whose body
marks individual entries as failed; the sink retries just those entries with
jittered exponential backoff. The three knobs that describe it used to sit
flat and byte-identical in two connector configs, beside unrelated sizing
keys — one block, one definition, per Principle 4.

Attempts per record before it is reported failed (DLQ-routable).
Default 5; `1` means "no retry".

First backoff, in milliseconds. Doubles per attempt, jittered by the
shared [`apply_jitter`]. Default 100.

max_backoff_ms.description: Backoff ceiling in milliseconds, applied before jitter. Default 30000.

config_fields.description:
Records per emitted `StreamPage`. `batch_size = 0` is the "no batching"

config_fields.name: verify_length
config_fields.description:
Verify each blob's byte length against the length the store
advertises, failing the read with
[`FaucetError::Source`](faucet_core::FaucetError::Source) on a short
(truncated) or over-long transfer. Cheap — a byte counter over a body
that is read anyway — so it defaults to `true`.

Skipped (with a debug log, not a failure) when the store advertises no
length, or when it reports a non-empty `Content-Encoding`: the body on
the wire is then transcoded and its length legitimately differs from
the stored blob's.

config_fields.name: verify_checksum
config_fields.description:

attribute and an Azure ETag is not a content hash, so there is nothing
to verify against. Setting it `true` is **rejected at config load**
rather than silently ignored — see `validate()`.

config_fields.name: compression
config_fields.description:
Compression codec applied to each downloaded object. Defaults to
[`CompressionConfig::Auto`](faucet_core::CompressionConfig::Auto) — the
codec is resolved per-object-key, so a single source can read a mix of
compressed and uncompressed objects. Requires the crate-local
`compression` feature.

`file-format-avro` (#719).

path. Requires the `arrow` feature (#777).
Detect from filename suffix: `.gz` → Gzip, `.zst` → Zstd, anything else → None.

delimiter.description: Field separator. A single character; `"\t"` is accepted for tabs.

has_headers.description:
Whether the first row names the fields. When false, fields are named

is written.

quote.description: Quote character. A single byte; default `"`.

flexible.description:
Whether rows may have a different number of fields than the header.
`false` fails the read on the first ragged row, naming its line; `true`
keeps the fields the row has. Unset, each connector picks: the `file`
source is strict, the object-store sources and the REST source are
lenient.

null_values.description: Cell values read as `null` instead of a string (e.g. `["", "NULL"]`).

on_unknown_field.description:
What a streaming CSV writer does with a field the header does not
have. See [`CsvUnknownField`]. Whole-object encoders always write the
union of every record's fields, so it only affects the `file` sink.

CsvUnknownField.description: What a CSV writer does with a field that is not in the header.

oneOf.description: Add it as a new column; earlier rows get an empty cell for it.

Fix the header from the first page and drop the field, logging a
warning once per field.
Fix the header from the first page and fail the write naming the field.

sheet.description: Worksheet name, or an index as a string. Default: the first sheet.

XmlOptions.description:
XML record framing.

XML has no canonical record boundary, so one must be declared. On read,
`record_element` names the repeated element; without it the decoder falls
back to "the document's root children", which is right for the common
`<rows><row/>…</rows>` shape and wrong often enough that naming the element
is recommended in the docs.

record_element.description:
Element that delimits one record. Read: select these. Write: wrap each
record in one.

root_element.description: Document element wrapping the records. Write only.

schema.description:
An Avro schema (the JSON form: an object, an array for a union, or a
primitive name). On a **source** it is the *reader* schema every file
is resolved against — projection, aliases, defaults for added fields.
On a **sink** it is the *writer* schema; without it the schema is
inferred from the records.

codec.description:
Block codec for written files: `null` (default), `deflate`, `snappy`,
`zstd`. Reading detects the codec from the file header.

oneOf.description: Uncompressed blocks — the Avro default and the most portable.
Raw deflate (RFC 1951), readable by every Avro implementation.
Snappy with the per-block CRC-32 the spec requires.
Zstandard.

columns.description:
Top-level columns to read, in file order. Default: every column. A
name the file does not have is an error, not an empty column.

ParquetReadOptions.description: Parquet reader options (the `parquet:` block of an object-store source).

columns.description:
Decode only these top-level columns. A name missing from an object is
an error naming the object and its columns. Unset: every column.

connectors.name: bigquery
connectors.title: Google BigQuery
connectors.description: Google BigQuery query source

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: project_id
config_fields.description: GCP project ID against which the query is billed and run.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description: Authentication — the `auth` field, consistent with every other connector.

config_fields.name: query
config_fields.description:
SQL statement to execute. May contain `${field.path}` placeholders that
are resolved against the parent-record context at runtime as
positional `?` markers; matched values are appended to
[`params`](Self::params) when the query is sent.

config_fields.name: use_legacy_sql
config_fields.description:
Whether to use BigQuery's legacy SQL dialect. Defaults to `false`
(Standard SQL). Set to `true` only for tables that use legacy
`[project:dataset.table]` references.

config_fields.name: location
config_fields.description:
Optional location override for non-`US` jobs (`"EU"`, `"asia-east1"`).
When `None`, BigQuery uses the default location for the queried tables.

config_fields.name: max_results_per_page
config_fields.description:
Maximum rows per page when calling `jobs.getQueryResults`. Smaller
values trade more HTTP round-trips for lower memory; larger values
trade memory for fewer requests. Defaults to 1000.

config_fields.name: params
config_fields.description:
Positional bind parameters for the query, sent as
[`POSITIONAL`](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/parameterized-queries)
query parameters in declaration order before any context-derived
values. Each value is shipped as a STRING parameter; BigQuery casts
as needed at execution time.

config_fields.name: statement_timeout
config_fields.description:
Per-statement server-side timeout. Forwarded to the
`timeoutMs` field on `jobs.query`. Defaults to 60 seconds. If
BigQuery does not finish the query within this window it responds
with `jobComplete=false`; the source then polls
`jobs.getQueryResults` until the job completes.

config_fields.name: poll_timeout
config_fields.description:
Maximum wall-clock time the source will spend polling
`jobs.getQueryResults` for a job that keeps reporting
`jobComplete=false`, before giving up with
[`FaucetError::Source`](faucet_core::FaucetError::Source).
Without this cap a job that never completes would loop forever.
Defaults to 300 seconds. Set to `0` to disable the cap and poll
indefinitely. Only the *completion* wait is bounded; once the job is
complete, ordinary `pageToken` paging is unaffected.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). Rows
returned by BigQuery are re-framed into pages of this size — every
time the buffer reaches `batch_size`, a page is yielded. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the **"no batching" sentinel**: the entire
result set is buffered and emitted in a single page. Useful for
small lookup tables, or for sinks that prefer one large request to
many small ones.

config_fields.name: read_api
config_fields.description:
Arrow columnar **Storage Read API** mode (#380). When `true`, the source
reads [`read_table`](Self::read_table) directly via the BigQuery Storage
Read gRPC API as Arrow `RecordBatch`es (no `jobs.query`), driving the
columnar fast path when the sink is also columnar and decoding Arrow →
JSON on the row path otherwise. Requires a binary built with this
crate's `arrow` feature and a `read_table`; the `query` field is ignored
in this mode. Full extract only — no incremental bookmark.

config_fields.name: read_table
config_fields.description:
Table to read in `read_api` mode: `dataset.table` (billed to
`project_id`) or a fully-qualified `project.dataset.table`. Required
when `read_api` is set; ignored otherwise.

config_fields.name: row_restriction
config_fields.description:
Optional Storage Read API `row_restriction` — a SQL predicate (e.g.
`state = "CA"`) pushed to the read session so BigQuery filters rows
server-side. Only used in `read_api` mode.

config_fields.name: selected_fields
config_fields.description:
Optional column projection for `read_api` mode — the columns to read.
Empty means all columns.

config_fields.name: max_streams
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of Storage Read API streams to request (`read_api`
mode). Defaults to 1 (a single ordered stream). Higher values let
BigQuery shard large tables; the source reads the returned streams
sequentially.

config_fields.name: stream_concurrency
config_fields.description:
How many Storage Read streams to consume concurrently (#621).

`max_streams` asks BigQuery to shard the table; this says how many of
those shards to read at once. Consuming them one at a time made the
request pointless — the read stayed as slow as a single stream.
Defaults to `4`; `0` and `1` both mean sequential.

Batches from different streams **interleave**. The Storage Read API
gives no ordering guarantee across streams — that is what sharding
means — so this costs nothing a caller could have relied on. Each
in-flight stream carries its own decode buffer, so this is also the
memory knob.

connectors.name: clickhouse
connectors.title: ClickHouse
connectors.description: ClickHouse query source (HTTP interface, JSONEachRow streaming)

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: query
config_fields.description:
SQL `SELECT` query to run. The output format is set to `JSONEachRow`
via the request settings, so **do not** append a `FORMAT` clause. Use
the literal `@bookmark` token to push the incremental cursor down into
the `WHERE` clause; use `{key}` tokens to inject parent-context values in
a matrix child.

config_fields.name: url
config_fields.description:
Full base URL of the ClickHouse HTTP interface, e.g.
`"http://localhost:8123"`. Mutually exclusive with
[`host`](Self::host). A trailing slash is trimmed.

config_fields.name: host
config_fields.description:

[`DEFAULT_HTTP_PORT`] (`8123`).

config_fields.name: tls

`false`.

config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). `0` emits
the whole result set as a single page. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

config_fields.name: replication
config_fields.description: Replication mode. Defaults to [`ClickHouseReplication::Full`].

config_fields.name: state_key
config_fields.description:
Explicit state-store key for the bookmark. When unset, a key is derived
from the connection host and a query fingerprint.

config_schema.title: ClickHouseSourceConfig
config_schema.description: Configuration for [`ClickHouseSource`](crate::ClickHouseSource).

url.description:
Full base URL of the ClickHouse HTTP interface, e.g.
`"http://localhost:8123"`. Mutually exclusive with
[`host`](Self::host). A trailing slash is trimmed.

host.description:
Hostname of the ClickHouse server. Mutually exclusive with
[`url`](Self::url); combined with [`http_port`](Self::http_port) and
[`tls`](Self::tls) to build the base URL.

http_port.description:
HTTP-interface port used with [`host`](Self::host). Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_HTTP_PORT`] (`8123`).

tls.description:
Use `https://` instead of `http://` when building the base URL from
[`host`](Self::host). Ignored when [`url`](Self::url) is set. Defaults to
`false`.

user.description: ClickHouse user. When set, sent as the `X-ClickHouse-User` header.

password.description: ClickHouse password. When set, sent as the `X-ClickHouse-Key` header.

query.description:
SQL `SELECT` query to run. The output format is set to `JSONEachRow`
via the request settings, so **do not** append a `FORMAT` clause. Use
the literal `@bookmark` token to push the incremental cursor down into
the `WHERE` clause; use `{key}` tokens to inject parent-context values in
a matrix child.

batch_size.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). `0` emits
the whole result set as a single page. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

state_key.description:
Explicit state-store key for the bookmark. When unset, a key is derived
from the connection host and a query fingerprint.

ClickHouseReplication.description:
How the source replicates rows across runs.

Serializes as `{ type: full }` or
`{ type: incremental, column: "...", initial_value: ... }`.

oneOf.description: Every run fetches the full result set (default).

Only rows whose `column` is strictly greater than the stored bookmark
(or `initial_value` on the first run) are emitted.

The bookmark is applied two ways: if the query contains the literal
token `@bookmark`, it is substituted as an injection-safe SQL literal so
the server filters (efficient pushdown); the source *also* filters
client-side as a correctness backstop. The new maximum of `column` is
persisted on the final page.

column.description: Column whose value is the replication cursor (e.g. `updated_at`).

initial_value.description: Lower bound used on the first run, before any bookmark is stored.

connectors.name: csv
connectors.title: CSV
connectors.description: CSV file source

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: path
config_fields.description: Path to the CSV file.

config_fields.name: has_headers
config_fields.description: Whether the file has a header row. Defaults to `true`.

config_fields.name: delimiter
config_fields.description: Field delimiter byte. Defaults to `b','`.

config_fields.name: quote
config_fields.description: Quote character byte. Defaults to `b'"'`.

config_fields.name: flexible
config_fields.description:
Whether to tolerate rows with a field count that differs from the
header (or from the first data row when header-less). Defaults to
`false` (strict).

When `false` (the default), a row whose field count does not match the
expected width is a structural defect and aborts the run with a typed
[`FaucetError::Source`](faucet_core::FaucetError::Source) naming the
offending line — silently emitting an incomplete record would corrupt
downstream consumers. Set to `true` only when ragged rows are expected
and acceptable (short rows yield records missing the trailing columns;
long rows gain `column_N` keys).

config_fields.name: null_values
config_fields.description:
Fields equal to any of these strings decode as JSON `null` instead of a
string (default: none, every field is a string). `[""]` treats empty
fields as null; sentinels such as `"NULL"` or `"#N/A"` can be listed.
Headers are never mapped, and a quoted empty field is mapped like an
unquoted one (the reader does not report quoting per field).

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). Rows are
parsed line-by-line from a tokio `BufReader` and yielded whenever the
buffer reaches this size. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the file is fully
drained and the entire result set is emitted in a single page. Useful
for small lookup tables or for sinks (e.g. SQL `COPY`, BigQuery load
jobs) that prefer one large request to many small ones.

config_fields.name: compression
config_fields.description:
Compression codec for the input file. Defaults to
[`CompressionConfig::Auto`](faucet_core::CompressionConfig::Auto) —
`.gz` / `.zst` suffix selects gzip / zstd. Requires the crate-local
`compression` feature.

connectors.name: databricks
connectors.title: Databricks
connectors.description: Databricks SQL query source (Statement Execution API; typed rows, chunk pagination, incremental)

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: workspace_url
config_fields.description: Workspace base URL, e.g. `https://dbc-abc123.cloud.databricks.com`.

config_fields.name: warehouse_id
config_fields.description: Target SQL Warehouse id.

config_fields.name: sql
config_fields.description:
The SQL statement to run. May contain `:name` parameter markers (see
[`parameters`](Self::parameters)) and a `${bookmark}` token for
incremental replication.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description: Authentication (PAT / OAuth bearer), inline or via a shared `auth: { ref }`.

config_fields.name: catalog
config_fields.description: Default Unity Catalog catalog for the statement.

config_fields.name: schema
config_fields.description: Default schema for the statement.

config_fields.name: parameters
config_fields.description: Named SQL parameters (`:name` markers).

config_fields.name: wait_timeout_secs
config_fields.description:
Server-side wait before the statement goes async (seconds). Databricks
accepts `0` (fully async) or `5`–`50`. Defaults to `50`.

config_fields.name: poll_interval_secs
config_fields.description: Client poll cadence while the statement is `PENDING`/`RUNNING` (seconds).

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Page size — rows accumulated before a `StreamPage` is emitted.
Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`](faucet_core::DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE).

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: result chunks are fully
drained and the entire result set is emitted in a single page. Useful
for small lookup tables or for sinks (e.g. SQL `COPY`, BigQuery load
jobs) that prefer one large request to many small ones.

config_fields.name: arrow_native
config_fields.description:
Fetch results as Apache Arrow instead of JSON. When `true`, the
statement is submitted with `EXTERNAL_LINKS` disposition +
`ARROW_STREAM` format; each chunk's presigned link is fetched and
decoded as an Arrow IPC stream. This enables the **columnar** fast path
([`Source::stream_batches`](faucet_core::Source::stream_batches)) so a
`databricks → parquet`/`delta` chain skips the per-cell JSON decode.

Requires the crate-local `arrow` feature, and (in this release) only
[`DatabricksReplication::Full`] — the columnar path does not run the
per-row client-side incremental filter. Defaults to `false` (the
`INLINE` + `JSON_ARRAY` row path, unchanged). RFC 0002 / #375.

config_fields.name: replication
config_fields.description: Replication mode. Defaults to [`DatabricksReplication::Full`].

config_fields.name: state_key
config_fields.description:
Explicit state-store key for the incremental bookmark. When unset, a key
is derived from the workspace/warehouse and a query fingerprint.

config_schema.title: DatabricksSourceConfig
config_schema.description:
Configuration for the Databricks SQL query source.

Runs `sql` against a Databricks SQL Warehouse via the Statement Execution
REST API and streams the result rows as typed JSON objects.

sql.description:
The SQL statement to run. May contain `:name` parameter markers (see
[`parameters`](Self::parameters)) and a `${bookmark}` token for
incremental replication.

auth.description: Authentication (PAT / OAuth bearer), inline or via a shared `auth: { ref }`.

catalog.description: Default Unity Catalog catalog for the statement.

schema.description: Default schema for the statement.

wait_timeout_secs.description:
Server-side wait before the statement goes async (seconds). Databricks
accepts `0` (fully async) or `5`–`50`. Defaults to `50`.

poll_interval_secs.description: Client poll cadence while the statement is `PENDING`/`RUNNING` (seconds).

batch_size.description:
Page size — rows accumulated before a `StreamPage` is emitted.
Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`](faucet_core::DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE).

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: result chunks are fully
drained and the entire result set is emitted in a single page. Useful
for small lookup tables or for sinks (e.g. SQL `COPY`, BigQuery load
jobs) that prefer one large request to many small ones.

arrow_native.description:
Fetch results as Apache Arrow instead of JSON. When `true`, the
statement is submitted with `EXTERNAL_LINKS` disposition +
`ARROW_STREAM` format; each chunk's presigned link is fetched and
decoded as an Arrow IPC stream. This enables the **columnar** fast path
([`Source::stream_batches`](faucet_core::Source::stream_batches)) so a
`databricks → parquet`/`delta` chain skips the per-cell JSON decode.

Requires the crate-local `arrow` feature, and (in this release) only
[`DatabricksReplication::Full`] — the columnar path does not run the
per-row client-side incremental filter. Defaults to `false` (the
`INLINE` + `JSON_ARRAY` row path, unchanged). RFC 0002 / #375.

state_key.description:
Explicit state-store key for the incremental bookmark. When unset, a key
is derived from the workspace/warehouse and a query fingerprint.

AuthSpec.description:
A connector's `auth:` field: **either** an inline auth definition `A`
(the `{ type, config }` shape), **or** a `{ ref: <name> }` reference to a
shared provider defined in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

`ref` is mutually exclusive with inline fields — supplying both is a
deserialization error.

anyOf.description: Inline auth, spelled out on the connector.
A reference to a shared provider in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

DatabricksAuth.description:
Authentication for the Databricks SQL Statement Execution API.

Both variants send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` — Databricks accepts a
Personal Access Token (PAT) or an OAuth machine-to-machine (M2M) access
token in the same header. Uses the project-wide adjacently-tagged
`{ type, config }` shape, e.g. `auth: { type: pat, config: { token: … } }`.
A shared `auth: { ref: <name> }` provider that yields a `Bearer`/`Token`
credential maps onto [`DatabricksAuth::Token`].

Same shape as [`faucet_common_databricks::DatabricksAuth`] (which the sink
uses); kept as this crate's own type so its public API is unchanged, and
converted with `From` where the shared client needs it.

oneOf.description: Databricks Personal Access Token.
A pre-obtained OAuth (M2M) bearer token.

AuthReference.description:
A `{ ref: <name> }` pointer to a named provider in the top-level `auth:`
catalog. The only permitted key is `ref`.

ref.description: Name of the provider in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

DatabricksParam.description: A named SQL parameter passed to the statement (`:name` markers in the SQL).

name.description: Parameter name (the `:name` marker in the SQL, without the colon).

value.description:
Parameter value. Sent to Databricks as its string form; `null` binds a
typed NULL.

type.description:
Optional Databricks SQL type (e.g. `INT`, `STRING`, `DATE`, `TIMESTAMP`).
When omitted, Databricks treats the value as `STRING`.

DatabricksReplication.description:
How the source replicates rows across runs.

Serializes as `{ type: full }` or
`{ type: incremental, column: "...", initial_value: ... }`.

oneOf.description: Every run fetches the full result set (default).

Only rows whose `column` is strictly greater than the stored bookmark
(or `initial_value` on the first run) are emitted. If the SQL contains
the literal token `${bookmark}`, it is bound as a `:_faucet_bookmark`
named parameter so the warehouse filters server-side (efficient); the
source also filters client-side as a correctness backstop. The new
maximum of `column` is persisted on the final page.

column.description: Column whose value is the replication cursor (e.g. `updated_at`).

initial_value.description: Lower bound used on the first run, before any bookmark is stored.

connectors.name: delta
connectors.title: Delta Lake
connectors.description: Apache Delta Lake source (local FS or S3/Azure/GCS; time travel, projection)

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: table_uri
config_fields.description:
Delta table location URI: `file:///abs/path`, `s3://bucket/key`,
`abfss://…`, `gs://bucket/key`. A bare local path is accepted and
treated as `file://`.

config_fields.name: credentials
config_fields.description: Object-store credentials. Defaults to the ambient provider chain.

config_fields.name: storage_options
config_fields.description:
Extra `storage_options` passed verbatim to delta-rs (e.g. a MinIO
endpoint override, or any object-store key the [`DeltaCredentials`]
enum does not model). Keys set here **win** over credential-derived
keys.

config_fields.name: version
config_fields.description:
Time travel: read the table as of this version. Mutually exclusive with
`timestamp`.

config_fields.name: timestamp
config_fields.description:
Time travel: read the table as of this RFC 3339 timestamp. Mutually
exclusive with `version`.

config_fields.name: columns
config_fields.description: Projection pushdown: only read these columns. Empty = all columns.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Page size hint for [`stream_pages`](faucet_core::Source::stream_pages).
Governs how many rows accumulate before a `StreamPage` is emitted; the
underlying parquet row-group size still bounds each read. `0` is the
"no batching" sentinel — one page per file.

config_schema.title: DeltaSourceConfig
config_schema.description:
Configuration for the Delta Lake source connector.

The `table_uri` / `credentials` / `storage_options` keys are flattened in
from the shared [`DeltaConnection`]. Reads scan the table's active data
files at the latest version (or a pinned `version` / `timestamp` for time
travel) and yield each row as a JSON object.

table_uri.description:
Delta table location URI: `file:///abs/path`, `s3://bucket/key`,
`abfss://…`, `gs://bucket/key`. A bare local path is accepted and
treated as `file://`.

credentials.description: Object-store credentials. Defaults to the ambient provider chain.

storage_options.description:
Extra `storage_options` passed verbatim to delta-rs (e.g. a MinIO
endpoint override, or any object-store key the [`DeltaCredentials`]
enum does not model). Keys set here **win** over credential-derived
keys.

version.description:
Time travel: read the table as of this version. Mutually exclusive with
`timestamp`.

timestamp.description:
Time travel: read the table as of this RFC 3339 timestamp. Mutually
exclusive with `version`.

columns.description: Projection pushdown: only read these columns. Empty = all columns.

batch_size.description:
Page size hint for [`stream_pages`](faucet_core::Source::stream_pages).
Governs how many rows accumulate before a `StreamPage` is emitted; the
underlying parquet row-group size still bounds each read. `0` is the
"no batching" sentinel — one page per file.

DeltaCredentials.description:
Object-store credentials for reading/writing a Delta table.

Uses the project-wide adjacently-tagged `{ type, config }` shape
(snake_case discriminators): e.g. `credentials: { type: aws, config: { … } }`.
The default is [`DeltaCredentials::Default`], which resolves credentials from
the ambient environment / instance metadata via the object-store default
provider chain — nothing is injected into `storage_options`.

oneOf.description:
Resolve credentials from the ambient environment / default provider
chain (AWS instance profile, `AZURE_*` env, GCP ADC, …). Injects no
keys of its own.
Static AWS credentials (or an S3-compatible endpoint such as MinIO).
Azure Blob / ADLS Gen2 credentials.
Google Cloud Storage credentials.

AwsCredentials.description:
Static AWS credentials and optional S3-compatible endpoint overrides.

Leaving a field unset lets the object-store default chain resolve it (so
`region` alone with an instance profile is valid). `endpoint_url` +
`allow_http: true` targets MinIO / LocalStack.

allow_http.description: `AWS_ALLOW_HTTP` — permit plaintext HTTP to the endpoint (MinIO in dev).

service_account_path.description: `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` — path to a service-account JSON key file.

source:
  type: delta
  config:
    table_uri: ""    # REQUIRED — Delta table location URI: `file:///abs/path`, `s3://bucket/key`, `abfss://…`, `gs://bucket/key`.
    # credentials: { type: default }    # one of: default, aws, azure, gcp
      # --- Alternative variants — replace the block above with one of these ---
      # type: aws
      # config:
        # access_key_id: ""
        # secret_access_key: ""
        # session_token: ""
        # region: ""
        # endpoint_url: ""
        # allow_http: false
      #
      # type: azure
      # config:
        # account_name: ""
        # access_key: ""
        # sas_token: ""
      #
      # type: gcp
      # config:
        # service_account_path: ""
        # service_account_key: ""
    # storage_options: {}    # Extra `storage_options` passed verbatim to delta-rs (e.g.
    # version: 0    # Time travel: read the table as of this version.
    # timestamp: ""    # Time travel: read the table as of this RFC 3339 timestamp.
    # columns: []    # Projection pushdown: only read these columns.
    # batch_size: 1000    # Page size hint for [`stream_pages`](faucet_core::Source::stream_pages).

database. A `duckdb://` / `duckdb:` scheme prefix is accepted and
stripped.

Open the database read-only. Defaults to `false` (read-write).

config_fields.description: Base URL of the Elasticsearch cluster (e.g. `"http://localhost:9200"`).

config_fields.description: Elasticsearch query DSL. Defaults to `{"match_all": {}}`.

config_fields.description: Scroll context timeout (e.g. `"1m"`). Defaults to `"1m"`.

pointer to a shared provider in the CLI's top-level `auth:` catalog.

config_fields.name: max_pages
config_fields.description: Maximum number of scroll pages to fetch. `None` means no limit.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage), which is
also the `size` parameter passed to the Elasticsearch scroll API
(`POST /{index}/_search?scroll={timeout}&size={batch_size}`). Each
scroll response becomes exactly one `StreamPage`. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the source issues a
single non-scroll `_search` request with `size = 10_000` (the default
`index.max_result_window`) and emits one `StreamPage`. Use it for
small indices or for sinks (e.g. SQL `COPY`, BigQuery load jobs) that
prefer one large request to many small ones. Indices that have raised
their `max_result_window` will still cap at 10_000 — raise this knob
or switch back to scroll if you need more.

connectors.description: Local file source; path/dir/glob/URL, every file format incl. Avro/ORC/Parquet, incremental by mtime or name

dimensions.name: Config schema

dimensions.name: Documented

config_fields.name: path
config_fields.description:
A file, a directory, a glob (`data/**/*.jsonl`), or one `http://` /
`https://` URL. A directory lists its regular files (descending into
subdirectories with `recursive: true`); every listing is sorted by path.

config_fields.name: format
config_fields.description:
File format, `auto` (by extension, per file) by default. Under `auto`
a file with no recognised extension is skipped with a warning, or
refused when `strict: true`. JSON Lines, Avro, ORC and Parquet stream;
JSON arrays, CSV, XML and Excel are read whole per file.

config_fields.name: compression
config_fields.description:
Compression codec. `auto` (default) resolves per file from its suffix
(`.gz`, `.zst`).

config_fields.name: recursive
config_fields.description: Descend into subdirectories when `path` is a directory.

config_fields.name: concurrency
config_fields.description:
Files opened ahead of the one being decoded (ordered prefetch). `0`
reads serially.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description: Records per emitted page. `0` emits one page per file.

config_fields.name: incremental
config_fields.description:
Read only files that are new since the previous run. Needs a
pipeline `state:` block; the bookmark is kept under `file:<path>`.

config_fields.name: stable_for_secs
config_fields.description:
Skip files modified less than this many seconds ago — files still
being written. They are read by a later run once they settle.

config_fields.name: strict
config_fields.description:
Refuse (instead of skipping with a warning) a file whose extension
names no format under `format: auto`.

config_fields.name: max_files
config_fields.description: Read at most this many files (after sorting and filtering).

config_fields.name: headers
config_fields.description: Request headers for an `http(s)://` path (e.g. `Authorization`).

config_fields.name: http_retries
config_fields.description:
Retries for a failed HTTP request (connection error, 429, 5xx), with
exponential backoff that honours `Retry-After`.

config_fields.name: csv
config_fields.description: CSV dialect, used for CSV files.

config_fields.name: excel
config_fields.description: Worksheet selection, used for Excel files.

config_fields.name: xml
config_fields.description: Record framing, used for XML files.

config_fields.name: avro
config_fields.description: Reader schema, used for Avro files.

config_fields.name: orc
config_fields.description: Column projection, used for ORC files.

config_fields.name: parquet
config_fields.description: Column projection, used for Parquet files.

config_fields.name: encryption
config_fields.description:
Decrypt files sealed by the file or jsonl sink's `encryption` block
(AES-256-GCM). An encrypted file is read into memory whole: JSON Lines
and raw text written line by line are then opened one line at a time,
every other file as one sealed body. A file that is not sealed fails
the read.

config_schema.description:
Configuration for the local (and `http(s)://`) file source.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

path.description:
A file, a directory, a glob (`data/**/*.jsonl`), or one `http://` /
`https://` URL. A directory lists its regular files (descending into
subdirectories with `recursive: true`); every listing is sorted by path.

File format, `auto` (by extension, per file) by default. Under `auto`
a file with no recognised extension is skipped with a warning, or
refused when `strict: true`. JSON Lines, Avro, ORC and Parquet stream;
JSON arrays, CSV, XML and Excel are read whole per file.

Compression codec. `auto` (default) resolves per file from its suffix
(`.gz`, `.zst`).

recursive.description: Descend into subdirectories when `path` is a directory.

concurrency.description:
Files opened ahead of the one being decoded (ordered prefetch). `0`
reads serially.

batch_size.description: Records per emitted page. `0` emits one page per file.

incremental.description:
Read only files that are new since the previous run. Needs a
pipeline `state:` block; the bookmark is kept under `file:<path>`.

stable_for_secs.description:
Skip files modified less than this many seconds ago — files still
being written. They are read by a later run once they settle.

strict.description:
Refuse (instead of skipping with a warning) a file whose extension
names no format under `format: auto`.

max_files.description: Read at most this many files (after sorting and filtering).

http_retries.description:
Retries for a failed HTTP request (connection error, 429, 5xx), with
exponential backoff that honours `Retry-After`.

csv.description: CSV dialect, used for CSV files.

excel.description: Worksheet selection, used for Excel files.

xml.description: Record framing, used for XML files.

avro.description: Reader schema, used for Avro files.

orc.description: Column projection, used for ORC files.

parquet.description: Column projection, used for Parquet files.

encryption.description:
Decrypt files sealed by the file or jsonl sink's `encryption` block
(AES-256-GCM). An encrypted file is read into memory whole: JSON Lines
and raw text written line by line are then opened one line at a time,
every other file as one sealed body. A file that is not sealed fails
the read.

FileFormatChoice.description: Which format a file is in: resolved from its extension (`auto`) or fixed.

oneOf.description:
Resolve per file from its extension, looking through a compression
suffix (`.csv.gz` is CSV): `.jsonl`/`.ndjson`, `.json`, `.csv`, `.xml`,
`.xlsx`, `.parquet`, `.avro`, `.orc`, `.txt`.
One JSON value per line.
A JSON array (a lone object is one record).
Delimited text; dialect from `csv`.
XML; record framing from `xml`.
An Excel workbook; sheet from `excel`.
Apache Parquet.
Unparsed text, one record per file.
Apache Avro Object Container File; schema and codec from `avro`.
Apache ORC (read-only); projection from `orc`.
Detect from filename suffix: `.gz` → Gzip, `.zst` → Zstd, anything else → None.

IncrementalSpec.description: Incremental mode: re-runs pick up only new files.

IncrementalBy.description: What makes a file "new" in incremental mode.

oneOf.description:
Modification time: a run reads files modified after the newest one the
previous run read (ties broken by path), so a rewritten file is read
again. Over HTTP the `Last-Modified` header is the modification time.

Name: a run reads files whose path sorts after the last one read —
the right choice for dated names (`export-2026-09-27.csv`) that are
never rewritten.

delimiter.description: Field separator. A single character; `"\t"` is accepted for tabs.

has_headers.description:
Whether the first row names the fields. When false, fields are named
`column_0`, `column_1`, … — the same fallback the REST source and the
`csv` connector already use. On write it decides whether a header row
is written.

quote.description: Quote character. A single byte; default `"`.

flexible.description:
Whether rows may have a different number of fields than the header.
`false` fails the read on the first ragged row, naming its line; `true`
keeps the fields the row has. Unset, each connector picks: the `file`
source is strict, the object-store sources and the REST source are
lenient.

null_values.description: Cell values read as `null` instead of a string (e.g. `["", "NULL"]`).

on_unknown_field.description:
What a streaming CSV writer does with a field the header does not
have. See [`CsvUnknownField`]. Whole-object encoders always write the
union of every record's fields, so it only affects the `file` sink.

CsvUnknownField.description: What a CSV writer does with a field that is not in the header.

oneOf.description: Add it as a new column; earlier rows get an empty cell for it.

Fix the header from the first page and drop the field, logging a
warning once per field.
Fix the header from the first page and fail the write naming the field.

sheet.description: Worksheet name, or an index as a string. Default: the first sheet.

XmlOptions.description:
XML record framing.

XML has no canonical record boundary, so one must be declared. On read,
`record_element` names the repeated element; without it the decoder falls
back to "the document's root children", which is right for the common
`<rows><row/>…</rows>` shape and wrong often enough that naming the element
is recommended in the docs.

record_element.description:
Element that delimits one record. Read: select these. Write: wrap each
record in one.

root_element.description: Document element wrapping the records. Write only.

schema.description:
An Avro schema (the JSON form: an object, an array for a union, or a
primitive name). On a **source** it is the *reader* schema every file
is resolved against — projection, aliases, defaults for added fields.
On a **sink** it is the *writer* schema; without it the schema is
inferred from the records.

codec.description:
Block codec for written files: `null` (default), `deflate`, `snappy`,
`zstd`. Reading detects the codec from the file header.

oneOf.description: Uncompressed blocks — the Avro default and the most portable.
Raw deflate (RFC 1951), readable by every Avro implementation.
Snappy with the per-block CRC-32 the spec requires.
Zstandard.

columns.description:
Top-level columns to read, in file order. Default: every column. A
name the file does not have is an error, not an empty column.

ParquetReadOptions.description: Parquet reader options (the `parquet:` block of an object-store source).

columns.description:
Decode only these top-level columns. A name missing from an object is
an error naming the object and its columns. Unset: every column.

EncryptionSpec.description:
The user-facing `encryption:` config block (state store / jsonl sink).

```yaml
encryption:
  key: ${vault:secret/faucet#state-key}
  # previous_keys: ["${env:OLD_STATE_KEY}"]   # rotation: read-only
  # algorithm: aes-256-gcm                     # default
```

key.description:
Key material used to seal new writes (and tried first on reads).
Should come from a secrets manager; derived to a 32-byte AES key via
SHA-256.

previous_keys.description:
Older keys tried (in order) when decrypting, for rotation. Never used
to seal new writes.

EncryptionAlgorithm.description:
Supported AEAD algorithms. A single variant today; the format byte in the
on-disk header leaves room for more without breaking old files.

oneOf.description: AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption (the default and only option).

dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: bucket
config_fields.description: GCS bucket name.

config_fields.name: prefix
config_fields.description: Object name prefix filter. Ignored when `object_keys` is set.

config_fields.name: object_keys
config_fields.description:
Explicit object names. When set, listing is skipped and `prefix`
is ignored.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description: Credential source.

config_fields.name: file_format
config_fields.description: File format.

config_fields.name: max_objects
config_fields.description: Hard cap on the number of objects read (after listing).

config_fields.name: concurrency
config_fields.description: Maximum concurrent object reads (default: 10).

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted `StreamPage`. See "Streaming and batching"
in the README. `batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel and
emits one page per object.

config_fields.name: verify_length
config_fields.description:
Verify each object's byte length against the length the store
advertises, failing the read with
[`FaucetError::Source`](faucet_core::FaucetError::Source) on a short
(truncated) or over-long transfer (#161). Cheap — a byte counter over
a body that is read anyway — so it defaults to `true`.

Skipped (with a debug log, not a failure) when the store advertises no
length, or when it reports a non-empty `Content-Encoding`: the body on
the wire is then transcoded and its length legitimately differs from
the stored object's.

config_fields.name: verify_checksum
config_fields.description:
Verify each object's body against the checksum the store advertises
(#161). Stronger than the length check but costs a hash over the full
body, so it defaults to `false`. When the store advertises no usable
checksum for an object, verification is skipped for that object (a
debug log notes it); the length check still applies.

config_fields.name: storage_host
config_fields.description:
Optional storage-host override (e.g. `http://localhost:4443` for
fake-gcs-server). Production users should leave this unset.

config_fields.name: compression
config_fields.description:
Compression codec applied to each downloaded object. Defaults to
[`CompressionConfig::Auto`](faucet_core::CompressionConfig::Auto) —
the codec is resolved per-object-key, so a single source can read a
mix of compressed and uncompressed objects. Requires the
crate-local `compression` feature.

config_fields.name: csv
config_fields.description: CSV dialect, used when `file_format: csv` (#604).

config_fields.name: excel
config_fields.description: Worksheet selection, used when `file_format: xlsx` (#604).

config_fields.name: xml
config_fields.description: Record framing, used when `file_format: xml` (#604).

config_fields.name: avro
config_fields.description: Reader schema, used when `file_format: avro` (#719).

config_fields.name: orc
config_fields.description: Column projection, used when `file_format: orc` (#719).

config_fields.name: parquet
config_fields.description:
Column projection, used when `file_format: parquet` (#777): only
`parquet.columns` are decoded, before any row group is read.

config_schema.description: Configuration for the GCS source connector.

Column projection, used when `file_format: parquet` (#777): only

GcsCredentials.description:
Credential source for a GCS client.

Serializes as `{ type: <method>, config: { … } }` (adjacent tagging,
snake_case discriminators) — the consistent auth wire shape shared by
every faucet connector:
`{ type: service_account_json_file, config: { path: "/run/secrets/sa.json" } }`.

oneOf.description: Path to a service-account JSON key file on disk.

Service-account JSON key as an inline string. Useful for
environment-variable injection via `${env:GCP_SA_JSON}` in CLI
configs.

Application Default Credentials — honours
`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, gcloud user creds, and the
GCE/GKE metadata server, in that order.

Anonymous credentials. Use this with emulators (e.g.
`fake-gcs-server`) that do not validate bearer tokens — the SDK
otherwise tries to fetch ADC tokens at request time and fails in
environments without GCP credentials.

GcsFileFormat.description: Format of files stored in GCS.

oneOf.description: Each line in the file is a separate JSON record.
The entire file is a JSON array of records.
Each file becomes a single record with `"key"` and `"content"` fields.

Apache Parquet objects. Decoded via the Arrow Parquet reader; the
resulting `RecordBatch`es feed both the row path (converted to JSON)
and the **columnar** fast path
([`Source::stream_batches`](faucet_core::Source::stream_batches)) so a
`gcs(parquet) → parquet`/`delta` chain never materializes
`serde_json::Value`. Requires the crate-local `arrow` feature
(RFC 0002 / #375).

Delimited text, decoded through [`faucet_core::file_format`] so the
records match what every other connector produces for the same file.
Dialect from [`csv`](GcsSourceConfig::csv). Requires
`file-format-csv` (#604).

XML, decoded to the compact element→object mapping. The repeated
element is named by [`xml`](GcsSourceConfig::xml). Requires
`file-format-xml` (#604).

An Excel workbook. Sheet and header row from
[`excel`](GcsSourceConfig::excel). **Buffered whole** — a workbook is a
zip container whose directory sits at the end. Requires
`file-format-excel` (#604).

Apache Avro Object Container Files. Each file's embedded writer
schema is resolved against [`avro.schema`](GcsSourceConfig::avro) when
set, else against the first object's schema, so the prefix reads as one
shape. Joins the columnar path with the `arrow` feature. Requires
`file-format-avro` (#719).

Apache ORC, projected by [`orc.columns`](GcsSourceConfig::orc).
**Buffered whole** (the footer sits at the end) and decoded stripe by
stripe; joins the columnar path. Requires `file-format-orc` (#719).
Detect from filename suffix: `.gz` → Gzip, `.zst` → Zstd, anything else → None.

delimiter.description: Field separator. A single character; `"\t"` is accepted for tabs.

has_headers.description:
Whether the first row names the fields. When false, fields are named
`column_0`, `column_1`, … — the same fallback the REST source and the
`csv` connector already use. On write it decides whether a header row
is written.

quote.description: Quote character. A single byte; default `"`.

flexible.description:
Whether rows may have a different number of fields than the header.
`false` fails the read on the first ragged row, naming its line; `true`
keeps the fields the row has. Unset, each connector picks: the `file`
source is strict, the object-store sources and the REST source are
lenient.

null_values.description: Cell values read as `null` instead of a string (e.g. `["", "NULL"]`).

on_unknown_field.description:
What a streaming CSV writer does with a field the header does not
have. See [`CsvUnknownField`]. Whole-object encoders always write the
union of every record's fields, so it only affects the `file` sink.

CsvUnknownField.description: What a CSV writer does with a field that is not in the header.

oneOf.description: Add it as a new column; earlier rows get an empty cell for it.

Fix the header from the first page and drop the field, logging a
warning once per field.
Fix the header from the first page and fail the write naming the field.

sheet.description: Worksheet name, or an index as a string. Default: the first sheet.

XmlOptions.description:
XML record framing.

XML has no canonical record boundary, so one must be declared. On read,
`record_element` names the repeated element; without it the decoder falls
back to "the document's root children", which is right for the common
`<rows><row/>…</rows>` shape and wrong often enough that naming the element
is recommended in the docs.

record_element.description:
Element that delimits one record. Read: select these. Write: wrap each
record in one.

root_element.description: Document element wrapping the records. Write only.

schema.description:
An Avro schema (the JSON form: an object, an array for a union, or a
primitive name). On a **source** it is the *reader* schema every file
is resolved against — projection, aliases, defaults for added fields.
On a **sink** it is the *writer* schema; without it the schema is
inferred from the records.

codec.description:
Block codec for written files: `null` (default), `deflate`, `snappy`,
`zstd`. Reading detects the codec from the file header.

oneOf.description: Uncompressed blocks — the Avro default and the most portable.
Raw deflate (RFC 1951), readable by every Avro implementation.
Snappy with the per-block CRC-32 the spec requires.
Zstandard.

columns.description:
Top-level columns to read, in file order. Default: every column. A
name the file does not have is an error, not an empty column.

ParquetReadOptions.description: Parquet reader options (the `parquet:` block of an object-store source).

columns.description:
Decode only these top-level columns. A name missing from an object is
an error naming the object and its columns. Unset: every column.

connectors.name: graphql
connectors.title: GraphQL
connectors.description: GraphQL API source with cursor pagination

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: endpoint
config_fields.description: GraphQL endpoint URL.

config_fields.name: query
config_fields.description: The GraphQL query string.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description:
Authentication: either inline (`{ type, config }`) or a `{ ref: <name> }`
pointer to a shared provider in the CLI's top-level `auth:` catalog.

config_fields.name: variables
config_fields.description: Variables to pass with the query. Defaults to an empty object.

config_fields.name: records_path
config_fields.description: JSONPath expression to extract records from the response.

config_fields.name: pagination
config_fields.description:
Pagination configuration. `None` for single-page queries. Accepts either
the Relay cursor block (no `type:`) or an offset block (`type: Offset`) —
see [`GraphqlPaginationSpec`].

config_fields.name: max_pages
config_fields.description: Maximum number of pages to fetch.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage), and the
value injected as the GraphQL `first:` cursor argument (or whatever
variable name [`GraphqlPagination::page_size_variable`] specifies).
Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the page-size variable
is omitted from the request so the upstream uses its own default page
size, and the entire result set is emitted as a single page. If the
upstream schema requires a non-null `first:` argument this will
surface as `FaucetError::Config` at stream-time.

config_fields.name: tls
config_fields.description:
Optional client-certificate (mutual TLS) config. When set, the source
presents a client certificate on every request (data + inline auth token
request). Requires the crate's `mtls` feature.

config_fields.name: replication_method
config_fields.description:
`full_table` (default) re-reads everything each run; `incremental`
filters on [`replication_key`](Self::replication_key) and emits a
bookmark on the final page so the next run resumes (#751).

config_fields.name: replication_key
config_fields.description:
Field used for incremental replication bookmarking: a top-level field
(`updatedAt`), a dot path into nested objects (`node.updatedAt`), or a
JSON Pointer (`/node/updatedAt`). Must resolve to one value per record.

config_fields.name: on_missing_key
config_fields.description:
What to do with a record whose `replication_key` is missing or `null`
once a start bookmark exists: `keep` (default), `drop`, or `fail`.

config_fields.name: start_replication_value
config_fields.description:
Initial bookmark used when no stored bookmark exists: records whose
`replication_key` is not greater than it are filtered out, and a
`replication_bind` renders it into the request.

config_fields.name: state_key
config_fields.description:
Identifier the pipeline persists this stream's bookmark under. Derived
from the endpoint when unset and replicating incrementally.

config_fields.name: replication_bind
config_fields.description:
Bind the bookmark into a GraphQL variable (see [`GraphqlReplicationBind`]).
Requires `replication_method: incremental` + `replication_key`.

config_fields.name: retry_on_response
config_fields.description:
Responses to treat as throttling and retry — including a `200` whose
body reports it (`match_success: true` with
`body_path: "$.errors[*].extensions.code"`, `values: [THROTTLED]`). A
rule's `backoff_from` reads the wait from the response (`cost_bucket`
for a leaky-bucket cost report, or a reset header / body value).
Checked before the response's `errors[]` are classified; a match
retries the whole request, so partial `data` is never emitted.
