AuthSpec.description:
A connector's `auth:` field: **either** an inline auth definition `A`
(the `{ type, config }` shape), **or** a `{ ref: <name> }` reference to a
shared provider defined in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

`ref` is mutually exclusive with inline fields — supplying both is a
deserialization error.

anyOf.description: Inline auth, spelled out on the connector.
A reference to a shared provider in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

oneOf.description: No authentication.
Bearer token in the Authorization header.
Custom headers (e.g. API keys, cookies).

AuthReference.description:
A `{ ref: <name> }` pointer to a named provider in the top-level `auth:`
catalog. The only permitted key is `ref`.

ref.description: Name of the provider in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

GraphqlPaginationSpec.description:
Pagination style for the GraphQL source.

Deserialized **untagged** so the legacy cursor block (which carries no
`type:` discriminator) keeps working unchanged, while the offset block is
selected by its required `type: Offset` field. The two field sets are
disjoint (cursor requires `cursor_path` / `has_next_page_path`; offset
requires `type` / `offset_variable` / `page_size`), so serde routes each
config to exactly one variant. The cursor variant is tried first.

anyOf.description: Relay-style cursor pagination (the original, `type`-less shape).
Offset-into-variable pagination — selected by `type: Offset`.

GraphqlPagination.description:
Cursor-based pagination configuration for GraphQL.

Most GraphQL APIs use the Relay cursor specification with
`pageInfo { hasNextPage, endCursor }`.

has_next_page_path.description: JSONPath to the `hasNextPage` boolean in the response.

cursor_path.description: JSONPath to the `endCursor` string in the response.

cursor_variable.description: Name of the cursor variable in the GraphQL query (default: `"after"`).

page_size_variable.description:
Name of the page size variable (default: `"first"`).

The per-page record count itself comes from
[`GraphqlStreamConfig::batch_size`] — the variable named here is the
GraphQL variable that the `batch_size` value is injected into on each
request. The plain `batch_size = 0` sentinel omits the variable so the
upstream uses its own default page size.

GraphqlOffsetPagination.description:
Offset-into-query-variable pagination (query languages that embed `LIMIT … OFFSET …`).

Increments an integer offset injected into a GraphQL variable and
terminates on a **short page** (fewer than `page_size` records) — unlike
cursor pagination, which follows a `pageInfo` boolean. Suited to APIs whose
query language embeds `LIMIT … OFFSET …`: bake the limit
into the query string and parameterize only the offset with `${…}`.

The offset starts at `0`, is sent as a JSON number in the `variables` map on
every request, and advances by `page_size` after each page.

offset_variable.description:
Name of the GraphQL variable that receives the current offset. It is
injected as a JSON number (starting at `0`, incremented by `page_size`
after each page). Reference it from the query string or as a variable
(e.g. `${q_offset}` inside the query string).

page_size.description:
Records requested per page. Used both to advance the offset
(`offset += page_size`) and, with `stop_when_short`, to detect the final
page. Must be greater than `0`. This value is **not** injected into the
request — bake the limit into your query (`LIMIT 250 OFFSET ${q_offset}`).

stop_when_short.description:
Terminate when a page yields fewer than `page_size` records (default
`true`). When `false`, pagination continues until a fully empty page (or
`max_pages`) is reached.

substitute_in_query.description:
Substitute `${offset_variable}` occurrences in the **query string** with
the current offset before each request, instead of sending it as a
GraphQL variable. Required for query languages that embed the offset in a
string-literal argument — e.g.
`reportQuery(query: "… LIMIT 250 OFFSET ${q_offset}")`, where a GraphQL
variable cannot interpolate into a string literal (#569). Default
`false` (variable injection, the #550 behavior).

OffsetPaginationKind.description:
Discriminator for [`GraphqlOffsetPagination`]; serializes as `"Offset"`.

A dedicated single-variant enum (rather than a bare `String`) so the
`type: Offset` marker is validated at config-load time and gives the
untagged [`GraphqlPaginationSpec`] a reliable way to route an offset block.

oneOf.description: The offset pagination style.

TlsClientConfig.description:
Client-certificate (mutual TLS) configuration for the HTTP sources.

Supply **either** a PEM certificate + key pair (`client_cert` + `client_key`)
**or** a PKCS#12 identity file (`client_identity_pkcs12` [+ `pkcs12_password`]).
PEM values may be inline or pulled in with `${file:…}` / `${secret:…}` /
`${vault:…}`; the PKCS#12 value is a path to a `.p12`/`.pfx` file (its binary
content can't be embedded in a text config).

client_cert.description: PEM-encoded client certificate chain. Pair with `client_key`.

client_key.description: PEM-encoded PKCS#8 private key. Pair with `client_cert`.

client_identity_pkcs12.description:
Path to a PKCS#12 (`.p12`/`.pfx`) identity file — an alternative to the
PEM pair.

pkcs12_password.description: Password for the PKCS#12 file (omit or empty if the file is unencrypted).

min_version.description:
Minimum negotiated TLS version: `"1.2"` or `"1.3"`. Defaults to the
TLS backend's own minimum when unset.

ReplicationMethod.description: Determines how records are replicated from the source.

oneOf.description: All records are fetched on every run (default).

Only records where the `replication_key` field is strictly greater than
the stored bookmark (`start_replication_value`) are kept.

OnMissingKey.description: What to do with a record whose replication key is missing or `null` (#747).

oneOf.description:
Keep the record, count it, and warn (default): dropping it would be
silent data loss.
Drop the record (counted and warned, never silent).
Fail the run.

GraphqlReplicationBind.description:
Binds the stored bookmark into a GraphQL **variable** (#751), so the server
returns only newer records. The client-side `replication_key` filter stays
active as a safety net.

```yaml
replication_bind:
  variable: since                    # or a JSON Pointer: /filter/updatedAt/gte
  template: "updated_at:>${bookmark}"
  format: iso8601
```

variable.description:
The variable to set: a top-level variable name (`since`), or an RFC 6901
JSON Pointer into `variables` (`/filter/updatedAt/gte`) that resolves to
an existing value or to a new key of an existing object.

template.description:
Template rendered with `${bookmark}` replaced by the formatted bookmark.
Defaults to the bare `${bookmark}`. When the bookmark sits inside a
query-language string filter (`query: "updated_at:>…"`), escaping is
the template author's job.

format.description: How to format the bookmark before substitution.

value_type.description: JSON type of the variable: `string` (default) or `number`.

BindFormat.description:
How the bookmark value is formatted before it is substituted into the
[`ReplicationBind::template`].

For every non-[`Raw`](BindFormat::Raw) format the bookmark is first parsed
into an instant: a string is read as RFC 3339, a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` date
(midnight UTC), or a naive `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` (assumed UTC); a JSON
number is read as **epoch seconds**. It is then re-emitted in the target
representation, so `epoch_ms` ← ISO string and `iso8601` ← epoch number both
work.

oneOf.description:
Emit the scalar verbatim (string as-is, number as its decimal form).
The default; no timestamp parsing.
Unix epoch **seconds** (integer).
Unix epoch **milliseconds** (integer).
Calendar date `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC).

BindValueType.description: The JSON type a body-target bind writes (#748).

oneOf.description: A JSON string (default).
A JSON number (e.g. an `epoch_ms` bookmark an API requires unquoted).

RetryMatcher.description:
One `retry_on_response` rule: a response that matches every set condition
is treated as throttling.

status.description:
HTTP statuses this rule applies to (empty = any non-2xx, or any status
with `match_success`).

match_success.description:
Also match 2xx responses, for APIs that report throttling inside a
successful response (GraphQL `THROTTLED` errors, `x-ratelimit-remaining:
0`). Requires `body_path` or `header`.

body_path.description:
JSONPath into the (JSON) response body; any match equal to one of
`values` satisfies the rule. A non-JSON body never matches.

values.description:
Values that match (numbers and strings compare by their text, so `17`
matches `"17"`). Required with `body_path`; with only `header`, they
are compared against the header value.

header.description:
A response header that must be present (and, without `body_path`,
equal one of `values` when any are listed).

backoff_from.description:
Where the response says how long to wait. Takes precedence over
`backoff_secs`; when the value is missing or unreadable the rule falls
back to `backoff_secs`, then `Retry-After`, then exponential backoff.

backoff_secs.description:
Fixed wait before retrying. Without it the server's `Retry-After` is
honoured, else exponential backoff applies.

max_wait_secs.description:
Longest wait `backoff_from` may ask for (default 3600). A longer one
fails the run with an error naming the reset instead of parking it.

BackoffFrom.description: Where a matched response states its wait.

oneOf.description: A response header (`x-ratelimit-reset`).

name.description: Header name.

oneOf.description:
A JSON-valued response header, read at a JSONPath
(a usage header carrying a JSON object).

name.description: Header name.

path.description:
JSONPath into the parsed header value; the first number or string
found is used.

oneOf.description: A value in the JSON response body.

path.description: JSONPath into the body; the first number or string found is used.

oneOf.description:
A leaky-bucket cost report (a GraphQL cost extension): wait
`ceil((requested - available) / restore_rate)` seconds, at least 1.

requested.description: JSONPath to the cost the request asked for.

available.description: JSONPath to the points currently available.

restore_rate.description: JSONPath to the points restored per second.

oneOf.description: A wait in seconds.
A wait in milliseconds.
A wait in minutes.
An absolute Unix time in seconds.
An absolute Unix time in milliseconds.
An absolute RFC 3339 instant.

    auth:

    # tls: null    # Optional client-certificate (mutual TLS) config.
    # replication_method: { type: FullTable }    # one of: FullTable, Incremental

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: endpoint
config_fields.description: gRPC endpoint URL (e.g. `"http://localhost:50051"`).

config_fields.name: service_name
config_fields.description: Fully qualified service name (e.g. `"mypackage.MyService"`).

config_fields.name: method_name
config_fields.description: Method name (e.g. `"ListUsers"`).

config_fields.name: request
config_fields.description:
Request message as JSON. Fields are mapped to protobuf fields
using the `FileDescriptorSet`.

config_fields.name: descriptor_set_path
config_fields.description: Path to the compiled `FileDescriptorSet` file.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description:
Authentication: either inline (`{ type, config }`) or a `{ ref: <name> }`
pointer to a shared provider in the CLI's top-level `auth:` catalog.

config_fields.name: tls
config_fields.description: Whether to use TLS (detected from `https://` in endpoint by default).

config_fields.name: records_path
config_fields.description:
JSONPath to extract records from the response.
If not set, the entire response is returned as a single record.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). Defaults
to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

For unary RPCs the source has no native paging primitive to honour
this hint: the default
[`Source::stream_pages`](faucet_core::Source::stream_pages) impl
buffers the full response and then chunks it in memory, bounding
**sink-side** memory only.

For server-streaming RPCs (`rpc_kind = "server_streaming"`) the source
overrides `stream_pages` and flushes a page each time `batch_size`
messages accumulate, bounding both source-side and sink-side memory.
`batch_size = 0` drains the entire stream into a single page.

config_fields.name: rpc_kind
config_fields.description: Kind of RPC to invoke. Defaults to [`RpcKind::Unary`].

config_fields.name: max_messages
config_fields.description:
For [`RpcKind::ServerStreaming`]: maximum number of messages to consume
before terminating the stream. `None` means consume until the server
closes the stream (or the run is cancelled).

config_fields.name: terminate_on_error
config_fields.description:
For [`RpcKind::ServerStreaming`]: if `true`, transient stream errors
(server-side disconnects, transport errors, etc.) terminate the run
with [`FaucetError::Source`](faucet_core::FaucetError::Source). When
`false` (the default), the source reconnects with exponential backoff
up to [`reconnect_max_attempts`](Self::reconnect_max_attempts).

Ignored for [`RpcKind::Unary`].

config_fields.name: reconnect_initial_backoff
config_fields.description:
For [`RpcKind::ServerStreaming`] reconnect: initial backoff delay
before the first retry. Doubles after each failure up to
[`reconnect_max_backoff`](Self::reconnect_max_backoff). Defaults to 1s.

config_fields.name: reconnect_max_backoff
config_fields.description:
For [`RpcKind::ServerStreaming`] reconnect: maximum backoff cap.
Defaults to 30s.

config_fields.name: reconnect_max_attempts
config_fields.description:
For [`RpcKind::ServerStreaming`] reconnect: maximum reconnect attempts
before surfacing the error. `None` (the default) means unlimited
retries.

The historical WebSocket-source spelling `max_reconnect_attempts` is
accepted as an alias (#654 M20) — the prefix used to be reversed
between the two connectors, so a user who learned one spelling had the
other silently ignored and reconnected without a bound.

config_fields.name: reconnect_replay_from_start
config_fields.description:
For [`RpcKind::ServerStreaming`] reconnect: whether the server replays
the response stream from the beginning when the identical request is
re-issued after a disconnect. Defaults to `true`.

Because the request is resolved once per run, a reconnect sends the
*same* request — a stateless server therefore re-streams from message
0. When `true` the source skips the messages it already emitted before
the disconnect, so consumers see each message once. Set to `false`
only for servers that resume mid-stream on the same request (rare):
there, skipping would drop genuinely-new messages, so every received
message is emitted (at-least-once; duplicates possible).

config_fields.name: max_decoding_message_size
config_fields.description:
Maximum size, in bytes, of a single inbound (decoded) gRPC message.
`None` (the default) keeps tonic's built-in 4 MiB limit. Raise this
for sources that legitimately return large messages; a too-low limit
surfaces as a decode error and aborts the call. Applies to both unary
and server-streaming RPCs.

config_fields.name: max_encoding_message_size
config_fields.description:
Maximum size, in bytes, of a single outbound (encoded) gRPC request
message. `None` (the default) keeps tonic's built-in limit. Rarely
needs tuning for a data source, since requests are typically small.

AuthSpec.description:
A connector's `auth:` field: **either** an inline auth definition `A`
(the `{ type, config }` shape), **or** a `{ ref: <name> }` reference to a
shared provider defined in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

`ref` is mutually exclusive with inline fields — supplying both is a
deserialization error.

anyOf.description: Inline auth, spelled out on the connector.
A reference to a shared provider in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

oneOf.description: No authentication.
Bearer token sent as `authorization` metadata.
Custom metadata key-value pairs.

MetadataEntry.description:
A single piece of gRPC request metadata.

Use a `Vec<MetadataEntry>` rather than a map because gRPC allows duplicate
keys and order is occasionally observable.

key.description:
Metadata key. gRPC lowercases keys on the wire; a `-bin` suffix marks a
binary value.

value.description:

credentials rather than inlining them.

catalog. The only permitted key is `ref`.

ref.description: Name of the provider in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

RpcKind.description:

oneOf.description: One request, one response (default).

each streamed message and emits records as they arrive. Useful for
event feeds, change feeds, log tails, and any long-lived gRPC stream.

dimensions.name: Documented

config_fields.name: catalog
config_fields.description: Catalog type and connection settings.

config_fields.name: table
config_fields.description:
Table to read, as `namespace.table` (multi-level namespaces are
dot-separated: `lake.analytics.events`).

config_fields.name: columns
config_fields.description: Columns to read (projection). Empty reads every column.

config_fields.name: filter
config_fields.description:
Row filter pushed down to the scan, e.g.
`status = 'active' and (amount >= 10 or vip is not null)`.

Operators: `=`, `!=`, `<>`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `in (…)`,
`not in (…)`, `is null`, `is not null`, `starts_with`,
`not starts_with`, combined with `and` / `or` / `not` and parentheses.
Literals are numbers, `'strings'`, `true` / `false`; dates and
timestamps are written as strings and typed against the column.

config_fields.name: snapshot_id
config_fields.description:
Time travel: read this snapshot id instead of the current one.
`mode: full` only; mutually exclusive with `as_of_timestamp`.

config_fields.name: as_of_timestamp
config_fields.description:
Time travel: read the snapshot that was current at this RFC 3339
instant (e.g. `2026-01-31T00:00:00Z`). `mode: full` only.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description: Arrow batch size (rows per page). `0` emits one page per snapshot read.

config_fields.name: concurrency
config_fields.description: Data files read concurrently.

config_fields.name: mode
config_fields.description:
`full` (default) re-reads the table each run; `incremental` reads only
data appended since the bookmarked snapshot.

config_fields.name: on_rewrite
config_fields.description:
Incremental only: reaction to an `overwrite` / `delete` snapshot since
the bookmark.

config_fields.name: on_expired
config_fields.description: Incremental only: reaction to a bookmarked snapshot that has expired.

`not in (…)`, `is null`, `is not null`, `starts_with`,
`not starts_with`, combined with `and` / `or` / `not` and parentheses.
Literals are numbers, `'strings'`, `true` / `false`; dates and

CatalogConfig.description:
Iceberg catalog type and its connection settings.

Uses serde's internally-tagged enum: the JSON/YAML `type` key selects the
variant. Each variant carries the same inner fields (`uri`, `warehouse`,
`credential`, `properties`); the relevant set differs per catalog type and
is documented in each variant.

| Variant | Cargo feature required   |
|---------|--------------------------|
| `rest`  | `catalog-rest` (default) |
| `glue`  | `catalog-glue`           |
| `sql`   | `catalog-sql`            |
| `hms`   | `catalog-hms`            |

oneOf.description:
Apache Iceberg REST catalog. `uri` is the catalog endpoint; `credential`
becomes the REST bearer token.

uri.description:
Catalog endpoint URI.

For REST: `https://catalog.example.com`.
For HMS: `thrift://hms:9083`.
For SQL: the JDBC/SQLx connection string, e.g. `postgres://…`.

credential.description:
REST bearer token or other catalog-specific credential.

Redacted in `Debug` output — never logged.

properties.description:
Arbitrary catalog properties passed through to the catalog builder
(e.g. S3 region, endpoint, access key).

oneOf.description:
AWS Glue catalog. `warehouse` is the S3 root; AWS credentials are
supplied via `properties` or the default AWS credential chain.

Catalog endpoint URI.

For HMS: `thrift://hms:9083`.
For SQL: the JDBC/SQLx connection string, e.g. `postgres://…`.

credential.description:
REST bearer token or other catalog-specific credential.

Redacted in `Debug` output — never logged.

Arbitrary catalog properties passed through to the catalog builder
(e.g. S3 region, endpoint, access key).

credential.description:
REST bearer token or other catalog-specific credential.

Redacted in `Debug` output — never logged.

Arbitrary catalog properties passed through to the catalog builder
(e.g. S3 region, endpoint, access key).

Hive Metastore catalog. `uri` is the Thrift endpoint
(`thrift://hms:9083`).

properties.description:

ReadMode.description: How much of the table each run reads.

oneOf.description: Read the whole table at the selected snapshot on every run.

Read only the data files added by `append` snapshots since the
bookmarked snapshot. The first run (no bookmark) reads the current
snapshot in full; the bookmark is the last processed snapshot id.

OnRewrite.description:
What an incremental run does when a snapshot since the bookmark rewrote
existing data (`overwrite` / `delete`), or the bookmark is no longer an
ancestor of the current snapshot (a rollback).

oneOf.description: Fail the run with a message naming the snapshot.

Re-read the current snapshot in full and move the bookmark to it.
Rows already delivered are delivered again — pair with an upsert or
overwrite sink.

OnExpired.description:
What an incremental run does when the bookmarked snapshot (or one between
it and the current snapshot) has been expired from the table metadata.

oneOf.description: Fail the run with guidance.
Re-read the current snapshot in full and move the bookmark to it.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Messages per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). Messages
drained from the consumer are accumulated into an in-memory buffer and
yielded whenever the buffer reaches this size or the idle window flushes
a partially-filled buffer. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

defeats the point of streaming and exists only for tests or one-shot

config_fields.description:
Cursor batch size: documents per server round-trip on the MongoDB
driver cursor. This is a wire-level tuning knob — distinct from
[`Self::batch_size`], which controls the size of each emitted
[`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage).

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). Documents
are pulled from the cursor and yielded whenever the buffer reaches
this size. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the cursor is fully
drained and the entire result set is emitted in a single page. Useful
for small lookup tables or for sinks (e.g. SQL `COPY`, BigQuery load
jobs) that prefer one large request to many small ones.

config_schema.title: MongoSourceConfig
config_schema.description:
Configuration for the MongoDB source connector.

# Example

```
use faucet_source_mongodb::MongoSourceConfig;
use serde_json::json;

let config = MongoSourceConfig::new(
    "mongodb://localhost:27017",
    "my_database",
    "my_collection",
)
.filter(json!({"status": "active"}))
.projection(json!({"_id": 0, "name": 1, "email": 1}))
.sort(json!({"created_at": -1}))
.limit(1000)
.cursor_batch_size(200)
.with_batch_size(500);
```

Terminator: flush the buffer and end the fetch cycle after this much

unbounded. The OOM safety valve: with `batch_size: 0` (or a library
caller using `fetch_all`) the change-event buffer would otherwise grow
without bound for the whole fetch cycle and risk an OOM-kill on a
high-throughput stream. Mirrors the same field on the sibling
`postgres-cdc` / `mysql-cdc` sources.

config_fields.name: state_key
config_fields.description:
Explicit state-store key for the bookmark. When unset, a key is derived
from the connection host and a query fingerprint.

config_fields.name: shard
config_fields.description:
Optional primary-key range sharding for clustered (Mode B) execution.

When set, the source advertises itself as shardable: the cluster
coordinator splits the query's `key` range into contiguous slices that
different workers process concurrently. Has **no effect** outside the
cluster coordinator (a plain `faucet run` streams the whole query), so
it is fully backward compatible. See [`ShardConfig`].

config_schema.title: MssqlSourceConfig
config_schema.description: Configuration for [`MssqlSource`](crate::MssqlSource).

connection_string.description:
ADO.NET-style connection string handed straight to `tiberius`, e.g.
`Server=tcp:host,1433;Database=db;User Id=sa;Password=...;`. Mutually
exclusive with [`connection_url`](Self::connection_url).

tls.description: TLS / encryption settings. Defaults to [`MssqlTlsMode::Prefer`].

query.description:
SQL query to run. Use `@P1`, `@P2`, … for [`params`](Self::params), and
the literal `@bookmark` token to bind the incremental cursor server-side.

params.description: Positional bind parameters for the query (`@P1`…`@Pn`). Defaults to empty.

batch_size.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). `0` emits the
whole result set as a single page. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

statement_timeout_secs.description: Per-query timeout in seconds (`0` disables). Defaults to 300.

state_key.description:
Explicit state-store key for the bookmark. When unset, a key is derived
from the connection host and a query fingerprint.

shard.description:
Optional primary-key range sharding for clustered (Mode B) execution.

When set, the source advertises itself as shardable: the cluster
coordinator splits the query's `key` range into contiguous slices that
different workers process concurrently. Has **no effect** outside the
cluster coordinator (a plain `faucet run` streams the whole query), so
it is fully backward compatible. See [`ShardConfig`].

MssqlTls.description:
TLS configuration for an MSSQL connection.

Matches the YAML shape `tls: { type: <mode>, ca_cert_path: <path> }`.

ca_cert_path.description:
Optional path to a CA certificate (PEM/DER) to trust for server
validation. Ignored when `mode` is [`MssqlTlsMode::Disable`].

oneOf.description:
Encrypt the connection if the server supports it (the safe modern
default). Maps to `tiberius` `EncryptionLevel::On`.

Require encryption; fail if the server does not offer it. Maps to
`EncryptionLevel::Required`.

Encrypt and accept the server certificate without validating its chain
(self-signed dev servers). Maps to `EncryptionLevel::On` + `trust_cert()`.
**Insecure against MITM — never use in production.**
No transport encryption. Maps to `EncryptionLevel::NotSupported`.

MssqlReplication.description:
How the source replicates rows across runs.

Serializes as `{ type: full }` or
`{ type: incremental, column: "...", initial_value: ... }`.

oneOf.description: Every run fetches the full result set (default).

Only rows whose `column` is strictly greater than the stored bookmark
(or `initial_value` on the first run) are emitted.

The bookmark is applied two ways: if the query contains the literal
token `@bookmark`, it is bound as a parameter so the server filters
(efficient); the source *also* filters client-side as a correctness
backstop. The new maximum of `column` is persisted on the final page.

column.description: Column whose value is the replication cursor (e.g. `updated_at`).

initial_value.description: Lower bound used on the first run, before any bookmark is stored.

ShardConfig.description:
Primary-key range sharding settings for the MSSQL source.

The source is split by contiguous ranges of an **integer-typed** column:
each shard runs `SELECT * FROM (<query>) WHERE [key] >= lo AND [key] < hi`.
The column must be present in the query's output and orderable as a 64-bit
integer (e.g. a `BIGINT`/`INT` `IDENTITY` primary key).

**`ORDER BY`:** T-SQL forbids `ORDER BY` inside a derived table (without
`TOP`/`OFFSET`), so a sharded query must not end in a top-level `ORDER BY`
— ordering across concurrently-executing shards is meaningless anyway.

**Nullable keys:** if the key column contains NULLs, those rows are not
visible to the `MIN`/`MAX` range enumeration. They are still read — exactly
one shard (the last) additionally matches `[key] IS NULL`, so NULL-key rows
are covered by precisely one shard with no loss and no duplication.

key.description:
Integer column to range-partition on. Quoted as an identifier (brackets)
before use, so it is safe against injection but must name a real output
column.

TLS configuration for an MSSQL connection.

ca_cert_path.description:
Optional path to a CA certificate (PEM/DER) to trust for server

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: subject
config_fields.description:
Subject to subscribe to. Supports NATS wildcards (`*` for one token,
`>` for the remaining tokens). In JetStream mode the durable consumer's
own filter subject governs delivery and this field is informational.

config_fields.name: servers
config_fields.description:
One or more NATS server URLs, e.g. `["nats://127.0.0.1:4222"]`. The
client connects to the first reachable server and uses the rest for
failover.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description: Authentication mode. Defaults to [`NatsAuth::None`] (anonymous).

config_fields.name: tls
config_fields.description: Require a TLS connection to the server. Defaults to `false`.

config_fields.name: name
config_fields.description: Optional client connection name (surfaced in NATS server monitoring).

config_fields.name: queue_group
config_fields.description:
Optional queue group for core-NATS load-balanced subscriptions — all
subscribers sharing a group split the subject's messages. Ignored in
JetStream mode.

config_fields.name: jetstream_stream
config_fields.description:
JetStream stream name. When set together with
[`jetstream_consumer`](Self::jetstream_consumer) the source pulls from a
durable JetStream consumer instead of a core-NATS subscription.

config_fields.name: jetstream_consumer
config_fields.description:
Name of the durable JetStream (pull) consumer to bind to. Required when
[`jetstream_stream`](Self::jetstream_stream) is set; the consumer must
already exist on the server.

config_fields.name: max_messages
config_fields.description:
Stop after this many messages have been drained. At least one of
`max_messages` / `idle_timeout_secs` must be set so a run terminates.

config_fields.name: idle_timeout_secs
config_fields.description:
Stop after this many seconds elapse with no new message. At least one of
`max_messages` / `idle_timeout_secs` must be set so a run terminates.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Messages per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). Drained
messages accumulate in an in-memory buffer and a page is yielded when
the buffer reaches this size (or when the run terminates with a partial
buffer). Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "drain-entire-run-window" sentinel: every
message produced before the terminator fires goes into a single page.

```yaml

subject: "events.>"
idle_timeout_secs: 5
```

Stop after this many messages have been drained. At least one of

NatsAuth.description:
NATS client authentication configuration.

Serializes with an adjacent `{ "type": <method>, "config": { … } }` tag in
snake_case, matching every other faucet connector's auth shape.

connectors.title: Apache Parquet
connectors.description: Apache Parquet file source (local, glob, or S3)

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: source
config_fields.description: Where to read Parquet from — a local file, a local glob pattern, or S3.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Arrow `RecordBatch` size used as the per-page hint when streaming.

Passed verbatim to
`ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder::with_batch_size`, which is itself
only a hint — Arrow may emit smaller batches at row-group boundaries,
so a single emitted [`faucet_core::StreamPage`] can hold fewer rows
than this number. Larger values improve throughput at the cost of
memory.

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the call to
`with_batch_size` is skipped and the underlying file's native
row-group size drives the page cadence (one page per row-group).
Useful for sinks like SQL `COPY` / BigQuery load jobs that prefer one
large request to many small ones.

Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

config_fields.name: columns
config_fields.description:
Optional column projection (column pruning).

When set, only the named columns are decoded — non-projected columns
are skipped entirely at the Parquet level, reducing I/O. Errors out
if a name does not exist in the file's schema.

config_fields.name: concurrency
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of files to read concurrently for `Glob` / S3 prefix
modes. Ignored for single-file modes.

connectors.name: postgres
connectors.title: PostgreSQL
connectors.description: PostgreSQL query source

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: connection_url
config_fields.description: PostgreSQL connection URL (e.g. `postgres://user:pass@host/db`).

config_fields.name: query
config_fields.description: SQL query to execute.

config_fields.name: params
config_fields.description: Bind parameters for the query. Defaults to empty.

config_fields.name: max_connections
config_fields.description: Maximum number of connections in the pool. Defaults to 10.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). Rows are
drained from the sqlx cursor and yielded whenever the buffer reaches
this size. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the cursor is fully
drained and the entire result set is emitted in a single page. Useful
for small lookup tables or for sinks (e.g. SQL `COPY`, BigQuery load
jobs) that prefer one large request to many small ones.

config_fields.name: shard
config_fields.description:
Optional primary-key range sharding for clustered (Mode B) execution.

When set, the source advertises itself as shardable: the cluster
coordinator splits the query's `key` range into contiguous slices that
different workers process concurrently. Has **no effect** outside the
cluster coordinator (a plain `faucet run` streams the whole query), so
it is fully backward compatible. See [`ShardConfig`].

config_schema.title: PostgresSourceConfig
config_schema.description: Configuration for the PostgreSQL query source.

params.description: Bind parameters for the query. Defaults to empty.

max_connections.description: Maximum number of connections in the pool. Defaults to 10.

batch_size.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). Rows are
drained from the sqlx cursor and yielded whenever the buffer reaches
this size. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the cursor is fully
drained and the entire result set is emitted in a single page. Useful
for small lookup tables or for sinks (e.g. SQL `COPY`, BigQuery load
jobs) that prefer one large request to many small ones.

shard.description:
Optional primary-key range sharding for clustered (Mode B) execution.

When set, the source advertises itself as shardable: the cluster
coordinator splits the query's `key` range into contiguous slices that
different workers process concurrently. Has **no effect** outside the
cluster coordinator (a plain `faucet run` streams the whole query), so
it is fully backward compatible. See [`ShardConfig`].

ShardConfig.description:
Primary-key range sharding settings for the PostgreSQL source.

The source is split by contiguous ranges of an **integer-typed** column:
each shard runs `SELECT * FROM (<query>) WHERE <key> >= lo AND <key> < hi`.
The column must be present in the query's output and orderable as a 64-bit
integer (e.g. a `bigint`/`int`/`serial` primary key).

**Nullable keys:** if the key column contains NULLs, those rows are not
visible to the `MIN`/`MAX` range enumeration. They are still read — exactly
one shard (the last) additionally matches `<key> IS NULL`, so NULL-key rows
are covered by precisely one shard with no loss and no duplication.

key.description:
Integer column to range-partition on. Quoted as an identifier before use,
so it is safe against injection but must name a real output column.

connectors.name: postgres-cdc
connectors.title: PostgreSQL CDC
connectors.description: PostgreSQL CDC source (logical replication)

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: connection_url
config_fields.description:
Connection URL pointing at the database whose WAL we want to read.
The crate internally upgrades the connection to `replication=database`
— callers do **not** need to add it themselves.

config_fields.name: slot_name
config_fields.description:
Logical replication slot name. Must match the Postgres naming rules:
1–63 chars, lowercase letters / digits / underscores only.

config_fields.name: publication_name
config_fields.description:
Publication name on the server. Must already exist (faucet does not
create publications — they're a DBA-level concern that determines
which tables are replicated).

config_fields.name: create_slot_if_missing
config_fields.description:
If the slot does not exist, create it as a logical/`pgoutput` slot
at connection time. Default: `true`.

config_fields.name: slot_type
config_fields.description:
Whether a newly-created slot is `permanent` (survives disconnect) or
`temporary` (auto-dropped when the replication connection closes).

Default `permanent` (back-compatible). **A permanent slot pins WAL on
the server until it is consumed or dropped** — an abandoned permanent
slot fills `pg_wal` and can take the whole instance down. Use
`temporary` for ephemeral / test runs (note: a temporary slot resets on
reconnect, so bookmark-based resume across runs requires a permanent
slot). Drop an unused permanent slot explicitly with
[`PostgresCdcSource::drop_slot`](crate::PostgresCdcSource::drop_slot).

config_fields.name: slot_acquire_retries
config_fields.description:
Number of times to retry acquiring the replication slot when the server
reports it is still **active** (held by a not-yet-released prior
connection). On a rapid restart — a scheduler or `serve` re-running the
pipeline before the previous backend has dropped the slot — both the
pre-stream `pg_replication_slot_advance` and `START_REPLICATION` fail
with *"replication slot … is active for PID …"*. Each retry waits an
exponentially increasing backoff (250 ms, doubling, capped at 4 s).
`0` disables retries (fail fast). Defaults to 10.

config_fields.name: tls
config_fields.description:
TLS settings for the replication connection. Default `disable`
(plaintext) for back-compatibility, but credentials and all WAL data
then travel unencrypted — set `require`/`verify_ca`/`verify_full` in
production.

config_fields.name: start_lsn
config_fields.description:
Optional starting LSN override (e.g. `"0/16A4F88"`). Ignored when a
state-store-managed bookmark is present (that bookmark wins).
When neither is set, replication starts from the slot's
`confirmed_flush_lsn`.

config_fields.name: proto_version
config_fields.description:
pgoutput protocol version. Only `1` is fully exercised in v1; `2` is
accepted but streaming-transaction messages (S/E/c/A) are not yet
decoded. Default: `1`.

config_fields.name: idle_timeout
config_fields.description:
Maximum time to wait for new replication messages before returning
the current batch. Default: 30 s.

config_fields.name: max_messages
config_fields.description:
Optional cap on the number of change events drained per fetch call.
Acts as a safety bound — `idle_timeout` is the primary terminator.

**Note:** the cap is checked **after each COMMIT**, never mid-
transaction. A single transaction larger than `max_messages` will
still be emitted atomically (the fetch returns only after that
transaction's COMMIT and may produce more records than `max_messages`).
To bound the memory a *single* in-progress transaction can consume,
use [`max_staged_records`](Self::max_staged_records) instead.

config_fields.name: max_staged_records
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of change records buffered in memory for a *single*
in-progress transaction before it is aborted.

Logical replication requires a transaction to be buffered until its
COMMIT so it can be emitted atomically (partial transactions must
never leak downstream). A single bulk `UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`COPY` of
millions of rows therefore buffers every decoded row as a
`serde_json::Value` in RAM, which can OOM the process. This bound is a
safety valve: when an in-progress transaction's staged record count
exceeds it, the source aborts with a typed
[`FaucetError::Source`] rather than
being OOM-killed.

`None` (the default) means unbounded — atomic delivery of arbitrarily
large transactions at the cost of unbounded memory. Set a value sized
to your available memory if you replicate tables subject to large
bulk writes.

config_fields.name: status_update_interval
config_fields.description:
Interval at which Standby Status Update keepalives are sent to the
server. Must be shorter than `idle_timeout` and well under the
server's `wal_sender_timeout` (default 60 s). Default: 10 s.

config_fields.name: tcp_keepalive
config_fields.description: TCP keepalive for the replication connection. Default: 60 s.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Advisory page size for
[`Source::stream_pages`](faucet_core::Source::stream_pages). The CDC
source emits **one `StreamPage` per committed transaction** so the
pipeline gets per-transaction durability via its per-page bookmark
persist. Because transactions are atomic units they are never split
across pages — a single transaction whose record count exceeds
`batch_size` still emits as one page. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: every committed
transaction during the run window is accumulated into a single page
that is emitted at the end with `bookmark = max(commit_lsn)`. This
negates per-transaction durability and is only useful for tests or
initial-snapshot style runs.

config_schema.title: PostgresCdcSourceConfig
config_schema.description: Configuration for [`PostgresCdcSource`](crate::PostgresCdcSource).

connection_url.description:
Connection URL pointing at the database whose WAL we want to read.
The crate internally upgrades the connection to `replication=database`
— callers do **not** need to add it themselves.

slot_name.description:
Logical replication slot name. Must match the Postgres naming rules:
1–63 chars, lowercase letters / digits / underscores only.

publication_name.description:
Publication name on the server. Must already exist (faucet does not
create publications — they're a DBA-level concern that determines
which tables are replicated).

create_slot_if_missing.description:
If the slot does not exist, create it as a logical/`pgoutput` slot
at connection time. Default: `true`.

slot_type.description:
Whether a newly-created slot is `permanent` (survives disconnect) or
`temporary` (auto-dropped when the replication connection closes).

Default `permanent` (back-compatible). **A permanent slot pins WAL on
the server until it is consumed or dropped** — an abandoned permanent

reconnect, so bookmark-based resume across runs requires a permanent
slot). Drop an unused permanent slot explicitly with
[`PostgresCdcSource::drop_slot`](crate::PostgresCdcSource::drop_slot).

slot_acquire_retries.description:

reports it is still **active** (held by a not-yet-released prior

pipeline before the previous backend has dropped the slot — both the

with *"replication slot … is active for PID …"*. Each retry waits an

`0` disables retries (fail fast). Defaults to 10.

tls.description:

(plaintext) for back-compatibility, but credentials and all WAL data
then travel unencrypted — set `require`/`verify_ca`/`verify_full` in
production.

Optional starting LSN override (e.g. `"0/16A4F88"`). Ignored when a
state-store-managed bookmark is present (that bookmark wins).
When neither is set, replication starts from the slot's
`confirmed_flush_lsn`.

accepted but streaming-transaction messages (S/E/c/A) are not yet
decoded. Default: `1`.

idle_timeout.description:
Maximum time to wait for new replication messages before returning
the current batch. Default: 30 s.

Optional cap on the number of change events drained per fetch call.
Acts as a safety bound — `idle_timeout` is the primary terminator.

To bound the memory a *single* in-progress transaction can consume,
use [`max_staged_records`](Self::max_staged_records) instead.

Maximum number of change records buffered in memory for a *single*

Logical replication requires a transaction to be buffered until its

status_update_interval.description:
Interval at which Standby Status Update keepalives are sent to the
server. Must be shorter than `idle_timeout` and well under the
server's `wal_sender_timeout` (default 60 s). Default: 10 s.

tcp_keepalive.description: TCP keepalive for the replication connection. Default: 60 s.

batch_size.description:
Advisory page size for
[`Source::stream_pages`](faucet_core::Source::stream_pages). The CDC
source emits **one `StreamPage` per committed transaction** so the
pipeline gets per-transaction durability via its per-page bookmark
persist. Because transactions are atomic units they are never split
across pages — a single transaction whose record count exceeds
`batch_size` still emits as one page. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: every committed

that is emitted at the end with `bookmark = max(commit_lsn)`. This
negates per-transaction durability and is only useful for tests or
initial-snapshot style runs.

SlotType.description: Lifetime of a newly-created replication slot.

oneOf.description: Survives disconnect; pins WAL until consumed or dropped. Default.
Auto-dropped by the server when the replication connection closes.

CdcTls.description: TLS configuration for the CDC replication connection.

oneOf.description: No TLS — plaintext (default, back-compatible).
Require TLS but do not verify the server certificate.

Require TLS and verify the certificate chain against `ca_path` (or the
system roots when `None`).
Require TLS and verify both the certificate chain and the hostname.

config_fields.name: subscription

Subscription id (short name, not the fully-qualified path). The client
forms `projects/<project>/subscriptions/<id>` from the connection's
project.

config_fields.name: project_id
config_fields.description:
GCP project id that owns the topic / subscription. Required for real
Pub/Sub; the emulator infers it from `PUBSUB_PROJECT_ID` when unset.

config_fields.name: endpoint
config_fields.description:
Override the Pub/Sub API endpoint (host:port or URL). Rarely needed —
prefer `emulator_host` for the emulator.

config_fields.name: emulator_host
config_fields.description:
Point the client at a Pub/Sub emulator (`host:port`). When set, auth is
skipped and the endpoint is taken from this value — mirrors the
`PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST` environment variable the SDK honours.

config_fields.name: credentials
config_fields.description: How to authenticate. Defaults to Application Default Credentials.

config_fields.name: value_format
config_fields.description: Payload decoding for the message `data` field.

config_fields.name: attributes_key
config_fields.description:
JSON key the message attribute map is surfaced under. Default
`__attributes`.

config_fields.name: max_messages_per_pull
config_fields.description: Messages requested per `pull` RPC (1–1000). Default 100.

config_fields.name: idle_termination_secs
config_fields.description:
Stop after this many seconds without a new message. At least one of
`idle_termination_secs` and `max_messages` must be set (mirrors the
Kafka / Kinesis sources) — a batch run must terminate.

config_fields.name: max_messages
config_fields.description: Stop after this many messages in total.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). `0` is the
"no batching" sentinel: one page per drain. Default 1000. A page's
messages are acked once the pipeline has durably written the page.

PubsubCredentials.description:
How to authenticate with Google Cloud Pub/Sub.

Serializes as `{ type: <method>, config: { … } }` (adjacent tagging,
snake_case discriminators) — the consistent auth wire shape shared by
every faucet connector:
`{ type: service_account_json_file, config: { path: "/run/secrets/sa.json" } }`.

oneOf.description:
Application Default Credentials — honours
`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS_JSON`,
gcloud user creds, and the GCE/GKE metadata server, in that order.
Path to a service-account JSON key file on disk.

path.description: Filesystem path to the service-account key JSON.

oneOf.description:
Service-account JSON key as an inline string. Pair with
`${env:GCP_SA_JSON}` / `${secret:…}` interpolation in CLI configs so

connectors.name: rabbitmq
connectors.title: RabbitMQ
connectors.description: RabbitMQ (AMQP 0.9.1) source; queue consume, ack after sink confirm, idle/max termination

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: queue
config_fields.description: Queue to consume from.

config_fields.name: url
config_fields.description:
Full AMQP URI, e.g. `amqp://user:pass@rabbit:5672/%2f` (the vhost is
URL-encoded; `%2f` is `/`). `amqps://` selects TLS. Mutually exclusive
with `host`/`port`/`vhost`.

config_fields.name: host
config_fields.description: Broker host. Defaults to `127.0.0.1` when `url` is not set.

config_fields.name: port
config_fields.description: Broker port. Defaults to `5672` (`5671` with TLS).

config_fields.name: vhost
config_fields.description: Virtual host. Defaults to `/`.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description: Authentication. Defaults to [`RabbitMqAuth::None`].

config_fields.name: tls
config_fields.description: TLS settings. Disabled by default.

config_fields.name: connection_name
config_fields.description: Client connection name shown in the RabbitMQ management UI.

config_fields.name: heartbeat_secs
config_fields.description:
Requested heartbeat interval in seconds (`0` disables heartbeats).
Unset uses the broker's proposal.

config_fields.name: connect_timeout_secs
config_fields.description:
Upper bound, in seconds, on establishing the connection (TCP + AMQP
handshake, including any retries). Defaults to 30.

config_fields.name: connect_retries
config_fields.description:
Extra TCP connect attempts (exponential backoff) before giving up.
Defaults to 0 — an unreachable broker fails immediately.

config_fields.name: declare_queue
config_fields.description:
Declare the queue before consuming (idempotent when it already exists
with the same properties). Defaults to `true`. Set `false` to consume
a queue managed elsewhere (it must exist).

config_fields.name: queue_durable
config_fields.description:
Whether a declared queue is durable (survives a broker restart).
Defaults to `true`. Must match an existing queue's durability.

config_fields.name: bindings
config_fields.description: Exchange → queue bindings to declare before consuming.

config_fields.name: prefetch
config_fields.description:
Consumer QoS window: the most unacknowledged deliveries the broker
sends ahead. `0` is unlimited. Defaults to `batch_size` (capped at
65535; unlimited when `batch_size` is 0 or larger than 65535). Under
`ack_mode: on_sink_confirm` it must be `0` or ≥ `batch_size`, or the
broker would stop delivering before a page could fill.

config_fields.name: ack_mode
config_fields.description: When deliveries are acknowledged. Defaults to `on_sink_confirm`.

config_fields.name: value_format
config_fields.description: How message bodies decode into records. Defaults to `json`.

config_fields.name: on_decode_error
config_fields.description: What to do with a body that fails to decode. Defaults to `fail`.

config_fields.name: include_metadata
config_fields.description:
Wrap each record as `{ "data": <body>, "exchange", "routing_key",
"delivery_tag", "redelivered", "headers", … }` instead of emitting the
decoded body alone. Defaults to `false`.

config_fields.name: consumer_tag
config_fields.description: Consumer tag. Defaults to a broker-generated one.

config_fields.name: max_messages
config_fields.description:
Stop after this many messages. At least one of `max_messages` /
`idle_timeout_secs` must be set so a run terminates.

config_fields.name: idle_timeout_secs
config_fields.description:
Stop after this many seconds with no new message. At least one of
`max_messages` / `idle_timeout_secs` must be set so a run terminates.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Messages per emitted page (and per acknowledgement under
`on_sink_confirm`). Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`]. `0` drains the
whole run window into one page.

config_schema.title: RabbitMqSourceConfig
config_schema.description:
Configuration for [`RabbitMqSource`](crate::RabbitMqSource).

The [`RabbitMqConnectionConfig`] surface (`url` / `host` / `port` / `vhost`
/ `auth` / `tls` / …) is flattened in:

```yaml
url: "amqp://guest:guest@127.0.0.1:5672/%2f"
queue: orders
idle_timeout_secs: 5
batch_size: 500
```

url.description:
Full AMQP URI, e.g. `amqp://user:pass@rabbit:5672/%2f` (the vhost is
URL-encoded; `%2f` is `/`). `amqps://` selects TLS. Mutually exclusive
with `host`/`port`/`vhost`.

host.description: Broker host. Defaults to `127.0.0.1` when `url` is not set.

port.description: Broker port. Defaults to `5672` (`5671` with TLS).

auth.description: Authentication. Defaults to [`RabbitMqAuth::None`].

tls.description: TLS settings. Disabled by default.

connection_name.description: Client connection name shown in the RabbitMQ management UI.

heartbeat_secs.description:
Requested heartbeat interval in seconds (`0` disables heartbeats).
Unset uses the broker's proposal.

connect_timeout_secs.description:
Upper bound, in seconds, on establishing the connection (TCP + AMQP
handshake, including any retries). Defaults to 30.

connect_retries.description:
Extra TCP connect attempts (exponential backoff) before giving up.
Defaults to 0 — an unreachable broker fails immediately.

declare_queue.description:
Declare the queue before consuming (idempotent when it already exists
with the same properties). Defaults to `true`. Set `false` to consume
a queue managed elsewhere (it must exist).

queue_durable.description:
Whether a declared queue is durable (survives a broker restart).
Defaults to `true`. Must match an existing queue's durability.

bindings.description: Exchange → queue bindings to declare before consuming.

prefetch.description:
Consumer QoS window: the most unacknowledged deliveries the broker
sends ahead. `0` is unlimited. Defaults to `batch_size` (capped at
65535; unlimited when `batch_size` is 0 or larger than 65535). Under
`ack_mode: on_sink_confirm` it must be `0` or ≥ `batch_size`, or the
broker would stop delivering before a page could fill.

ack_mode.description: When deliveries are acknowledged. Defaults to `on_sink_confirm`.

value_format.description: How message bodies decode into records. Defaults to `json`.

on_decode_error.description: What to do with a body that fails to decode. Defaults to `fail`.

include_metadata.description:
Wrap each record as `{ "data": <body>, "exchange", "routing_key",
"delivery_tag", "redelivered", "headers", … }` instead of emitting the
decoded body alone. Defaults to `false`.

consumer_tag.description: Consumer tag. Defaults to a broker-generated one.

max_messages.description:
Stop after this many messages. At least one of `max_messages` /
`idle_timeout_secs` must be set so a run terminates.

idle_timeout_secs.description:
Stop after this many seconds with no new message. At least one of
`max_messages` / `idle_timeout_secs` must be set so a run terminates.

batch_size.description:
Messages per emitted page (and per acknowledgement under
`on_sink_confirm`). Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`]. `0` drains the
whole run window into one page.

RabbitMqAuth.description:
RabbitMQ authentication.

Serializes with an adjacent `{ "type": <method>, "config": { … } }` tag in
snake_case, matching every other faucet connector's auth shape. The
hand-written [`std::fmt::Debug`] never prints the password.

oneOf.description:
No explicit credentials: the userinfo embedded in `url` is used, or the
AMQP default (`guest`/`guest`, which RabbitMQ only accepts from
loopback).
SASL `PLAIN` username + password. Overrides any userinfo in `url`.

SASL `EXTERNAL` — the broker authenticates the TLS client certificate
(requires `tls.enabled` plus `tls.client_cert_path`/`client_key_path`).

RabbitMqTls.description:
TLS (`amqps://`) settings. Server certificates are always verified — there
is no insecure mode.

enabled.description:
Connect over TLS. Also implied by an `amqps://` `url`. Requires the
connector's `tls` Cargo feature.

ca_cert_path.description:
PEM file of extra CA certificates to trust (in addition to the
platform's native root store) — for brokers with a private CA.

client_cert_path.description:
PEM client certificate for mutual TLS. Must be set together with
`client_key_path`.

RabbitMqBinding.description: A binding from an exchange to the consumed queue, declared before consuming.

exchange.description: Exchange to bind the queue to. Must not be the default exchange (`""`).

routing_key.description: Binding key (a pattern for `topic` exchanges). Defaults to `""`.

exchange_kind.description:
When set, the exchange is declared (durable) with this type before
binding; otherwise it must already exist.

RabbitMqExchangeKind.description: An AMQP exchange type, used when a connector declares an exchange.

oneOf.description: Route on an exact routing-key match.
Broadcast to every bound queue, ignoring the routing key.
Route on a dotted routing-key pattern (`*` one word, `#` zero or more).
Route on message header values.

AckMode.description: When deliveries are acknowledged to the broker.

oneOf.description:
At-least-once: a page's deliveries are acknowledged only after the
pipeline has written **and flushed** that page to the sink. A crash or
failed write before that leaves them unacknowledged, and the broker
redelivers them — duplicates are possible, loss is not.

At-most-once: the broker considers a message delivered as soon as it is
sent (`no_ack`). Fastest, but a crash loses in-flight messages.

RabbitMqValueFormat.description: How a message body maps to and from a JSON record.

oneOf.description:
The body is a JSON document. The source fails (or skips, per
`on_decode_error`) a body that is not valid JSON; the sink serializes
each record as JSON.

The body is UTF-8 text, emitted as a JSON string. The sink requires
string records.

The body is opaque bytes, emitted as a standard base64 JSON string. The
sink requires base64 string records.

OnDecodeError.description: What to do with a message whose body does not decode under `value_format`.

oneOf.description: Fail the run. The message stays unacknowledged and is redelivered.

Reject the message without requeue — it is dropped, or routed to the
queue's dead-letter exchange when one is configured — and continue.

  config:
    # url: ""    # Full AMQP URI, e.g.
    # host: ""    # Broker host.
    # port: 0    # Broker port.
    # vhost: ""    # Virtual host.
    # auth: { type: none }    # one of: none, plain, external
      # --- Alternative variants — replace the block above with one of these ---
      # type: plain
      # config:
        # username: ""    # REQUIRED
        # password: ""    # REQUIRED
      #
      # type: external
    # tls: { ... }    # TLS (`amqps://`) settings.
    # connection_name: ""    # Client connection name shown in the RabbitMQ management UI.
    # heartbeat_secs: 0    # Requested heartbeat interval in seconds (`0` disables heartbeats).
    # connect_timeout_secs: 30    # Upper bound, in seconds, on establishing the connection (TCP + AMQP handshake, including any retries).
    # connect_retries: 0    # Extra TCP connect attempts (exponential backoff) before giving up.
    queue: ""    # REQUIRED — Queue to consume from.
    # declare_queue: true    # Declare the queue before consuming (idempotent when it already exists with the same properties).
    # queue_durable: true    # Whether a declared queue is durable (survives a broker restart).
    # bindings: []    # Exchange → queue bindings to declare before consuming.
    # prefetch: 0    # Consumer QoS window: the most unacknowledged deliveries the broker sends ahead.
    # ack_mode: null    # When deliveries are acknowledged to the broker.
    # value_format: null    # How a message body maps to and from a JSON record.
    # on_decode_error: null    # What to do with a message whose body does not decode under `value_format`.
    # include_metadata: false    # Wrap each record as `{ "data": <body>, "exchange", "routing_key", "delivery_tag", "redelivered", "headers", … }` instead of emitting the decoded body alone.
    # consumer_tag: ""    # Consumer tag.
    # max_messages: 0    # Stop after this many messages.
    # idle_timeout_secs: 0    # Stop after this many seconds with no new message.
    # batch_size: 1000    # Messages per emitted page (and per acknowledgement under `on_sink_confirm`).

connectors.name: redis
connectors.title: Redis
connectors.description: Redis (streams, lists, keys) source

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: url
config_fields.description: Redis connection URL (e.g. `"redis://127.0.0.1:6379"`).

config_fields.name: source_type
config_fields.description: The type of Redis data structure to read from.

config_fields.name: max_records
config_fields.description: Optional maximum number of records to return.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). Each mode
maps the knob onto its native paging primitive:

- `Keys`: `SCAN COUNT batch_size` hint, followed by an `MGET` batched
  to `batch_size` records per page.
- `Stream`: `XRANGE - + COUNT batch_size`, advancing the start ID per
  page.
- `List`: `LRANGE start stop`, sliding the window by `batch_size`.

Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: every mode drains its
underlying primitive in a single round-trip (or, for `Keys`, the
minimum number of round-trips the `SCAN` cursor needs) and emits the
entire result set as a single page. Useful for small lookup tables or
for sinks like SQL `COPY` / BigQuery load jobs that prefer one large
request to many small ones.

config_schema.title: RedisSourceConfig
config_schema.description: Configuration for the Redis source connector.

source_type.description: The type of Redis data structure to read from.

max_records.description: Optional maximum number of records to return.

batch_size.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). Each mode
maps the knob onto its native paging primitive:

- `Keys`: `SCAN COUNT batch_size` hint, followed by an `MGET` batched
  to `batch_size` records per page.
- `Stream`: `XRANGE - + COUNT batch_size`, advancing the start ID per
  page.
- `List`: `LRANGE start stop`, sliding the window by `batch_size`.

Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: every mode drains its
underlying primitive in a single round-trip (or, for `Keys`, the
minimum number of round-trips the `SCAN` cursor needs) and emits the
entire result set as a single page. Useful for small lookup tables or
for sinks like SQL `COPY` / BigQuery load jobs that prefer one large
request to many small ones.

RedisSourceType.description: The type of Redis data structure to read from.

oneOf.description: Read all elements from a Redis list via `LRANGE`.

key.description: The list key.

oneOf.description:
Read entries from a Redis stream via `XRANGE` (or `XREAD` / `XREADGROUP`
for the consumer-group convenience path on `fetch_all`).

key.description: The stream key.

group.description:
Optional consumer group name. When set, [`fetch_all`](super::RedisSource::fetch_all)
uses `XREADGROUP`. Streaming via [`stream_pages`](faucet_core::Source::stream_pages)
always uses `XRANGE` (consumer-group semantics are incompatible
with the page-then-write streaming contract).

consumer.description: Consumer name within the group (required when `group` is set).

count.description:
Maximum number of entries to read per call. Used by
[`fetch_all`](super::RedisSource::fetch_all)'s `XREAD` / `XREADGROUP`
path; ignored by streaming, which uses
[`RedisSourceConfig::batch_size`] as both the per-page count and
the `XRANGE COUNT` hint.

oneOf.description: Scan for keys matching a pattern, then `MGET` each batch.

    # batch_size: 1000    # Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage).

connectors.name: redshift
connectors.title: Amazon Redshift
connectors.description: Amazon Redshift query source (PostgreSQL wire; streaming rows, incremental replication)

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: host
config_fields.description: Cluster / endpoint host (e.g. `my-cluster.abc123.us-east-1.redshift.amazonaws.com`).

config_fields.name: database
config_fields.description: Database name.

config_fields.name: user
config_fields.description: Database user.

config_fields.name: credentials
config_fields.description: Authentication credentials.

config_fields.name: query
config_fields.description:
SQL query to execute. May contain `${field.path}` parent-context tokens
(resolved to positional binds at runtime) and, for incremental
replication, a `${bookmark}` token.

config_fields.name: port
config_fields.description: Port. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_PORT`] (5439).

config_fields.name: tls
config_fields.description:
Whether to require TLS. Defaults to `true` (Redshift clusters require SSL
by default). `true` maps to `sslmode=require`; `false` maps to
`sslmode=prefer` (opportunistic TLS with plaintext fallback) — it never
forbids encryption outright.

config_fields.name: params
config_fields.description:
Positional bind parameters for the query, applied in `$1, $2, …` order
before any context- or bookmark-derived values. Defaults to empty.

config_fields.name: max_connections
config_fields.description: Maximum number of connections in the pool. Defaults to 10.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). Rows are
drained from the `sqlx` cursor and yielded whenever the buffer reaches
this size. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the cursor is fully
drained and the entire result set is emitted in a single page.

config_fields.name: replication
config_fields.description: Replication mode. Defaults to [`RedshiftReplication::Full`].

config_fields.name: state_key
config_fields.description:
Explicit state-store key for the incremental bookmark. When unset, a key
is derived from the host / database and a query fingerprint.

config_schema.title: RedshiftSourceConfig
config_schema.description: Configuration for the Amazon Redshift query source.

tls.description:
Whether to require TLS. Defaults to `true` (Redshift clusters require SSL
by default). `true` maps to `sslmode=require`; `false` maps to
`sslmode=prefer` (opportunistic TLS with plaintext fallback) — it never
forbids encryption outright.

query.description:
SQL query to execute. May contain `${field.path}` parent-context tokens
(resolved to positional binds at runtime) and, for incremental
replication, a `${bookmark}` token.

params.description:
Positional bind parameters for the query, applied in `$1, $2, …` order
before any context- or bookmark-derived values. Defaults to empty.

max_connections.description: Maximum number of connections in the pool. Defaults to 10.

batch_size.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). Rows are
drained from the `sqlx` cursor and yielded whenever the buffer reaches
this size. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the cursor is fully
drained and the entire result set is emitted in a single page.

state_key.description:
Explicit state-store key for the incremental bookmark. When unset, a key
is derived from the host / database and a query fingerprint.

RedshiftCredentials.description:
How to authenticate with Amazon Redshift.

Serializes as `{ type: <method>, config: { … } }` (adjacent tagging,
snake_case discriminators) — the consistent auth wire shape shared by every
faucet connector.

v1 implements only [`RedshiftCredentials::Password`]. The [`Iam`] and
[`RedshiftDataApi`] variants are accepted by the config parser (so a future
version can add them without a breaking change) but currently return a typed
[`FaucetError::Config`](faucet_core::FaucetError::Config) at client-build
time.

[`Iam`]: RedshiftCredentials::Iam
[`RedshiftDataApi`]: RedshiftCredentials::RedshiftDataApi

oneOf.description:
Username/password authentication (the user comes from
[`RedshiftConnection::user`]). The only mechanism supported in v1.

password.description:
The password (use `${env:…}` / `${vault:…}` to inject it, never a
literal).

oneOf.description:
IAM authentication via temporary cluster credentials
(`GetClusterCredentials`). **Not yet supported** — reserved for a future
version; building a client with this variant returns a typed error.

cluster_identifier.description: Provisioned cluster identifier used to request temporary credentials.

oneOf.description:
Authentication through the Redshift Data API (HTTP, not the PG wire).
**Not yet supported** — reserved for a future version; building a client
with this variant returns a typed error.

secret_arn.description: Secrets Manager ARN holding the database credentials.

RedshiftReplication.description:
How the Redshift source replicates rows across runs.

Serializes as `{ type: full }` or
`{ type: incremental, column: "...", initial_value: ... }`.

oneOf.description: Every run re-fetches the full result set (default).

Only rows whose `column` is strictly greater than the stored bookmark
(or `initial_value` on the first run) are emitted. If the SQL contains
the literal token `${bookmark}`, it is replaced with a positional bind
parameter so Redshift filters server-side (efficient); the source also
filters client-side as a correctness backstop. The new maximum of
`column` is persisted on the final page.

column.description: Column whose value is the replication cursor (e.g. `updated_at`).

initial_value.description: Lower bound used on the first run, before any bookmark is stored.

  config:

    user: ""    # REQUIRED — Database user.
    credentials:

      config:

      # --- Alternative variants — replace the block above with one of these ---
