    # state_key: ""    # Explicit state-store key for the incremental bookmark.

connectors.name: rest
connectors.title: REST
connectors.description: REST API source with pagination, auth, transforms

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: base_url
config_fields.description:
Base URL of the API, e.g. `https://api.example.com/v2`. Required. Joined
with [`path`](Self::path); any trailing slash is handled either way.

config_fields.name: path
config_fields.description:
URL path, relative to `base_url`. May contain `{key}` placeholders that
are substituted per-partition (e.g. `"/orgs/{org_id}/users"`).

config_fields.name: method
config_fields.description:
HTTP method for the data request. Defaults to `GET`; use `POST` for
search-style APIs that take a query `body`.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description:
Authentication: either inline (`{ type, config }`) or a `{ ref: <name> }`
pointer to a shared provider in the CLI's top-level `auth:` catalog.

config_fields.name: headers
config_fields.description:
Static request headers sent on **every** request (data pages, async-job
submit/poll/fetch requests, and OData `$metadata` discovery probes).
Applied *before* the auth provider's header placements, so an auth
header of the same name always wins on a clash. Values honor
`${env:}` / `${param.*}` load-time interpolation and pass through the
secrets/redaction boundary like other config strings. Invalid header
names/values are rejected at config load
([`FaucetError::Config`](faucet_core::FaucetError::Config)), never a
mid-run panic.

```yaml
headers:
  Prefer: transient
  Accept: application/json
```

config_fields.name: query_params
config_fields.description:
Static query-string parameters, rendered as `?k=v`. Values honor
`{placeholder}` context substitution for child sources. Empty by
default.

The `#[serde(default)]` here is load-bearing: without it this field was
**required**, so any config omitting it failed to deserialize — while
its siblings `headers` and `query_params_multi` both defaulted. Several
shipped examples omitted it and could not run at all, which nothing
caught because `faucet validate` did not deserialize connector configs
until #609.

config_fields.name: query_params_multi
config_fields.description:
Repeated / array-valued query params (#536), rendered as repeated keys —
e.g. `{ "group_by[]": ["api_key_id", "model"] }` → `?group_by[]=api_key_id&group_by[]=model`.
Applied alongside (in addition to) [`query_params`](Self::query_params);
use this for APIs that need a key to appear more than once (`group_by[]`,
repeated `expand`/`fields`). Values honor `{placeholder}` context
substitution for child sources, like `query_params`. Empty by default.
Query parameters that may repeat, e.g. `{ "fields": ["id", "name"] }`
renders `?fields=id&fields=name`. Use this rather than `query_params`
when the API expects a key more than once.

config_fields.name: body
config_fields.description: JSON request body, for `POST`/`PUT`-style reads. Ignored for `GET`.

config_fields.name: pagination
config_fields.description:
How to walk pages. Defaults to `none` (a single request). Each style
carries its own termination guard — see the crate README's pagination
table.

config_fields.name: records_path
config_fields.description:
JSONPath to the array of records inside the response body, e.g.
`$.data.items`. When unset the body is expected to *be* the array (or a
single object, which is emitted as one record).

config_fields.name: max_pages
config_fields.description:
Hard cap on pages fetched per run, across every pagination style — the
backstop against a feed that never signals completion. `None` removes
the cap.

config_fields.name: request_delay
config_fields.description:
Fixed delay between page requests, in seconds — a politeness knob for
APIs that rate-limit by request frequency. Applied *in addition* to any
`Retry-After` honoured by the retry path.

config_fields.name: timeout
config_fields.description:
Per-request timeout in seconds. Covers one HTTP request, not the whole
run, so a paginated extract is bounded per page.

config_fields.name: max_retries
config_fields.description:
Number of retries (after the first attempt) for transient request
failures. Default `3`.

**Precedence note:** the REST source predates the unified pipeline
`resilience:` policy. When this field (or [`retry_backoff`](Self::retry_backoff))
is left at its default, an injected `RetryPolicy` (e.g. from a
pipeline-level `resilience:` block, via
[`RestStream::with_retry_policy`](crate::RestStream::with_retry_policy))
governs the retry budget. Setting this field away from its default makes
it win — an explicit per-connector value is never silently overridden by
a pipeline-wide default.

config_fields.name: retry_backoff
config_fields.description:
Base exponential-backoff delay between retries. Default `1s`. Shares the
legacy-field precedence rule documented on [`max_retries`](Self::max_retries).

config_fields.name: tolerated_http_errors
config_fields.description:
HTTP status codes that should **not** cause an error. Responses with
these codes are treated as empty pages (no records, no further pages).

config_fields.name: retry_on_response
config_fields.description:
Responses to treat as throttling and retry, for APIs that signal a rate
limit with a 4xx other than 429 plus an error code in the body (e.g.
HTTP 400 with `error.code` 17 / 80004), or inside a 2xx
(`match_success`). A rule's `backoff_from` reads the wait from the
response (a reset header, a JSON header, the body). A matching response
counts as a rate-limit response (`faucet_source_throttled_total`,
`faucet_source_retries_total{class="rate_limited"}`) and is retried up
to `max_retries` times in a row before the original error is surfaced.
Checked before `tolerated_http_errors`. Applies to data pages,
`async_job` submit/poll requests and discovery requests.

config_fields.name: replication_method
config_fields.description:
`full_table` (default) re-reads everything each run; `incremental`
filters on [`replication_key`](Self::replication_key) and emits a
bookmark so the next run resumes.

config_fields.name: replication_key
config_fields.description:
Field used for incremental replication bookmarking: a top-level field
name (`updated_at`), a dot path into nested objects (`fields.updated`;
numeric segments index arrays, and a literal top-level field of that
exact name wins), or a JSON Pointer (`/fields/updated`) for field names
that contain dots. Not a JSONPath: it must resolve to one value.

config_fields.name: on_missing_key
config_fields.description:
What to do with a record whose `replication_key` is missing or `null`
once a start bookmark exists: `keep` (default — kept, counted in
`faucet_source_replication_key_missing_total`, warned once per run),
`drop` (counted and warned), or `fail` the run.

config_fields.name: start_replication_value
config_fields.description:
Bookmark value: records where `record[replication_key] <= start_replication_value`
are filtered out when `replication_method` is `Incremental`.

config_fields.name: state_key
config_fields.description:
Opt-in identifier used by [`Pipeline::with_state_store`](faucet_core::Pipeline::with_state_store)
to persist this stream's bookmark across runs. When set, the pipeline
will load any previously-stored bookmark before fetching and write the
new bookmark only after the sink confirms the batch.

Keys must satisfy [`faucet_core::state::validate_state_key`].

config_fields.name: name
config_fields.description: Human-readable stream name (used in logging and Singer SCHEMA messages).

config_fields.name: primary_keys
config_fields.description: Field names that uniquely identify a record (Singer `key_properties`).

config_fields.name: schema
config_fields.description: JSON Schema describing the structure of each record.

config_fields.name: schema_sample_size
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of records to sample when inferring the schema via
[`crate::stream::RestStream::infer_schema`].  `0` means sample all
available records (up to `max_pages`).  Defaults to `100`.

config_fields.name: requests
config_fields.description:
`requests:` — one entry per request: a context map whose values are
substituted into `path` placeholders. The stream is executed once per
entry and results are concatenated. Empty means run once with no
substitution. The pre-#670 spelling `partitions:` is still accepted.

config_fields.name: request_concurrency
config_fields.description:
`request_concurrency:` — maximum number of `requests` entries fetched
concurrently (`partition_concurrency:` is still accepted).
`None` (and `0`/`1`) means sequential processing — the default.

Honoured on **both** read paths since #624: the buffering `fetch_all`
and the `stream_pages` path the pipeline actually drives, where it used
to be silently ignored. Above 1, partition pages **interleave**: the
streams are polled together, so a page from partition 3 can arrive
before partition 1 has finished. Partitions are disjoint and the
persisted bookmark is a max across all of them, so this changes
throughput rather than the resume position — but a downstream that
assumed partition-at-a-time page order no longer gets it.

config_fields.name: tls
config_fields.description:
Optional client-certificate (mutual TLS) config. When set, the source
presents a client certificate on **every** request — data requests and
any inline auth token request (both go through the same HTTP client).
Requires the crate's `mtls` feature; a `tls` block on a build without it
is a load-time error rather than being silently ignored.

config_fields.name: response_format
config_fields.description:
How to parse the response body. `json` (default) uses JSONPath
extraction (`records_path`); `csv` / `excel` parse a tabular **file**
body into records — for authenticated file endpoints such as a cloud-drive
`…/content` download or any signed export
URL. In file mode a single response is fetched (pagination must be
`none`) and `records_path` does not apply. `excel` requires the crate's
`excel` feature.

config_fields.name: csv_delimiter
config_fields.description:
CSV field delimiter byte (default `,`). Used only when
`response_format: csv`.

config_fields.name: csv_has_headers
config_fields.description:
Whether the first CSV row is a header row supplying field names
(default `true`). When `false`, fields are named `column_0`, `column_1`, …

config_fields.name: csv_quote
config_fields.description:
CSV quote character (default `"`). Set it when the export quotes with
something else — without this knob a `'`-quoted export parsed as literal
quote characters inside every field (#670 L29). `response_format: csv`
and the `parse: csv` decode step both honour it.

config_fields.name: csv_null_values
config_fields.description:
CSV fields equal to any of these strings decode as JSON `null` instead
of a string (default: none). Some bulk-export APIs write a
null as an empty field, so their templates set `[""]`; other APIs list
sentinels such as `"NULL"` or `"#N/A"`. Headers are never mapped, and a
quoted empty field (`""`) is mapped like an unquoted one — the CSV
reader does not report quoting per field. `response_format: csv` only.

config_fields.name: excel_sheet
config_fields.description:
Excel worksheet to read: a sheet name, or a 0-based index as a string.
When omitted, the first worksheet is used. `response_format: excel` only.

config_fields.name: excel_header_row
config_fields.description:
0-based index of the Excel header row (default `0`). Rows above it are
skipped; the header row supplies field names. `response_format: excel` only.

config_fields.name: replication_bind
config_fields.description:
Bind the stored bookmark into the outgoing request (query param / header /
body field / path) so the server returns only new rows. Composes with the
existing `replication_key` client-side filter, which stays active as a
safety net. Requires `replication_method: incremental` + `replication_key`.

config_fields.name: odata
config_fields.description:
Speak the OData protocol: `@odata.nextLink` paging, the `$.value`
envelope, `$select`/`$filter`/`$expand`/`$orderby` sugar, and
`$metadata` (EDMX) → schema discovery. When set, it derives the
pagination, `records_path`, query params, and `Prefer` header at load
time (explicit values still win). See [`ODataConfig`].

config_fields.name: drop_key_prefixes
config_fields.description:
Drop per-record keys starting with any of these prefixes (#654 M24).

Protocol control fields — OData's `@odata.etag` / `@odata.editLink`,
JSON:API's `links`, HAL's `_links` — are metadata, not data, and are
often invalid column names downstream. An `odata:` block implies
`@odata.` (the prefix that used to be hardcoded), so existing configs
need no change; list prefixes here for any other protocol envelope.

config_fields.name: decode
config_fields.description:
Decode the response body before record extraction: a chain of
`extract` (JSONPath) / `base64` / `gunzip` / `unzip` / `parse`
(json|csv|xlsx|xml) steps. Lets a source consume base64/compressed/file
payloads (e.g. a base64 XLSX inside a SOAP body, or a gzipped-CSV export).
When set, it replaces the `response_format` body parsing, and pagination
must be `none`. See [`DecodeStep`](crate::decode::DecodeStep).

config_fields.name: async_job
config_fields.description:
Run a submit→poll→fetch job lifecycle instead of a single GET, for
bulk/export/report-run APIs (bulk export jobs, report runs, …). The
fetched result flows through `decode:` / `response_format`. When set,
pagination must be `none`. See [`AsyncJobConfig`](crate::async_job::AsyncJobConfig).

config_fields.name: window
config_fields.description:
Bound each request to a rolling `[start, end)` window between the stored
bookmark and `now`, iterating the windows within one run (each `step`
wide) with per-window bookmark durability. For APIs that require — or cap —
a bounded date range (analytics/ads/reporting feeds). Parity with Airbyte's
`DatetimeBasedCursor`. Requires `replication_method: incremental` +
`replication_key`, and a start bookmark (from state, or
`start_replication_value`). See [`WindowSpec`](faucet_core::WindowSpec).

config_fields.name: record_ancestors
config_fields.description:
When `records_path` selects a **nested** array element (e.g.
`$.data[*].data.object`), copy fields from the enclosing `[*]`
array-element ancestor onto each emitted record. The map is
`dest_field: ancestor_relative_path` — for each matched leaf, the source
walks up to the array-element ancestor and copies the named path onto the
record under `dest_field`. Absent ⇒ records are emitted unchanged.

```yaml
records_path: "$.data[*].data.object"
record_ancestors: { event_id: "id", event_created: "created" }
```

Requires `records_path` to contain an array wildcard `[*]`; mutually
exclusive with [`records_multi`](Self::records_multi).

config_fields.name: records_multi
config_fields.description:
Emit several record arrays from one response in a single page (sharing one
pagination advance), each stamped with a user-defined op marker under
[`op_field`](Self::op_field). Composes with a downstream
`write_mode: upsert` + `delete_marker` so added/modified/removed feeds
route correctly. Mutually exclusive with `records_path` /
`record_ancestors`, and requires `response_format: json` with no
`decode:` pipeline.

```yaml
records_multi:
  - { path: "$.added[*]",    op: upsert }
  - { path: "$.modified[*]", op: upsert }
  - { path: "$.removed[*]",  op: delete }
op_field: _op
```

config_fields.name: op_field
config_fields.description:
Field name each [`records_multi`](Self::records_multi) record is stamped
with its spec's `op` value. Defaults to `_op` when omitted.

config_fields.name: records_route
config_fields.description:
Route each record to a named stream by its GID type or a discriminator
field, stamping the stream into `stream_field` — so one bulk job's
parents and children reach separate sinks. See
[`RecordsRoute`](crate::route::RecordsRoute).

config_fields.name: persist_cursor
config_fields.description:
Persist the terminal pagination cursor as this run's bookmark (riding the
existing `StreamPage.bookmark` / `StateStore` path — no core trait change)
and, on resume, seed the stored bookmark back into the first request
(query param for `cursor`, request body field for `cursor_in_body`) before
paging. Only meaningful with `pagination: cursor` / `cursor_in_body`;
mutually exclusive with `window` slicing. Default `false`.

config_fields.name: discovery
config_fields.description:
Generic, vendor-neutral discovery recipe: declare which API calls to make
and how to extract datasets from their JSON responses (reusing this
source's `auth` / `base_url` / `headers`). Powers `faucet discover` and
run-time fan-out for any REST API with a listing / describe shape, with no
connector-specific code. See [`DiscoverySpec`](crate::discovery::DiscoverySpec).

config_schema.title: RestStreamConfig
config_schema.description:
Configuration for a RestStream.

`#[serde(default)]` at the container level: every field falls back to its
value from the [`Default`] impl below when omitted. Without it, **22 fields
were required** — a config had to spell out `max_retries`, `retry_backoff`,
`tolerated_http_errors`, `primary_keys`, `partitions`,
`schema_sample_size` and more before it would deserialize at all. That is
why the shipped examples are so verbose, and several of them still omitted
one field and could not run; nothing caught it because `faucet validate`
did not deserialize connector configs until #609.

`base_url` stays required — in serde *and* in the generated JSON Schema, so
`faucet init` still marks it `# REQUIRED`. Everything else defaults to the
value in the [`Default`] impl below.

base_url.description:
Base URL of the API, e.g. `https://api.example.com/v2`. Required. Joined
with [`path`](Self::path); any trailing slash is handled either way.

path.description:
URL path, relative to `base_url`. May contain `{key}` placeholders that
are substituted per-partition (e.g. `"/orgs/{org_id}/users"`).

method.description:
HTTP method for the data request. Defaults to `GET`; use `POST` for
search-style APIs that take a query `body`.

auth.description:
Authentication: either inline (`{ type, config }`) or a `{ ref: <name> }`
pointer to a shared provider in the CLI's top-level `auth:` catalog.

headers.description:
Static request headers sent on **every** request (data pages, async-job
submit/poll/fetch requests, and OData `$metadata` discovery probes).
Applied *before* the auth provider's header placements, so an auth
header of the same name always wins on a clash. Values honor
`${env:}` / `${param.*}` load-time interpolation and pass through the
secrets/redaction boundary like other config strings. Invalid header
names/values are rejected at config load
([`FaucetError::Config`](faucet_core::FaucetError::Config)), never a
mid-run panic.

```yaml
headers:
  Prefer: transient
  Accept: application/json
```

query_params.description:
Static query-string parameters, rendered as `?k=v`. Values honor
`{placeholder}` context substitution for child sources. Empty by
default.

The `#[serde(default)]` here is load-bearing: without it this field was
**required**, so any config omitting it failed to deserialize — while
its siblings `headers` and `query_params_multi` both defaulted. Several
shipped examples omitted it and could not run at all, which nothing
caught because `faucet validate` did not deserialize connector configs
until #609.

query_params_multi.description:
Repeated / array-valued query params (#536), rendered as repeated keys —
e.g. `{ "group_by[]": ["api_key_id", "model"] }` → `?group_by[]=api_key_id&group_by[]=model`.
Applied alongside (in addition to) [`query_params`](Self::query_params);
use this for APIs that need a key to appear more than once (`group_by[]`,
repeated `expand`/`fields`). Values honor `{placeholder}` context
substitution for child sources, like `query_params`. Empty by default.
Query parameters that may repeat, e.g. `{ "fields": ["id", "name"] }`
renders `?fields=id&fields=name`. Use this rather than `query_params`
when the API expects a key more than once.

body.description: JSON request body, for `POST`/`PUT`-style reads. Ignored for `GET`.

pagination.description:
How to walk pages. Defaults to `none` (a single request). Each style
carries its own termination guard — see the crate README's pagination
table.

records_path.description:
JSONPath to the array of records inside the response body, e.g.
`$.data.items`. When unset the body is expected to *be* the array (or a
single object, which is emitted as one record).

max_pages.description:
Hard cap on pages fetched per run, across every pagination style — the
backstop against a feed that never signals completion. `None` removes
the cap.

request_delay.description:
Fixed delay between page requests, in seconds — a politeness knob for
APIs that rate-limit by request frequency. Applied *in addition* to any
`Retry-After` honoured by the retry path.

timeout.description:
Per-request timeout in seconds. Covers one HTTP request, not the whole
run, so a paginated extract is bounded per page.

max_retries.description:
Number of retries (after the first attempt) for transient request
failures. Default `3`.

**Precedence note:** the REST source predates the unified pipeline
`resilience:` policy. When this field (or [`retry_backoff`](Self::retry_backoff))
is left at its default, an injected `RetryPolicy` (e.g. from a
pipeline-level `resilience:` block, via
[`RestStream::with_retry_policy`](crate::RestStream::with_retry_policy))
governs the retry budget. Setting this field away from its default makes
it win — an explicit per-connector value is never silently overridden by
a pipeline-wide default.

retry_backoff.description:
Base exponential-backoff delay between retries. Default `1s`. Shares the
legacy-field precedence rule documented on [`max_retries`](Self::max_retries).

tolerated_http_errors.description:
HTTP status codes that should **not** cause an error. Responses with
these codes are treated as empty pages (no records, no further pages).

retry_on_response.description:
Responses to treat as throttling and retry, for APIs that signal a rate
limit with a 4xx other than 429 plus an error code in the body (e.g.
HTTP 400 with `error.code` 17 / 80004), or inside a 2xx
(`match_success`). A rule's `backoff_from` reads the wait from the
response (a reset header, a JSON header, the body). A matching response
counts as a rate-limit response (`faucet_source_throttled_total`,
`faucet_source_retries_total{class="rate_limited"}`) and is retried up
to `max_retries` times in a row before the original error is surfaced.
Checked before `tolerated_http_errors`. Applies to data pages,
`async_job` submit/poll requests and discovery requests.

replication_method.description:
`full_table` (default) re-reads everything each run; `incremental`
filters on [`replication_key`](Self::replication_key) and emits a
bookmark so the next run resumes.

replication_key.description:
Field used for incremental replication bookmarking: a top-level field
name (`updated_at`), a dot path into nested objects (`fields.updated`;
numeric segments index arrays, and a literal top-level field of that
exact name wins), or a JSON Pointer (`/fields/updated`) for field names
that contain dots. Not a JSONPath: it must resolve to one value.

on_missing_key.description:
What to do with a record whose `replication_key` is missing or `null`
once a start bookmark exists: `keep` (default — kept, counted in
`faucet_source_replication_key_missing_total`, warned once per run),
`drop` (counted and warned), or `fail` the run.

start_replication_value.description:
Bookmark value: records where `record[replication_key] <= start_replication_value`
are filtered out when `replication_method` is `Incremental`.

state_key.description:
Opt-in identifier used by [`Pipeline::with_state_store`](faucet_core::Pipeline::with_state_store)
to persist this stream's bookmark across runs. When set, the pipeline
will load any previously-stored bookmark before fetching and write the
new bookmark only after the sink confirms the batch.

Keys must satisfy [`faucet_core::state::validate_state_key`].

name.description: Human-readable stream name (used in logging and Singer SCHEMA messages).

primary_keys.description: Field names that uniquely identify a record (Singer `key_properties`).

schema.description: JSON Schema describing the structure of each record.

schema_sample_size.description:
Maximum number of records to sample when inferring the schema via
[`crate::stream::RestStream::infer_schema`].  `0` means sample all
available records (up to `max_pages`).  Defaults to `100`.

requests.description:
`requests:` — one entry per request: a context map whose values are
substituted into `path` placeholders. The stream is executed once per
entry and results are concatenated. Empty means run once with no
substitution. The pre-#670 spelling `partitions:` is still accepted.

request_concurrency.description:
`request_concurrency:` — maximum number of `requests` entries fetched
concurrently (`partition_concurrency:` is still accepted).
`None` (and `0`/`1`) means sequential processing — the default.

Honoured on **both** read paths since #624: the buffering `fetch_all`
and the `stream_pages` path the pipeline actually drives, where it used
to be silently ignored. Above 1, partition pages **interleave**: the
streams are polled together, so a page from partition 3 can arrive
before partition 1 has finished. Partitions are disjoint and the
persisted bookmark is a max across all of them, so this changes
throughput rather than the resume position — but a downstream that
assumed partition-at-a-time page order no longer gets it.

tls.description:
Optional client-certificate (mutual TLS) config. When set, the source
presents a client certificate on **every** request — data requests and
any inline auth token request (both go through the same HTTP client).
Requires the crate's `mtls` feature; a `tls` block on a build without it
is a load-time error rather than being silently ignored.

response_format.description:
How to parse the response body. `json` (default) uses JSONPath
extraction (`records_path`); `csv` / `excel` parse a tabular **file**
body into records — for authenticated file endpoints such as a cloud-drive
`…/content` download or any signed export
URL. In file mode a single response is fetched (pagination must be
`none`) and `records_path` does not apply. `excel` requires the crate's
`excel` feature.

csv_delimiter.description:
CSV field delimiter byte (default `,`). Used only when
`response_format: csv`.

csv_has_headers.description:
Whether the first CSV row is a header row supplying field names
(default `true`). When `false`, fields are named `column_0`, `column_1`, …

csv_quote.description:
CSV quote character (default `"`). Set it when the export quotes with
something else — without this knob a `'`-quoted export parsed as literal
quote characters inside every field (#670 L29). `response_format: csv`
and the `parse: csv` decode step both honour it.

csv_null_values.description:
CSV fields equal to any of these strings decode as JSON `null` instead
of a string (default: none). Some bulk-export APIs write a
null as an empty field, so their templates set `[""]`; other APIs list
sentinels such as `"NULL"` or `"#N/A"`. Headers are never mapped, and a
quoted empty field (`""`) is mapped like an unquoted one — the CSV
reader does not report quoting per field. `response_format: csv` only.

excel_sheet.description:
Excel worksheet to read: a sheet name, or a 0-based index as a string.
When omitted, the first worksheet is used. `response_format: excel` only.

excel_header_row.description:
0-based index of the Excel header row (default `0`). Rows above it are
skipped; the header row supplies field names. `response_format: excel` only.

replication_bind.description:
Bind the stored bookmark into the outgoing request (query param / header /
body field / path) so the server returns only new rows. Composes with the
existing `replication_key` client-side filter, which stays active as a
safety net. Requires `replication_method: incremental` + `replication_key`.

odata.description:
Speak the OData protocol: `@odata.nextLink` paging, the `$.value`
envelope, `$select`/`$filter`/`$expand`/`$orderby` sugar, and
`$metadata` (EDMX) → schema discovery. When set, it derives the
pagination, `records_path`, query params, and `Prefer` header at load
time (explicit values still win). See [`ODataConfig`].

drop_key_prefixes.description:
Drop per-record keys starting with any of these prefixes (#654 M24).

Protocol control fields — OData's `@odata.etag` / `@odata.editLink`,
JSON:API's `links`, HAL's `_links` — are metadata, not data, and are
often invalid column names downstream. An `odata:` block implies
`@odata.` (the prefix that used to be hardcoded), so existing configs
need no change; list prefixes here for any other protocol envelope.

decode.description:
Decode the response body before record extraction: a chain of
`extract` (JSONPath) / `base64` / `gunzip` / `unzip` / `parse`
(json|csv|xlsx|xml) steps. Lets a source consume base64/compressed/file
payloads (e.g. a base64 XLSX inside a SOAP body, or a gzipped-CSV export).
When set, it replaces the `response_format` body parsing, and pagination
must be `none`. See [`DecodeStep`](crate::decode::DecodeStep).

async_job.description:
Run a submit→poll→fetch job lifecycle instead of a single GET, for
bulk/export/report-run APIs (bulk export jobs, report runs, …). The
fetched result flows through `decode:` / `response_format`. When set,
pagination must be `none`. See [`AsyncJobConfig`](crate::async_job::AsyncJobConfig).

window.description:
Bound each request to a rolling `[start, end)` window between the stored
bookmark and `now`, iterating the windows within one run (each `step`
wide) with per-window bookmark durability. For APIs that require — or cap —
a bounded date range (analytics/ads/reporting feeds). Parity with Airbyte's
`DatetimeBasedCursor`. Requires `replication_method: incremental` +
`replication_key`, and a start bookmark (from state, or
`start_replication_value`). See [`WindowSpec`](faucet_core::WindowSpec).

record_ancestors.description:
When `records_path` selects a **nested** array element (e.g.
`$.data[*].data.object`), copy fields from the enclosing `[*]`
array-element ancestor onto each emitted record. The map is
`dest_field: ancestor_relative_path` — for each matched leaf, the source
walks up to the array-element ancestor and copies the named path onto the
record under `dest_field`. Absent ⇒ records are emitted unchanged.

```yaml
records_path: "$.data[*].data.object"
record_ancestors: { event_id: "id", event_created: "created" }
```

Requires `records_path` to contain an array wildcard `[*]`; mutually
exclusive with [`records_multi`](Self::records_multi).

records_multi.description:
Emit several record arrays from one response in a single page (sharing one
pagination advance), each stamped with a user-defined op marker under
[`op_field`](Self::op_field). Composes with a downstream
`write_mode: upsert` + `delete_marker` so added/modified/removed feeds
route correctly. Mutually exclusive with `records_path` /
`record_ancestors`, and requires `response_format: json` with no
`decode:` pipeline.

```yaml
records_multi:
  - { path: "$.added[*]",    op: upsert }
  - { path: "$.modified[*]", op: upsert }
  - { path: "$.removed[*]",  op: delete }
op_field: _op
```

op_field.description:
Field name each [`records_multi`](Self::records_multi) record is stamped
with its spec's `op` value. Defaults to `_op` when omitted.

records_route.description:
Route each record to a named stream by its GID type or a discriminator
field, stamping the stream into `stream_field` — so one bulk job's
parents and children reach separate sinks. See
[`RecordsRoute`](crate::route::RecordsRoute).

persist_cursor.description:
Persist the terminal pagination cursor as this run's bookmark (riding the
existing `StreamPage.bookmark` / `StateStore` path — no core trait change)
and, on resume, seed the stored bookmark back into the first request
(query param for `cursor`, request body field for `cursor_in_body`) before
paging. Only meaningful with `pagination: cursor` / `cursor_in_body`;
mutually exclusive with `window` slicing. Default `false`.

discovery.description:
Generic, vendor-neutral discovery recipe: declare which API calls to make
and how to extract datasets from their JSON responses (reusing this
source's `auth` / `base_url` / `headers`). Powers `faucet discover` and
run-time fan-out for any REST API with a listing / describe shape, with no
connector-specific code. See [`DiscoverySpec`](crate::discovery::DiscoverySpec).

AuthSpec.description:
A connector's `auth:` field: **either** an inline auth definition `A`
(the `{ type, config }` shape), **or** a `{ ref: <name> }` reference to a
shared provider defined in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

`ref` is mutually exclusive with inline fields — supplying both is a
deserialization error.

anyOf.description: Inline auth, spelled out on the connector.
A reference to a shared provider in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

oneOf.description: Bearer token in the `Authorization` header.
API key sent in a request header.

API key sent as a query parameter (e.g. `?api_key=secret`).

Some APIs require the key in the URL rather than a header. The `param`
field is the query parameter name, and `value` is the key itself.

expiry_ratio.description:
Fraction of `expires_in` after which the cached token is considered
expired and a new one is fetched. Must be in `(0.0, 1.0]`.
Defaults to `0.9` (refresh after 90 % of the token lifetime).

oneOf.description:
Fetch a token from an arbitrary HTTP endpoint.

The endpoint is called, the token is extracted from the JSON response
using `token_path` (a JSONPath expression), and then used as a Bearer
token (or in a custom header if `header_name` is set).

Tokens are cached and refreshed automatically when `expiry_path`
is provided and the server returns an expiry value.

method.description: HTTP method for the token request (e.g. GET, POST).

body.description: Optional JSON body for the token request.

token_path.description: JSONPath expression to extract the token string from the response.

expiry_path.description:
Optional JSONPath expression to extract the expiry (in seconds)
from the response. When absent, the token is cached indefinitely.

expiry_ratio.description:
Fraction of the expiry after which the token is proactively refreshed.
Must be in `(0.0, 1.0]`. Defaults to `0.9`.

encoding.description:
Body encoding: `json` (default) or `form`
(`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, required by RFC-6749 OAuth
token endpoints).

oneOf.description:
Arbitrary headers attached to every request (e.g. multi-tenant routing,
API keys split across several headers).

TokenBodyEncoding.description: Body encoding for the token-endpoint request.

oneOf.description: JSON body (`application/json`) — the default (back-compat).

Form-urlencoded body (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) — required by
RFC-6749 OAuth token endpoints (most OAuth servers),
which reject a JSON body with `unsupported_grant_type`.

AuthReference.description:
A `{ ref: <name> }` pointer to a named provider in the top-level `auth:`
catalog. The only permitted key is `ref`.

ref.description: Name of the provider in the top-level `auth:` catalog.

oneOf.description:
POST-search pagination: the next-page cursor is read from the response
body via `next_token_path` and written **into the request JSON body** at
`body_cursor_field` for the next request (rather than a query param).

The first request uses `config.body` unchanged; each subsequent request
sets `body[body_cursor_field] = <extracted cursor>`. Pagination stops when
`next_token_path` is null/absent, and a repeated cursor trips the same
loop guard as [`PaginationStyle::Cursor`]. Used by e.g. CRM object
search (`POST /crm/v3/objects/{obj}/search`, `$.paging.next.after` → `after`).

`body_cursor_field` may also be an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer
(`/variables/after`) for a nested location — e.g. a GraphQL request
sent through the REST source. The pointer must resolve to an existing
value, or to a new key of an existing object (#751).

The full URL of the next page is embedded in the response body.
`next_link_path` is a JSONPath expression pointing to that URL field
(e.g. `"$.next_link"`).  Pagination stops when the field is absent,
null, or an empty string.

Offset/limit pagination that writes the offset and limit into the JSON
**request body** (POST-query APIs), rather than the query string
([`Offset`](Self::Offset)) or a cursor token
([`CursorInBody`](Self::CursorInBody)). Each request sends
`body[offset_field] = <offset>` and `body[limit_field] = <limit>`; the
offset advances by the page's record count. With `stop_when_short`
(default `true`) a page shorter than `limit` ends pagination; a zero-record
page always ends it, and a repeated identical page trips a loop guard.
Either field may be a JSON Pointer (`/page/offset`) for a nested
location, with the same rules as `CursorInBody.body_cursor_field`.

rows_path.description:
JSONPath whose matches are counted to advance the offset and detect a
short page, instead of the extracted record count — for report APIs
whose whole response is one record (`$.rows`). An array counts its
elements, an object 1, null or no match 0 (which ends pagination).

total_path.description:
JSONPath to the total row count; pagination stops once the offset
reaches it. A missing or non-numeric total falls back to the
short-page rule.

oneOf.description:
Keyset pagination by the running max/min of a record field (#554). After
each page the aggregate of `field` over its records is injected into the
next request (as a query param or body field per `into`) at `param`. With
`stop_when_short` (default `true`) a page shorter than `page_size` ends
pagination; a zero-record page always ends it, and a non-advancing cursor
trips a loop guard.

field.description: Record field whose value drives the cursor.

into.description: Where the cursor is injected on the next request (default `query`).

param.description: Request parameter/body-field name the cursor is written to.

stop_when_short.description: Stop when a page returns fewer than `page_size` records (default `true`).

page_size.description: Expected page size, used for the short-page stop check.

RecordCursorTarget.description:
Where a [`PaginationStyle::RecordFieldCursor`] keyset value is injected on the
next request.

oneOf.description: Inject the cursor as a query parameter (default).
Inject the cursor into the JSON request body.

RecordCursorAgg.description:
How a [`PaginationStyle::RecordFieldCursor`] aggregates the cursor field over
a page.

oneOf.description: The maximum value seen so far (ascending keyset, the default).
The minimum value seen so far (descending keyset).

RetryMatcher.description:
One `retry_on_response` rule: a response that matches every set condition
is treated as throttling.

status.description:
HTTP statuses this rule applies to (empty = any non-2xx, or any status
with `match_success`).

match_success.description:
Also match 2xx responses, for APIs that report throttling inside a
successful response (GraphQL `THROTTLED` errors, `x-ratelimit-remaining:
0`). Requires `body_path` or `header`.

body_path.description:
JSONPath into the (JSON) response body; any match equal to one of
`values` satisfies the rule. A non-JSON body never matches.

values.description:
Values that match (numbers and strings compare by their text, so `17`
matches `"17"`). Required with `body_path`; with only `header`, they
are compared against the header value.

header.description:
A response header that must be present (and, without `body_path`,
equal one of `values` when any are listed).

backoff_from.description:
Where the response says how long to wait. Takes precedence over
`backoff_secs`; when the value is missing or unreadable the rule falls
back to `backoff_secs`, then `Retry-After`, then exponential backoff.

backoff_secs.description:
Fixed wait before retrying. Without it the server's `Retry-After` is
honoured, else exponential backoff applies.

max_wait_secs.description:
Longest wait `backoff_from` may ask for (default 3600). A longer one
fails the run with an error naming the reset instead of parking it.

BackoffFrom.description: Where a matched response states its wait.

oneOf.description: A response header (`x-ratelimit-reset`).

name.description: Header name.

oneOf.description:
A JSON-valued response header, read at a JSONPath
(a usage header carrying a JSON object).

name.description: Header name.

path.description:
JSONPath into the parsed header value; the first number or string
found is used.

oneOf.description: A value in the JSON response body.

path.description: JSONPath into the body; the first number or string found is used.

oneOf.description:
A leaky-bucket cost report (a GraphQL cost extension): wait
`ceil((requested - available) / restore_rate)` seconds, at least 1.

requested.description: JSONPath to the cost the request asked for.

available.description: JSONPath to the points currently available.

restore_rate.description: JSONPath to the points restored per second.

oneOf.description: A wait in seconds.
A wait in milliseconds.
A wait in minutes.
An absolute Unix time in seconds.
An absolute Unix time in milliseconds.
An absolute RFC 3339 instant.

ReplicationMethod.description: Determines how records are replicated from the source.

oneOf.description: All records are fetched on every run (default).

Only records where the `replication_key` field is strictly greater than
the stored bookmark (`start_replication_value`) are kept.

OnMissingKey.description: What to do with a record whose replication key is missing or `null` (#747).

oneOf.description:
Keep the record, count it, and warn (default): dropping it would be
silent data loss.
Drop the record (counted and warned, never silent).
Fail the run.

TlsClientConfig.description:
Client-certificate (mutual TLS) configuration for the HTTP sources.

Supply **either** a PEM certificate + key pair (`client_cert` + `client_key`)
**or** a PKCS#12 identity file (`client_identity_pkcs12` [+ `pkcs12_password`]).
PEM values may be inline or pulled in with `${file:…}` / `${secret:…}` /
`${vault:…}`; the PKCS#12 value is a path to a `.p12`/`.pfx` file (its binary
content can't be embedded in a text config).

client_cert.description: PEM-encoded client certificate chain. Pair with `client_key`.

client_key.description: PEM-encoded PKCS#8 private key. Pair with `client_cert`.

client_identity_pkcs12.description:
Path to a PKCS#12 (`.p12`/`.pfx`) identity file — an alternative to the
PEM pair.

pkcs12_password.description: Password for the PKCS#12 file (omit or empty if the file is unencrypted).

min_version.description:
Minimum negotiated TLS version: `"1.2"` or `"1.3"`. Defaults to the
TLS backend's own minimum when unset.

ResponseFormat.description: How to parse the response body into records.

oneOf.description: JSON — extract records via `records_path` (JSONPath). The default.

CSV — parse a tabular file body (each row → a JSON object). For
authenticated file endpoints (e.g. an export URL). Always available.

Excel (`.xlsx`/`.xls`) — parse a workbook body. Requires the crate's
`excel` feature.

JSON Lines — one JSON object per line (a bulk export job's
result, #768). An async-job fetch is decoded line by line into pages
of `batch_size`, so the file is never held in memory whole.

ReplicationBind.description:
Declarative binding of the stored bookmark into the **outgoing request** —
"server-side incremental push-down" (#513).

Today faucet tracks bookmarks and filters incrementally *client-side* (after
download). A bind lets a source instead push the bookmark into the request
(query param / header / body field / path) so the server returns only the
new rows. The existing client-side [`filter_incremental`] stays active as a
safety net for servers that don't honour the filter exactly.

into.description: Where to place the rendered value.

name.description:
The parameter / header / body-field / path-placeholder name. Optional
only for `into: body` with a `path`.

path.description:
`into: body` only: an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the configured `body`
(`/filterGroups/0/filters/0/value`) instead of a top-level `name` (#748).
It must resolve to an existing scalar or to a new key of an existing
object; array elements are never created.

value_type.description: JSON type written by a body bind: `string` (default) or `number`.

template.description:
Template rendered with [`BIND_PLACEHOLDER`] (`${bookmark}`) replaced by
the formatted bookmark. Defaults to the bare `${bookmark}`; set e.g.
`"gte|${bookmark}"` (an operator-prefixed filter) or `"[${bookmark} TO *]"` (Lucene).

format.description: How to format the bookmark before substitution.

advance_from.description:
Optional JSONPath into the response body to advance the bookmark from,
instead of `max(record[replication_key])`.

BindTarget.description: Where a rendered bookmark is injected into the outgoing request.

oneOf.description: A query-string parameter (default) — e.g. `?updated_after=…`.
A request header — e.g. `If-Modified-Since: …`.

A field of the JSON request body (POST-search APIs): a top-level field
named by `name`, or any existing location addressed by a JSON Pointer
`path` (#748).
A `{name}` placeholder in the request path.

BindValueType.description: The JSON type a body-target bind writes (#748).

oneOf.description: A JSON string (default).
A JSON number (e.g. an `epoch_ms` bookmark an API requires unquoted).

BindFormat.description:
How the bookmark value is formatted before it is substituted into the
[`ReplicationBind::template`].

For every non-[`Raw`](BindFormat::Raw) format the bookmark is first parsed
into an instant: a string is read as RFC 3339, a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` date
(midnight UTC), or a naive `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` (assumed UTC); a JSON
number is read as **epoch seconds**. It is then re-emitted in the target
representation, so `epoch_ms` ← ISO string and `iso8601` ← epoch number both
work.

oneOf.description:
Emit the scalar verbatim (string as-is, number as its decimal form).
The default; no timestamp parsing.
Unix epoch **seconds** (integer).
Unix epoch **milliseconds** (integer).
Calendar date `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC).

ODataConfig.description:
OData protocol options for the REST source (#512).

A minimal block — `{ entity: Orders }` — is enough; it derives paging,
the `$.value` envelope, and (for `faucet discover`) `$metadata` parsing.
The query-option fields render into the standard `$select`/`$filter`/
`$expand`/`$orderby` params.

entity.description:
Entity set to read (appended to `base_url` as the path, e.g. `Orders`).
Optional when the path already names the entity.

page_size.description: Server page size, sent as `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=<n>`.

fan_out.description:
**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): the fan-out key group may change
shape in a minor release; changes are called out in the changelog.

Fan out **at run time**: when `true`, `faucet run` / `faucet serve` turn the
[`objects`](Self::objects) list into one matrix row per entity set (each
with its `odata.entity` selected and its sink `table_id` rendered from
[`emit`](Self::emit)), so one generic template with
`objects: "${param.objects}"` syncs any entity set passed at trigger — no
pre-generated matrix, no field discovery needed (OData returns every column
by default). Default `false` (the block then only affects a single-entity
run / `faucet discover`). Same key and semantics as `discovery.fan_out`.

objects.description:
Entity sets to select — a YAML list **or** a comma-separated string (so a
single string run-param can drive it: `objects: "${param.objects}"`).
Empty means fall back to `$metadata` discovery of every declared entity
set (`faucet discover`). Same key and semantics as `discovery.objects`.

emit.description:
What each discovered/fanned-out entity emits (sink `table_id` template,
sink routing, extra per-entity config). Same shape as `discovery.emit`.
Unset ⇒ defaults (`table_id: "${name_snake}"`, the default sink).

key_ranges.description:
`key_ranges:` — split large entities into contiguous primary-key
ranges fetched concurrently, instead of one sequential
`@odata.nextLink` page walk. See [`PartitionSpec`]. The pre-#670
spelling `partition:` is still accepted.

ODataVersion.description: OData protocol version, which selects the paging-link key.

oneOf.description: OData v2 — JSON-light next link `odata.nextLink`.
OData v4 (default) — next link `@odata.nextLink`.

EmitSpec.description:
**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

What each discovered dataset **emits** — shared by every discovery mechanism
(`discovery.emit` and `odata.emit`), so the vocabulary is identical wherever
datasets fan out. All string leaves are templates over the dataset:
`${name}` (verbatim), `${name_snake}`, `${name_lower}`, and (where a
`describe` step ran) `${field_names}`.

config.description:
A JSON object deep-merged into the dataset's source config (e.g. an
`async_job` query, or extra per-entity overrides). Every string leaf is
templated. Optional for mechanisms whose selection patch is implicit
(OData sets `odata.entity` itself).

table_id.description:
Sink `table_id` template (e.g. `"raw_${name_snake}"`). Rendered per
dataset into the descriptor's `sink_patch`.

sink_ref.description:
Sink template (an entry under `pipeline.sinks`) each fanned-out dataset
routes to. Unset ⇒ the default (singular `pipeline.sink`) template, with
the rendered `table_id` merged in.

PartitionSpec.description:
**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

Key-range partitioned extraction of a paged dataset (`odata.partition`):
tile the dataset's integer primary-key space into contiguous ranges and
fetch them concurrently. Range planning is
[`faucet_core::shard::plan_pk_shards`] — the same primitive the SQL sources
shard with, including its unbounded first/last ranges (rows inserted below
MIN / above MAX during the run are still read).

objects.description:
With `fan_out`: which datasets to partition (a YAML list or a
comma-separated string). Each listed dataset whose `$metadata` declares a
**single integer** key partitions on it; others fall back to sequential
paging. Empty on a single-entity run (where [`key`](Self::key) applies
directly).

key.description:
Integer key column to range-split on. On the fan-out path this is derived
from `$metadata` per dataset; set it explicitly for a single-entity run.

count.description:
Number of ranges to tile into (default `workers ×`
[`RANGES_PER_WORKER`], clamped to [`MAX_PARTITION_COUNT`]).

DecodeStep.description: One step of the decode chain.

anyOf.description: Parameterless byte step (`base64` / `gunzip`).
Pull a (string) field out of a JSON body first.

extract.description: JSONPath to a string field whose value becomes the buffer.

anyOf.description: Select a member from a zip archive.
Terminal parse into records.

SimpleStep.description: A byte-chain step with no parameters (`- base64`, `- gunzip`).

oneOf.description: Base64-decode the (UTF-8 text) buffer into bytes.
Gzip-decompress the buffer.

UnzipSpec.description: Select a member of a zip archive.

member.description:
Glob (`*.csv`, `prefix*`, `*mid*`, or an exact name) selecting the member.
When omitted, the first file entry is used.

ParseSpec.description: Parse the decoded bytes into records.

records_path.description:
JSONPath selecting the record array (json/xml). When omitted, an array
body becomes the records and an object becomes a single record.

has_headers.description: Whether the first CSV row is a header (default `true`).

ParseFormat.description: Final-parse format for a decode chain.

oneOf.description: JSON (default).
Delimited text.
Excel workbook (requires the crate's `excel` feature).
XML → JSON.

job_id.description: JSONPath to the job id in the submit response.

lookback.description:
Incremental replication only: re-read margin subtracted from the
persisted bookmark, same grammar as `window.lookback` (`45s` / `30m` /
`6h` / `30d`; default `5m`). The bookmark is the client's run-start
clock, so without a margin a client clock running *ahead* of the server
would permanently skip records stamped in the gap; the margin turns
that loss into a bounded re-read (deduped by an upsert sink).

query_path.description:
Where the bulk **statement** sits inside the [`submit`](Self::submit)
body, as an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer (#654 M23). Defaults to `/query` — the
top-level `query` key that used to be hardcoded, so an API putting its
statement at `sql`, `statement`, or a nested path silently lost
incremental push-down and collapsed every object onto one dataset
identity. Three behaviours read it: the incremental predicate
injection, `validate()`'s incremental gate, and the catalog/lineage
dataset name.

sync_below_rows.description:
Skip the job entirely and read through the source's **ordinary
paginated path** when a cheap probe says the object is small (#629).

An async bulk API has a fixed async floor — job queue plus processing,
measured at ~14s of a 22s 701-row bulk-export run — that is paid
whatever the row count. A synchronous query API answers the same
request immediately. Bulk is still right for the large objects it was
designed for, so the choice is per-run and made from data rather than
from a guess baked into the config.

Requires [`count`](Self::count). The source's own `path` / `params` /
`pagination` describe the synchronous read, so a config that opts in
carries both shapes and faucet picks between them.

count.description:
Row-count probe for [`sync_below_rows`](Self::sync_below_rows) — a
request plus a JSONPath to the count in its response.

incremental.description:
How an incremental run pushes its bookmark into the submit body (#768).
Absent means `inject: { mode: sql }` — the `WHERE` predicate at
[`query_path`](Self::query_path).

submit_errors.description:
Errors a submit can return with a `200` and no job id — GraphQL
`userErrors`, or a "job already running" rejection (#768).

JobRequest.description: One HTTP request in a job lifecycle (submit / fetch).

url.description:
URL — absolute, or a `base_url`-relative path. `${job_id}` is substituted.

Required for `submit`. For `fetch`, set **exactly one** of `url` (a fixed
template) or [`url_from`](Self::url_from) (a JSONPath into the poll body).

url_from.description:
`fetch` only (#543): resolve the download URL from the **last poll
response body** via JSONPath, instead of rendering [`url`](Self::url).
For APIs that return a one-time signed download link in the poll body
(e.g. a report run's `result.url`) rather than at a deterministic
`/{job_id}` path. The matched value must be a string; an absolute URL is
used verbatim, a relative one is resolved against `base_url`. Mutually
exclusive with [`url`](Self::url).

locator_header.description:
`fetch` only (#557): result-set continuation. Response header carrying a
pagination locator (e.g. a bulk-export `X-Locator` header). While present
(and not empty / `"null"`), the fetch is repeated with the locator sent as
[`locator_param`](Self::locator_param), appending records across pages.

locator_body.description:
`fetch` only (#557): JSONPath into the fetch response **body** for the
continuation locator, when it rides the body rather than a header.
Alternative to [`locator_header`](Self::locator_header).

locator_param.description:
`fetch` only (#557): query-param name the locator is sent as on each
continuation request. Required when a locator source is configured.

records_path.description:
`fetch` only (#557): JSONPath for extracting records from each fetch page,
overriding the source-level `records_path`. Applies to a JSON result body.

locator_terminal_values.description:
`fetch` only (#654 M24): locator values that mean **no more pages**,
compared case-insensitively after trimming. Defaults to `["null"]` — one
vendor's sentinel, which used to be hardcoded in the pagination loop, so
an API signalling completion with `none` / `-1` / `EOF` needed a code
change. An empty/whitespace locator is always terminal regardless of
this list; set it to `[]` to make *only* emptiness terminal.

json.description:
JSON request body (#768) — for status checks that are a `POST` with a
query body, such as a GraphQL `node(id:)` lookup. `${job_id}` is
substituted in every string leaf.

interval_secs.description:
Ceiling on the poll cadence in seconds (default `5`). Polling starts at
1s and doubles up to this cap, so a job that finishes seconds after
submit is noticed quickly while a long-running one isn't hammered. Set
it to the slowest acceptable poll rate — it is the maximum gap between
polls, not a fixed wait.

timeout_secs.description: Give up after this many seconds (default `1800`).

JobStatus.description: How to read the job's terminal state from a poll response.

path.description: JSONPath to the status value in the poll response.

error_path.description:
JSONPath to an error code or message in the poll response (e.g. a
bulk export job's `$.data.node.errorCode`), named in the error a
failed job raises (#768).

RowCountProbe.description:
A cheap row-count request, used to decide between the async-job and the
synchronous read paths (#629).

url.description:
URL — absolute, or a `base_url`-relative path. `${job_id}` is substituted.

Required for `submit`. For `fetch`, set **exactly one** of `url` (a fixed
template) or [`url_from`](Self::url_from) (a JSONPath into the poll body).

url_from.description:
`fetch` only (#543): resolve the download URL from the **last poll
response body** via JSONPath, instead of rendering [`url`](Self::url).
For APIs that return a one-time signed download link in the poll body
(e.g. a report run's `result.url`) rather than at a deterministic
`/{job_id}` path. The matched value must be a string; an absolute URL is
used verbatim, a relative one is resolved against `base_url`. Mutually
exclusive with [`url`](Self::url).

locator_header.description:
`fetch` only (#557): result-set continuation. Response header carrying a
pagination locator (e.g. a bulk-export `X-Locator` header). While present
(and not empty / `"null"`), the fetch is repeated with the locator sent as
[`locator_param`](Self::locator_param), appending records across pages.

locator_body.description:
`fetch` only (#557): JSONPath into the fetch response **body** for the
continuation locator, when it rides the body rather than a header.
Alternative to [`locator_header`](Self::locator_header).

locator_param.description:
`fetch` only (#557): query-param name the locator is sent as on each
continuation request. Required when a locator source is configured.

records_path.description:
`fetch` only (#557): JSONPath for extracting records from each fetch page,
overriding the source-level `records_path`. Applies to a JSON result body.

locator_terminal_values.description:
`fetch` only (#654 M24): locator values that mean **no more pages**,
compared case-insensitively after trimming. Defaults to `["null"]` — one
vendor's sentinel, which used to be hardcoded in the pagination loop, so
an API signalling completion with `none` / `-1` / `EOF` needed a code
change. An empty/whitespace locator is always terminal regardless of
this list; set it to `[]` to make *only* emptiness terminal.

count_path.description:
JSONPath to the count in the probe response. The match must be a
number, or a string parsing as one.

inject.description: Where and how the bookmark is written into the submit body.

template.description:
`template` mode: the filter text, with `${bookmark}` replaced by the
formatted bookmark — e.g. `updated_at:>'${bookmark}'`.

format.description: `template` mode: how the bookmark is formatted (default `raw`).

initial.description:
`template` mode: what `${faucet.filter}` renders to when there is no
bookmark yet (the first run, or `full_table`). Default empty.

InjectMode.description: How the incremental bookmark reaches the submit body.

oneOf.description:
`WHERE <replication_key> > <bookmark>` injected into the SQL statement
at `query_path` (#630). The default.

Render [`IncrementalInject::template`] and substitute it for every
`${faucet.filter}` placeholder in the submit body — for search-syntax
filters such as `updated_at:>'…'`.

path.description:
JSONPath to the error messages in the submit response, e.g.
`$.data.bulkOperationRunQuery.userErrors[*].message`. A non-empty match
fails the run with those messages.

retry_on.description:
Substrings marking a "busy" rejection — another job is still running —
that is retried after [`retry_interval_secs`](Self::retry_interval_secs)
instead of failing. Matched case-insensitively.

retry_timeout_secs.description: Stop retrying a busy rejection after this many seconds (default `900`).

step.description:
Window size — `45s` / `30m` / `6h` / `30d`, or a bare integer (= seconds).
Absolute UTC durations (`d` = 24h); calendar/DST-correct windows are a
[`faucet backfill`] concern, not the incremental cursor.

lower.description: Lower-bound bind, rendered with the window **start**.

upper.description:
Upper-bound bind, rendered with the window **end**. Optional: omit it when
`lower.template` renders both bounds through `${window.end}`; only the
`lower` bind is then applied.

granularity.description:
Subtract this from each window's *rendered* upper bound so `[start, end]`
is non-overlapping for inclusive-inclusive APIs (Airbyte
`cursor_granularity`). Same grammar as `step`. The **persisted bookmark is
always the true half-open boundary**, so resume never gaps or overlaps —
only the value sent to the server is adjusted.

lookback.description:
Re-scan this much *before* the bookmark on the first window, to catch
late-arriving updates without a full replay. Same grammar as `step`.

max_windows.description:
Safety cap on the number of windows enumerated in one run. On overflow the
sweep is truncated (logged, never silently), and the next run resumes from
the last window's end.

WindowBind.description:
Injects a rendered window boundary into the outgoing request — the window
analogue of [`ReplicationBind`](crate::ReplicationBind). Reuses the same
[`BindTarget`] placement and [`BindFormat`] formatting.

into.description:
Where to place the rendered boundary (query param / header / body field /
path placeholder).

name.description:
The parameter / header / body-field / path-placeholder name. Optional
only for `into: body` with a `path`.

path.description:
`into: body` only: an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the configured `body`
(`/dateRanges/0/startDate`) instead of a top-level `name` (#748).

value_type.description: JSON type written by a body bind: `string` (default) or `number`.

template.description:
Template rendered with [`WINDOW_PLACEHOLDER`] (`${window}`) replaced by the
formatted boundary. Defaults to the bare `${window}`; set e.g.
`"gte|${window}"` or `"[${window} TO *]"`. `${window.start}` and
`${window.end}` render the window's start and (granularity-adjusted) end
in any bind, so one bind can carry both bounds
(`"segments.date BETWEEN '${window.start}' AND '${window.end}'"`). The
rendered value is not escaped for any query language.

format.description: How to format the boundary before substitution.

RecordsMultiSpec.description:
One entry in a [`RestStreamConfig::records_multi`] fan-out (#548): a JSONPath
selecting an array of records, plus the op marker each is stamped with.

path.description: JSONPath selecting an array of records (e.g. `"$.added[*]"`).

op.description:
Op marker stamped onto each record from `path` under
[`RestStreamConfig::op_field`] (e.g. `upsert` / `delete`, or `u` / `d`).

field.description: `by: field` only: the top-level discriminator field.

routes.description:
Route key → target. Keys are object types (`Order`), `child_of:<Type>`
for id-less children, or discriminator values under `by: field`.

stream_field.description: Column each routed row is stamped with its stream name (default `_stream`).

only.description:
Emit only these streams; rows of the other configured routes are
skipped deliberately (not counted as unknown). Empty = every route.

strict.description:
Fail the run on a row no route names, instead of dropping it with a
one-shot warning per type. Default `false`.

RouteBy.description: What a route key is read from.

oneOf.description:
The object type in a GID (`gid://<app>/<Type>/<id>`) in the row's `id`.
A row without one is keyed `child_of:<ParentType>` from `__parentId`.
The value of a top-level [`RecordsRoute::field`] (e.g. `__typename`).

parent_key_as.description: Copy `__parentId` into this column so the child stream joins back.

DiscoverySpec.description:
A generic discovery recipe on a REST source.

**Experimental** (PRINCIPLES.md §3): this block's shape may change in a
minor release; any change is called out in the changelog.

list.description:
Step 1 — enumerate datasets from a listing endpoint. Optional: omit it and
supply [`objects`](Self::objects) directly (e.g. from a run param).

objects.description:
Datasets supplied directly — a YAML list **or** a comma-separated string
(`"A,B,C"`), so a single string run-param can drive it
(`objects: "${param.objects}"`). Used instead of `list` when non-empty.

describe.description:
Step 2 — per-dataset field discovery (builds a typed schema + a field list
to template into `emit`). Optional: omit when the dataset needs no field
enumeration (e.g. an API that returns every column by default).

emit.description:
Step 3 — what each discovered dataset emits (the source `config_patch`
that selects it, an optional sink `table_id` template, and sink routing).
Shared shape with `odata.emit` ([`EmitSpec`](crate::config::EmitSpec));
`emit.config` is required here — it is what selects the dataset.

fan_out.description:
Fan out **at run time**: `faucet run` / `serve` turn the discovered
datasets into one matrix row each, before `expand`. Default `false`
(the block then only powers `faucet discover`). Same key and semantics
as `odata.fan_out`.

DiscoveryList.description: Step 1 — the listing request + how to read dataset names out of its response.

items.description: JSONPath selecting the array of listing items (e.g. `$.objects[*]`).

name.description: JSONPath, relative to each item, yielding its name (e.g. `$.name`).

keep_if.description: Optional keep-if predicate over each item (e.g. `queryable == true`).

exclude_name_suffixes.description:
Drop any dataset whose name ends with one of these suffixes (e.g.
`[ChangeEvent, Feed, Share, History]`). Vendor-neutral name filtering.

DiscoveryPredicate.description:
A keep-if predicate: keep a listing item when the value at `path` equals
`equals`.

path.description: JSONPath relative to the item.

equals.description: Keep the item iff the extracted value equals this.

DiscoveryDescribe.description: Step 2 — the per-dataset describe request + how to read fields + types.

get.description:
Request path template (relative to `base_url`), with `${name}` for the
dataset (e.g. `/catalog/objects/${name}/fields`); `GET`.

fields.description: JSONPath selecting the array of field objects (e.g. `$.fields[*]`).

field_name.description: JSONPath, relative to each field, yielding its name.

field_type.description:
JSONPath, relative to each field, yielding its raw type string. Absent ⇒
no typed schema is built (fields are still listed for templating).

field_nullable.description:
JSONPath, relative to each field, yielding a truthy "is nullable" flag.
Absent ⇒ every column is nullable.

type_map.description:
Raw-type → JSON-Schema-type map (`integer` / `number` / `boolean` /
`string` / `object` / `array`). Key `"*"` is the fallback; absent ⇒
`string`.

skip_types.description:
Drop fields whose raw type is one of these (e.g. compound / blob types
not selectable in a query).

    # method: "GET"    # HTTP method for the data request.
    # auth: { type: none }    # one of: none, bearer, basic, api_key, api_key_query, oauth2, token_endpoint, custom
      # --- Alternative variants — replace the block above with one of these ---

        # token: ""    # REQUIRED
      #
      # type: basic
      # config:
        # username: ""    # REQUIRED
        # password: ""    # REQUIRED
      #
      # type: api_key
      # config:
        # header: ""    # REQUIRED
        # value: ""    # REQUIRED
      #

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: bucket
config_fields.description: S3 bucket name.

config_fields.name: prefix
config_fields.description: Object key prefix filter.

config_fields.name: region
config_fields.description: AWS region. `None` uses the SDK default.

config_fields.name: endpoint_url
config_fields.description: Custom endpoint URL for S3-compatible services (e.g. MinIO).

config_fields.name: file_format
config_fields.description: Format of the files to read. Defaults to `json_lines`.

config_fields.name: max_objects
config_fields.description: Maximum number of objects to read.

config_fields.name: concurrency
config_fields.description:
Maximum number of concurrent object reads (default: 10).

These `#[serde(default)]`s are the same oversight the REST source
carried: without them every field here was **required**, so a config
naming only `bucket` could not deserialize at all (#609). `bucket` is
the one genuinely required field.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). For
`JsonLines` and `RawText` formats, the object body is decoded
line-by-line via [`tokio::io::AsyncBufReadExt`] and a page is yielded
whenever the buffer reaches this size; multi-object scans flatten so
a single page may contain lines from any object. For `JsonArray`,
each object is buffered fully before its records are chunked into
pages of this size (see the README "Streaming and batching" section
for the caveat). Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: every page is one
complete object — no within-object chunking. Useful for small
lookup files, or for sinks (e.g. SQL `COPY`, BigQuery load jobs)
that prefer one large request per file to many small ones.

config_fields.name: verify_length
config_fields.description:
Verify each object's byte length against the length the store
advertises, failing the read with
[`FaucetError::Source`](faucet_core::FaucetError::Source) on a short
(truncated) or over-long transfer (#161). Cheap — a byte counter over
a body that is read anyway — so it defaults to `true`.

Skipped (with a debug log, not a failure) when the store advertises no
length, or when it reports a non-empty `Content-Encoding`: the body on
the wire is then transcoded and its length legitimately differs from
the stored object's.

config_fields.name: verify_checksum
config_fields.description:
Verify each object's body against the checksum the store advertises
(#161). Stronger than the length check but costs a hash over the full
body, so it defaults to `false`. When the store advertises no usable
checksum for an object, verification is skipped for that object (a
debug log notes it); the length check still applies.

config_fields.name: compression
config_fields.description:
Compression codec applied to each downloaded object. Defaults to
[`CompressionConfig::Auto`](faucet_core::CompressionConfig::Auto) —
the codec is resolved per-object-key, so a single source can read a
mix of compressed and uncompressed objects. Requires the
crate-local `compression` feature.

config_fields.name: csv
config_fields.description: CSV dialect, used when `file_format: csv` (#604).

config_fields.name: excel
config_fields.description: Worksheet selection, used when `file_format: xlsx` (#604).

config_fields.name: xml
config_fields.description: Record framing, used when `file_format: xml` (#604).

config_fields.name: avro
config_fields.description: Reader schema, used when `file_format: avro` (#719).

config_fields.name: orc
config_fields.description: Column projection, used when `file_format: orc` (#719).

config_fields.name: parquet
config_fields.description:
Column projection, used when `file_format: parquet` (#777): only
`parquet.columns` are decoded, before any row group is read.

S3FileFormat.description: Format of files stored in S3.

oneOf.description: Each line in the file is a separate JSON record.
The entire file is a JSON array of records.
Each file becomes a single record with `"key"` and `"content"` fields.

Apache Parquet objects. Each object is decoded via the Arrow Parquet
reader; its `RecordBatch`es feed both the row path (converted to JSON
records) and the **columnar** fast path
([`Source::stream_batches`](faucet_core::Source::stream_batches)) so an
`s3(parquet) → parquet`/`delta` chain never materializes
`serde_json::Value`. Requires the crate-local `arrow` feature
(RFC 0002 / #375).

Delimited text, decoded through
[`faucet_core::file_format`] so the records match what every other
connector produces for the same file. Dialect from
[`csv`](S3SourceConfig::csv). Requires `file-format-csv` (#604).

XML, decoded to the compact element→object mapping. The repeated
element is named by [`xml`](S3SourceConfig::xml). Requires
`file-format-xml` (#604).

An Excel workbook. Sheet and header row from
[`excel`](S3SourceConfig::excel). **Buffered whole** — a workbook is a
zip container whose directory sits at the end, so peak memory is the
object, not the page. Requires `file-format-excel` (#604).

Apache Avro Object Container Files. Each file's embedded writer
schema is resolved against [`avro.schema`](S3SourceConfig::avro) when
set, else against the first object's schema, so the prefix reads as one
shape. Joins the columnar path with the `arrow` feature. Requires
`file-format-avro` (#719).

Apache ORC, projected by [`orc.columns`](S3SourceConfig::orc).
**Buffered whole** (the footer sits at the end) and decoded stripe by
stripe; joins the columnar path. Requires `file-format-orc` (#719).
Detect from filename suffix: `.gz` → Gzip, `.zst` → Zstd, anything else → None.

delimiter.description: Field separator. A single character; `"\t"` is accepted for tabs.

has_headers.description:
Whether the first row names the fields. When false, fields are named
`column_0`, `column_1`, … — the same fallback the REST source and the
`csv` connector already use. On write it decides whether a header row
is written.

quote.description: Quote character. A single byte; default `"`.

flexible.description:
Whether rows may have a different number of fields than the header.
`false` fails the read on the first ragged row, naming its line; `true`
keeps the fields the row has. Unset, each connector picks: the `file`
source is strict, the object-store sources and the REST source are
lenient.

null_values.description: Cell values read as `null` instead of a string (e.g. `["", "NULL"]`).

on_unknown_field.description:
What a streaming CSV writer does with a field the header does not
have. See [`CsvUnknownField`]. Whole-object encoders always write the
union of every record's fields, so it only affects the `file` sink.

CsvUnknownField.description: What a CSV writer does with a field that is not in the header.

oneOf.description: Add it as a new column; earlier rows get an empty cell for it.

Fix the header from the first page and drop the field, logging a
warning once per field.
Fix the header from the first page and fail the write naming the field.

sheet.description: Worksheet name, or an index as a string. Default: the first sheet.

XmlOptions.description:
XML record framing.

XML has no canonical record boundary, so one must be declared. On read,
`record_element` names the repeated element; without it the decoder falls
back to "the document's root children", which is right for the common
`<rows><row/>…</rows>` shape and wrong often enough that naming the element
is recommended in the docs.

record_element.description:
Element that delimits one record. Read: select these. Write: wrap each
record in one.

root_element.description: Document element wrapping the records. Write only.

schema.description:
An Avro schema (the JSON form: an object, an array for a union, or a
primitive name). On a **source** it is the *reader* schema every file
is resolved against — projection, aliases, defaults for added fields.
On a **sink** it is the *writer* schema; without it the schema is
inferred from the records.

codec.description:
Block codec for written files: `null` (default), `deflate`, `snappy`,
`zstd`. Reading detects the codec from the file header.

oneOf.description: Uncompressed blocks — the Avro default and the most portable.
Raw deflate (RFC 1951), readable by every Avro implementation.
Snappy with the per-block CRC-32 the spec requires.
Zstandard.

columns.description:
Top-level columns to read, in file order. Default: every column. A
name the file does not have is an error, not an empty column.

ParquetReadOptions.description: Parquet reader options (the `parquet:` block of an object-store source).

columns.description:
Decode only these top-level columns. A name missing from an object is
an error naming the object and its columns. Unset: every column.

yielded whenever the buffer reaches this size (bounded memory). For
`json_array`, each file is buffered fully, then its records are chunked

throughput improves without changing which file an error is attributed
to. Lower than the object-store sources' default because every read
shares one SSH channel, and many servers cap concurrent open handles.
`0` is treated as `1`.
