keeps the fields the row has. Unset, each connector picks: the `file`
source is strict, the object-store sources and the REST source are
lenient.

null_values.description: Cell values read as `null` instead of a string (e.g. `["", "NULL"]`).

on_unknown_field.description:
What a streaming CSV writer does with a field the header does not
have. See [`CsvUnknownField`]. Whole-object encoders always write the
union of every record's fields, so it only affects the `file` sink.

CsvUnknownField.description: What a CSV writer does with a field that is not in the header.

oneOf.description: Add it as a new column; earlier rows get an empty cell for it.

Fix the header from the first page and drop the field, logging a
warning once per field.
Fix the header from the first page and fail the write naming the field.

sheet.description: Worksheet name, or an index as a string. Default: the first sheet.

XmlOptions.description:
XML record framing.

XML has no canonical record boundary, so one must be declared. On read,
`record_element` names the repeated element; without it the decoder falls
back to "the document's root children", which is right for the common
`<rows><row/>…</rows>` shape and wrong often enough that naming the element
is recommended in the docs.

record_element.description:
Element that delimits one record. Read: select these. Write: wrap each
record in one.

root_element.description: Document element wrapping the records. Write only.

schema.description:
An Avro schema (the JSON form: an object, an array for a union, or a
primitive name). On a **source** it is the *reader* schema every file
is resolved against — projection, aliases, defaults for added fields.
On a **sink** it is the *writer* schema; without it the schema is
inferred from the records.

codec.description:
Block codec for written files: `null` (default), `deflate`, `snappy`,
`zstd`. Reading detects the codec from the file header.

oneOf.description: Uncompressed blocks — the Avro default and the most portable.
Raw deflate (RFC 1951), readable by every Avro implementation.
Snappy with the per-block CRC-32 the spec requires.
Zstandard.

columns.description:
Top-level columns to read, in file order. Default: every column. A
name the file does not have is an error, not an empty column.

ParquetReadOptions.description: Parquet reader options (the `parquet:` block of an object-store source).

columns.description:
Decode only these top-level columns. A name missing from an object is
an error naming the object and its columns. Unset: every column.

connectors.title: Snowflake
connectors.description: Snowflake query source (SQL REST API)

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: account
config_fields.description: Snowflake account identifier (e.g. `"xy12345.us-east-1"`).

config_fields.name: warehouse
config_fields.description: Warehouse to use for the session.

config_fields.name: database
config_fields.description: Database name.

config_fields.name: schema
config_fields.description: Schema name.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description:
Authentication: either inline (`{ type, config }`) or a `{ ref: <name> }`
pointer to a shared provider in the CLI's top-level `auth:` catalog.
A shared provider must yield a `Bearer` or `Token` credential, which
maps onto [`SnowflakeAuth::OAuth`]; key-pair JWT is always inline.

config_fields.name: query
config_fields.description:
SQL statement to execute. May contain `${field.path}` placeholders that
are resolved against the parent-record context at runtime; resolved
values are sent as positional bind parameters appended after
[`params`](Self::params).

config_fields.name: role
config_fields.description: Optional role to assume for the session.

config_fields.name: params
config_fields.description:
Positional bind parameters for the query, applied in order before any
context-derived values. Snowflake's SQL REST API uses 1-based positional
binds in the JSON request body (see the `bindings` field in the
[SQL API docs](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/sql-api/submitting-requests#using-bind-variables-in-a-statement)).

config_fields.name: statement_timeout
config_fields.description:
Per-statement server-side timeout. Defaults to 60 seconds. Passed
through as the `timeout` field on the `POST /api/v2/statements` request
body. The HTTP-level timeout for each individual request is configured
separately by the source via the underlying `reqwest` client defaults.

config_fields.name: poll_timeout
config_fields.description:
Maximum wall-clock time the source will spend polling an asynchronous
statement (one for which the initial `POST /api/v2/statements`
returns HTTP 202) before giving up with
[`FaucetError::Source`](faucet_core::FaucetError::Source).
Without this cap a statement that never finishes would loop forever.
Defaults to 300 seconds. Set to `0` to disable the cap and poll
indefinitely.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage).

Snowflake's SQL REST API splits large result sets into *partitions* (one
chunk of rows per HTTP response). The source re-frames partitions into
`batch_size`-sized pages: rows accumulate in a buffer and are yielded as
soon as the buffer reaches `batch_size`. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the **"no batching" sentinel**: the entire result
set is buffered and emitted in a single page. Useful for small lookup
tables, or for sinks (e.g. SQL `COPY`, BigQuery load jobs) that prefer
one large request to many small ones.

config_fields.name: partition_concurrency
config_fields.description:
How many result **partitions** to fetch concurrently (#621).

Snowflake splits a large result into server-chosen partitions, each
its own `GET …/partition={n}`. Fetching them one at a time makes the
read latency-bound on the round trip rather than throughput-bound on
the data, and the partition count is the server's choice — not
something `batch_size` can influence.

Defaults to `4`. `0` and `1` both mean sequential. Partitions are
fetched **in order** with a bounded look-ahead, so the emitted row
order is unchanged and a failure is still attributed to the partition
that caused it. The look-ahead holds up to this many partitions'
decoded rows, so raise it for throughput and lower it for memory.

AuthSpec.description:
A connector's `auth:` field: **either** an inline auth definition `A`

connectors.title: Cloud Spanner
connectors.description: Google Cloud Spanner query source (streaming SQL, incremental replication)

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: project_id
config_fields.description: GCP project ID that owns the Spanner instance.

config_fields.name: instance
config_fields.description: Spanner instance ID.

config_fields.name: database
config_fields.description: Database name within the instance.

config_fields.name: query
config_fields.description:
GoogleSQL query to run. Use named parameters (`@name`) for
[`params`](Self::params), and the named parameter `@bookmark` to bind
the incremental cursor server-side.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description: Credentials. Defaults to Application Default Credentials.

config_fields.name: max_sessions
config_fields.description:
Upper bound on pooled Spanner sessions (server-side resources).
Channels are sized automatically at one per 100 sessions.

config_fields.name: emulator_host
config_fields.description:
Emulator endpoint override (`host:port`, e.g. `localhost:9010`).
When set, the connection is plaintext and unauthenticated — exactly
what `SPANNER_EMULATOR_HOST` does, but scoped to this connector so
parallel pipelines/tests don't race on a process-global env var.
The env var is still honored when this field is unset.

config_fields.name: params
config_fields.description:
Named bind parameters for the query. Values must be scalars (string,
integer, float, or boolean) — Spanner parameters are typed, and
null/array/object values have no unambiguous parameter type.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). `0` emits
the whole result set as a single page. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

config_fields.name: exact_staleness_secs
config_fields.description:
Read at a timestamp this many seconds in the past instead of a strong
read. Stale reads can be served by any replica, offloading the leader
— at the cost of missing rows committed within the staleness window.

config_fields.name: replication
config_fields.description: Replication mode. Defaults to [`SpannerReplication::Full`].

config_fields.name: state_key
config_fields.description:
Explicit state-store key for the bookmark. When unset, a key is
derived from the database path and a query fingerprint.

config_fields.name: shard
config_fields.description:
Optional primary-key range sharding for clustered (Mode B) execution.

When set, the source advertises itself as shardable: the cluster
coordinator splits the query's `key` range into contiguous slices that
different workers process concurrently. Has **no effect** outside the
cluster coordinator (a plain `faucet run` streams the whole query).

config_schema.description: Configuration for [`SpannerSource`](crate::SpannerSource).

project_id.description: GCP project ID that owns the Spanner instance.

auth.description: Credentials. Defaults to Application Default Credentials.

The env var is still honored when this field is unset.

GoogleSQL query to run. Use named parameters (`@name`) for
[`params`](Self::params), and the named parameter `@bookmark` to bind
the incremental cursor server-side.

params.description:
Named bind parameters for the query. Values must be scalars (string,
integer, float, or boolean) — Spanner parameters are typed, and

Read at a timestamp this many seconds in the past instead of a strong
read. Stale reads can be served by any replica, offloading the leader
— at the cost of missing rows committed within the staleness window.

Explicit state-store key for the bookmark. When unset, a key is
derived from the database path and a query fingerprint.

shard.description:
Optional primary-key range sharding for clustered (Mode B) execution.

When set, the source advertises itself as shardable: the cluster
coordinator splits the query's `key` range into contiguous slices that
different workers process concurrently. Has **no effect** outside the
cluster coordinator (a plain `faucet run` streams the whole query).

SpannerCredentials.description:
Credentials used to authenticate against Cloud Spanner.

Serialized in the project-wide adjacently-tagged shape:

```yaml
auth:
  type: service_account_key_path
  config:
    path: /secrets/sa.json
```

oneOf.description: Load a service-account key from a JSON file on disk.

path.description: Filesystem path to the service-account key JSON.

oneOf.description:
Inline service-account key JSON (prefer `${vault:…}` / `${env:…}`
interpolation over literal keys in config files).

json.description: The full service-account key JSON document.

oneOf.description:
Application Default Credentials: `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`,
`gcloud auth application-default login`, or the GCE/GKE metadata
server.

SpannerReplication.description:
How the source replicates rows across runs.

Serializes as `{ type: full }` or
`{ type: incremental, column: "...", initial_value: ... }`.

oneOf.description: Every run fetches the full result set (default).

Only rows whose `column` is strictly greater than the stored bookmark
(or `initial_value` on the first run) are emitted.

The bookmark is applied two ways: if the query contains the named
parameter `@bookmark`, it is bound so the server filters (efficient);
the source *also* filters client-side as a correctness backstop. The
new maximum of `column` is persisted on the final page.

Spanner does not implicitly coerce parameter types: a string bookmark
compared against a `TIMESTAMP` column needs an explicit cast in the
query, e.g. `WHERE updated_at > TIMESTAMP(@bookmark)`.

column.description: Column whose value is the replication cursor (e.g. `updated_at`).

initial_value.description: Lower bound used on the first run, before any bookmark is stored.

ShardConfig.description:
Primary-key range sharding settings for the Spanner source (clustered
Mode B execution).

The source is split by contiguous ranges of an **INT64-typed** column:
each shard runs ``SELECT * FROM (<query>) AS _faucet_shard WHERE `key` >=
lo AND `key` < hi``. The column must be present in the query's output.

**Nullable keys:** rows whose key is NULL are invisible to the `MIN`/`MAX`
range enumeration but are still read — exactly one shard (the last)
additionally matches ``key IS NULL``, so NULL-key rows are covered by
precisely one shard with no loss and no duplication.

key.description:
INT64 column to range-partition on. Backtick-quoted before use, so it
is safe against injection but must name a real output column.

for small lookup tables or for sinks (e.g. SQL `COPY`, BigQuery load
jobs) that prefer one large request to many small ones.

config_fields.name: shard
config_fields.description:
Optional primary-key range sharding for clustered (Mode B) execution.

When set, the source advertises itself as shardable: the cluster
coordinator splits the query's `key` range into contiguous slices that
different workers process concurrently. Has **no effect** outside the
cluster coordinator (a plain `faucet run` streams the whole query), so
it is fully backward compatible. See [`ShardConfig`].

Note: sharding a SQLite source across cluster workers requires every
worker to reach the same database file (e.g. a shared volume).

config_schema.title: SqliteSourceConfig
config_schema.description: Configuration for the SQLite query source.

max_connections.description: Maximum number of connections in the pool. Defaults to 10.

batch_size.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). Rows are
drained from the sqlx cursor and yielded whenever the buffer reaches
this size. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the cursor is fully
drained and the entire result set is emitted in a single page. Useful
for small lookup tables or for sinks (e.g. SQL `COPY`, BigQuery load
jobs) that prefer one large request to many small ones.

shard.description:
Optional primary-key range sharding for clustered (Mode B) execution.

When set, the source advertises itself as shardable: the cluster
coordinator splits the query's `key` range into contiguous slices that
different workers process concurrently. Has **no effect** outside the
cluster coordinator (a plain `faucet run` streams the whole query), so
it is fully backward compatible. See [`ShardConfig`].

Note: sharding a SQLite source across cluster workers requires every
worker to reach the same database file (e.g. a shared volume).

ShardConfig.description:
Primary-key range sharding settings for the SQLite source.

The source is split by contiguous ranges of an **integer-typed** column:
each shard runs `SELECT * FROM (<query>) WHERE "key" >= lo AND "key" < hi`.
The column must be present in the query's output and orderable as a 64-bit
integer (e.g. an `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` rowid alias).

**Nullable keys:** if the key column contains NULLs, those rows are not
visible to the `MIN`/`MAX` range enumeration. They are still read — exactly
one shard (the last) additionally matches `"key" IS NULL`, so NULL-key rows
are covered by precisely one shard with no loss and no duplication.

key.description:
Integer column to range-partition on. Quoted as an identifier before use,
so it is safe against injection but must name a real output column.

connectors.name: webhook
connectors.title: Webhook
connectors.description: Webhook HTTP receiver source

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: listen_addr
config_fields.description:
Address to bind the HTTP server to (default: `"127.0.0.1:8080"`).

**Security:** the default binds to loopback only. Binding to
`0.0.0.0` exposes the receiver to the whole network — only do so
behind a trusted gateway, and set `auth_token` to require a shared
secret on every request.

config_fields.name: path
config_fields.description: Endpoint path for receiving webhooks (default: `"/webhook"`).

config_fields.name: max_payloads
config_fields.description: Stop after receiving this many payloads.

config_fields.name: timeout_secs
config_fields.description: How long to listen before returning, in seconds (default: 30).

config_fields.name: max_body_bytes
config_fields.description:
Maximum accepted request body size in bytes (default: 1 MiB). Larger
POSTs are rejected with `413 Payload Too Large` so a single huge
request can't exhaust memory.

config_fields.name: auth_token
config_fields.description:
Optional shared secret. When set, every request must carry it in the
`Authorization` header (either the raw token or `Bearer <token>`);
requests without it are rejected with `401 Unauthorized`. When `None`
(default) the endpoint is unauthenticated.

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). The webhook
source has no native streaming primitive — it accumulates incoming POSTs
into an in-memory buffer during the receive window, then the default
[`Source::stream_pages`](faucet_core::Source::stream_pages) impl chunks
that buffer into pages of this size. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`].

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the entire flush window
is emitted in a single page. For this source it is functionally
equivalent to any positive value larger than the received payload count
— the server-side buffering behaviour does not change.

connectors.title: WebSocket
connectors.description: WebSocket streaming source

dimensions.name: Config schema
dimensions.note: config_schema() powers faucet init / validate / schema

dimensions.name: Documented
dimensions.note: one-line description in the connector catalog

config_fields.name: url
config_fields.description:
WebSocket endpoint, `ws://` or `wss://`. Supports `{placeholder}`
parent-matrix context substitution.

config_fields.name: auth
config_fields.description:
Authentication applied to the HTTP upgrade request. Either inline
(`{ type, config }`) or a `{ ref: <name> }` pointer to a shared
provider in the CLI's top-level `auth:` catalog.

config_fields.name: subscribe_messages
config_fields.description:
Subscription frames sent (in order) immediately after every
(re)connect. Empty = send nothing.

config_fields.name: message_format
config_fields.description: How to interpret each incoming frame.

config_fields.name: on_parse_error
config_fields.description: In `Json` mode, what to do when a frame is not valid JSON.

config_fields.name: envelope
config_fields.description:
`false` (default) emits the record raw; `true` wraps it as
`{ data, received_at, url }`.

config_fields.name: ping_interval
config_fields.description:
If set, send a WebSocket Ping frame on this interval (seconds) to keep
the connection alive through proxies/load balancers.

config_fields.name: max_messages
config_fields.description:
Stop after this many messages. At least one of `max_messages` /
`idle_timeout` must be set.

config_fields.name: idle_timeout
config_fields.description:
Stop after this many seconds with no message. The idle clock keeps
ticking across reconnect gaps, so it also caps a connection outage.

config_fields.name: reconnect
config_fields.description: Reconnect on transport error / non-1000 close.

config_fields.name: reconnect_backoff
config_fields.description:
Base wait (seconds) for reconnect backoff. Default 1s.

Retries grow **exponentially with jitter** from this base and are
capped, so a dead endpoint is not dialled at a fixed rate forever.
Set it to the delay you want before the *first* retry.
Also accepted as `reconnect_initial_backoff` — the gRPC source's
spelling for the same knob (#654 M20).

config_fields.name: reconnect_max_attempts
config_fields.description:
Cap on *consecutive* failed reconnects (resets on any received
message). `None` = unlimited (then `idle_timeout` is the natural cap).

Spelled `reconnect_max_attempts` on the wire, matching the gRPC
source's `reconnect_*` prefix; the historical `max_reconnect_attempts`
stays accepted as an alias (#654 M20). The prefix used to be reversed
between the two connectors, so a user who learned one spelling had the
other silently ignored and reconnected without a bound.

config_fields.name: max_message_bytes
config_fields.description:
Bound the max WebSocket message/frame size (bytes) to prevent runaway
memory. `None` = tungstenite default (64 MiB message / 16 MiB frame).

config_fields.name: batch_size
config_fields.description:
Records per emitted [`StreamPage`](faucet_core::StreamPage). Default
[`DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`]. `0` drains the entire run window into a single
page (same sentinel as the Kafka source).

AuthSpec.description:

`ref` is mutually exclusive with inline fields — supplying both is a

the request body, injects the version-appropriate headers, and (by default)
resolves [`XmlStreamConfig::records_element_path`] relative to
`Envelope.Body` and surfaces SOAP `<Fault>` responses as errors.

action.description:
The SOAP action. For 1.1 it becomes the `SOAPAction` header; for 1.2 it
is carried as the `action` parameter of the `Content-Type` header.
Optional — omit for actionless operations.

body_inner.description:
The XML fragment placed inside `<soap:Body>` — typically the operation
element, e.g. `<GetUsers xmlns="urn:example"/>`. Mutually exclusive with
the top-level [`XmlStreamConfig::body`].

namespaces.description:
Extra namespace declarations (prefix → URI) added to the envelope
element. The `soap` prefix is reserved for the envelope namespace and
any entry using it is ignored.

path_relative_to_body.description:
When `true` (default), [`XmlStreamConfig::records_element_path`] is
resolved relative to `Envelope.Body` — i.e. `Envelope.Body.` is
auto-prepended, so you write `GetUsersResponse.Users.User`. Set `false`
to supply the fully-qualified path from the document root.

fault_as_error.description:
When `true` (default), a SOAP `<Fault>` in the response raises
[`FaucetError::Source`]. When `false`,
a fault yields zero records (logged once).

SoapVersion.description:
SOAP protocol version. Controls the envelope namespace and the HTTP
header shape used to carry the SOAP action.

Deserializes from the wire strings `"1.1"` / `"1.2"`.

oneOf.description:
SOAP 1.1 — envelope namespace `http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/`,
action carried in a separate `SOAPAction` header.

SOAP 1.2 — envelope namespace `http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope`,
action carried as a `Content-Type` parameter (no `SOAPAction` header).
Page-number pagination with a query parameter.
Offset/limit pagination.

Body-cursor pagination (#544): read a continuation token from the
response via a dot-path (namespace-insensitive, trailing-match), and on
each subsequent request replace the request body with `next_body` (with
`${next_token}` substituted). Stops when the token is absent/empty or
repeats (loop guard), honouring `max_pages`. For stateful XML/SOAP APIs
that page with a `readMore`/`resultId` handle (an XML gateway's continuation).

next_token_path.description: Dot-path to the continuation-token element in the response.

next_body.description:
Request-body template for pages after the first; `${next_token}` is
substituted with the captured token.

DecodeStep.description: One step of the decode chain.

anyOf.description: Parameterless byte step (`base64` / `gunzip`).
Pull a (string) field out of a JSON body first.

extract.description: JSONPath to a string field whose value becomes the buffer.

anyOf.description: Select a member from a zip archive.
Terminal parse into records.

SimpleStep.description: A byte-chain step with no parameters (`- base64`, `- gunzip`).

oneOf.description: Base64-decode the (UTF-8 text) buffer into bytes.
Gzip-decompress the buffer.

UnzipSpec.description: Select a member of a zip archive.

member.description:
Glob (`*.csv`, `prefix*`, `*mid*`, or an exact name) selecting the member.
When omitted, the first file entry is used.

ParseSpec.description: Parse the decoded bytes into records.

records_path.description:
JSONPath selecting the record array (json/xml). When omitted, an array
body becomes the records and an object becomes a single record.

has_headers.description: Whether the first CSV row is a header (default `true`).

ParseFormat.description: Final-parse format for a decode chain.

oneOf.description: JSON (default).
Delimited text.
Excel workbook (requires the crate's `excel` feature).
XML → JSON.

TlsClientConfig.description:
Client-certificate (mutual TLS) configuration for the HTTP sources.

Supply **either** a PEM certificate + key pair (`client_cert` + `client_key`)
**or** a PKCS#12 identity file (`client_identity_pkcs12` [+ `pkcs12_password`]).
PEM values may be inline or pulled in with `${file:…}` / `${secret:…}` /
`${vault:…}`; the PKCS#12 value is a path to a `.p12`/`.pfx` file (its binary
content can't be embedded in a text config).

client_cert.description: PEM-encoded client certificate chain. Pair with `client_key`.

client_key.description: PEM-encoded PKCS#8 private key. Pair with `client_cert`.

client_identity_pkcs12.description:
Path to a PKCS#12 (`.p12`/`.pfx`) identity file — an alternative to the
PEM pair.

pkcs12_password.description: Password for the PKCS#12 file (omit or empty if the file is unencrypted).

min_version.description:
Minimum negotiated TLS version: `"1.2"` or `"1.3"`. Defaults to the
TLS backend's own minimum when unset.
